3 Document Purpose & Target

3.1 Purpose of this SRS

This Software Requirements Specification defines what the NT.QMS Quality Management System must do: its business context, functional behavior, business rules, data, integrations, reports, and measurable non-functional qualities. It deliberately does not define how the system will be implemented — detailed technical design (API contracts, database schemas, UI screen designs, infrastructure topology) is produced in subsequent design documents that must trace back to the requirements in this SRS.

3.3 Approval Objective

The objective of issuing version 1.0 is to obtain formal written approval from the client Quality Director and Project Sponsor. Upon approval, the document status changes to Approved — Baseline, and all subsequent changes are managed through change requests with impact assessment and re-approval.

3.4 Document Limitations

  • Screen mockups, sample reports, and sample data in this document are illustrative and do not constitute UI design specifications.
  • Country-specific regulatory obligations require confirmation per deployment jurisdiction (Section 26).

4 Executive Summary

4.1 Business Problem

Organizations operating under ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 17025, and related regulatory frameworks manage quality today through a mixture of paper records, spreadsheets, shared folders, and email approvals. The consequences are consistent across industries: uncontrolled document copies in circulation, approvals that stall in inboxes, CAPA actions that silently pass their due dates, training and calibration records that cannot be produced during audits, and no single view of quality performance for management. Preparation for an external audit routinely consumes weeks of manual evidence gathering.

4.2 Proposed Solution

NT.QMS is a multi-tenant, web-based quality & compliance platform for accredited laboratories that digitizes the full quality lifecycle: controlled documents and SOPs, nonconformances, CAPA, complaints and feedback, audits, training and competency, personnel authorizations, equipment and calibration, reference standards, environmental monitoring, suppliers, risk, change control, management review, and a complete analytical-quality (statistical QC) suite — bound together by configurable approval workflows, electronic signatures, role-based permissions, an immutable hash-chained compliance ledger, notifications and escalations, and cross-module traceability. Each client organization (tenant) operates in a strictly isolated data space with its own organizational structure, workflows, and compliance configuration.

4.3 Strategic Value and Benefits

DimensionExpected outcome
OperationalSingle controlled source for quality records; automated routing, reminders, and escalations replace manual follow-up; overdue work is visible the day it becomes overdue.
GovernanceEnforced approval sequences and segregation of duties; complete, immutable audit trails; evidence retrievable on demand during inspections.
ComplianceConfigurable support for ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 17025, ISO 15189, ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 11, and GxP principles per tenant.
Management visibilityRole-based dashboards and a reporting catalogue covering executive, operational, compliance, and trend perspectives.
ScalabilityMulti-tenant, multi-company, multi-site, multilingual (English, Arabic with RTL, French) operation on one platform.
Note: This SRS makes no quantified financial or performance-improvement claims; measurable business objectives and their measurement approach are defined in Section 6.

4.4 Main User Groups and Core Modules

Primary users are laboratory quality managers and directors, document controllers, analysts and technicians, method-validation leads, calibration/equipment, training and PT coordinators, auditors, and platform/tenant administrators — personas are specified in Section 13. The application is organized into nine sidebar navigation groups plus a separate Platform portal (the full page catalogue is in Section 11A): Overview, Quality & Improvement (nonconformance & CAPA, complaints, feedback, audits, quality objectives, change control, management review), Documents & Records, Risk & Governance (risk, impartiality/COI, organizational context), Resources (equipment, reference standards, environmental monitoring, suppliers), People & Competence (competency, authorizations, training), Analytical Quality — a full statistical-QC suite (QC/Westgard, method validation and comparison, precision, linearity, detection limits, reference intervals, sigma metrics, uncertainty, proficiency testing and more) — and Administration. The core quality modules are specified in detail in Sections 11.1–11.13; every module's page-level behaviour, including the analytical-quality suite, is catalogued in Section 11A.

4.5 Scope Boundaries, Dependencies, and Major Risks

  • Scope: Release 1 covers the core platform and essential QMS functions; the full boundary, exclusions, and phasing are defined in Section 7 and Section 27.
  • Key dependencies: client identity provider for SSO, HR system for employee data, e-signature policy decisions, hosting/data-residency confirmation, and migration source-data quality (Section 26).
  • Major risks: regulatory-interpretation differences, migration data quality, user adoption, and permission-model complexity — with mitigations in Section 25.

5 Business Context

5.1 Typical Organization Structure

NT.QMS serves accredited testing, calibration and medical laboratories operating under ISO/IEC 17025 and ISO 15189 (with ISO 9001 and 21 CFR Part 11 support), from a single laboratory to multi-site laboratory groups. A typical tenant is a laboratory organization structured as a headquarters/main laboratory with branches, departments and sections (e.g. chemistry, hematology, microbiology, calibration), and operational sites. A central quality unit owns the quality policy, manual and procedures, while section quality teams execute local processes. Supporting functions — HR, metrology, IT, procurement — both feed and consume quality records (competency and training data, equipment calibration, reference standards, supplier performance).

Quality governance may be centralized (corporate quality approves all controlled documents and CAPAs), decentralized (each site manages its own records under a corporate policy umbrella), or hybrid. NT.QMS must support all three through organizational scoping of records, workflows, and permissions. The quality policy hierarchy runs: quality policy → quality manual → corporate procedures → site procedures / SOPs → work instructions → forms and records. Multiple legal companies can operate under one tenant, and multiple tenants coexist on one platform with strict isolation.

7 Scope

7.1 In Scope (Release 1 baseline unless marked otherwise)

  • Multi-tenant platform with tenant provisioning, entitlements, and platform administration (PLT).
  • Tenant and organization administration: companies, regions, branches, departments, laboratories, sites; workflow, numbering, calendar, and notification configuration (TEN).
  • Identity & access management: local authentication, SSO (OIDC/SAML), MFA, RBAC with organizational scoping, delegation, segregation of duties (IAM).
  • Document & SOP control with versioning, approval routes, electronic approval, publication, acknowledgement, and periodic review (DOC).
  • Nonconformance and CAPA management with root-cause analysis, action tracking, and effectiveness verification (NCR, CAPA).
  • Complaint, audit, training & competency, equipment & calibration, risk, and management review modules (CMP–MRV) — phased per Section 27.
  • Role-based dashboards, reporting catalogue, global search, and cross-module traceability.
  • Immutable audit trails; configurable 21 CFR Part 11 electronic-signature mode (Section 19).
  • Notifications (in-app, email) with reminders and escalations; SMS via gateway where contracted.
  • Localization: English (base), Arabic (RTL), French; localized dates and numbers.
  • Integrations per the catalogue in Section 14 (identity, HR, email/SMS, file storage, malware scanning; others phased).
  • Data migration of master data and open/historical quality records per Section 22.

7.2 Out of Scope

Out of scope: the following are excluded from the product scope of this SRS.
  • Laboratory test execution and result management (LIMS functionality) — NT.QMS links to LIMS records, it does not replace them.
  • Full ERP functions: procurement, inventory, invoicing, finance.
  • HR administration (payroll, leave, recruitment) — employee master data is consumed via integration.
  • Authoring platform for e-learning content (SCORM authoring); LMS integration is supported instead.
  • Hard-copy printing/stamping logistics of controlled paper distribution (system tracks controlled copies; physical handling is procedural).
  • Translation of tenant-authored content between languages (UI localization only).
  • Legal advice on jurisdiction-specific retention or e-signature acceptance.

7.3 Optional Future Scope

Optional future scope: candidate capabilities, not part of the approved Release 1 baseline.
  • Supplier quality management as a full module (supplier audits, scorecards, SCAR portal) — Release 3 candidate.
  • Native mobile applications with offline data capture; current baseline is responsive web.
  • WhatsApp/approved-messaging notifications; SCIM automated identity provisioning.
  • AI-assisted classification, root-cause suggestions, and trend anomaly detection.
  • Customer/self-service complaint portal for external parties; external auditor portal beyond read-only access.
  • OCR full-text indexing of scanned attachments.

7.4 Assumptions

  • SCP-ASM-01 Clients provide an identity provider for SSO or accept local authentication with MFA.
  • SCP-ASM-02 Employee master data can be sourced from the client HR system or maintained manually in NT.QMS.
  • SCP-ASM-03 Tenants operating under 21 CFR Part 11 will formally define which record types require Part 11 signatures.
  • SCP-ASM-04 Legacy data for migration is extractable in structured electronic form (see Section 22).

The full assumption and open-question register is maintained in Section 26.

7.5 Dependencies

  • Client identity provider availability and configuration for SSO integrations.
  • Client SMTP/SMS gateway accounts or approval to use platform-provided services.
  • Hosting environment and data-residency decision (cloud region or on-premises) per tenant.
  • E-signature policy decision per tenant (standard electronic approval vs. Part 11 mode).
  • Availability of source-system extracts and client subject-matter experts for migration mapping.

7.6 Constraints

  • The approved technical baseline in Section 10 (modular monolith, .NET, Angular, PostgreSQL with RLS) is a binding solution constraint.
  • English is the base language; all UI text must be externalized for localization from the first release.
  • Tenant context must derive only from trusted authentication claims or validated routing — never from request bodies.
  • The system must operate within the compliance vocabulary of ISO 9001:2015 as the common denominator; stricter regimes are layered as configurable profiles.

9 Enterprise Quality Workflow

9.1 End-to-End Quality Lifecycle — Narrative

NT.QMS implements one continuous improvement cycle across the organization. The lifecycle begins with governance: the quality unit defines quality policies and procedures (1) and creates them as controlled documents and forms (2) in the Document Control module. Content passes through review and approval (3) with enforced routes and, where configured, electronic signatures, and approved versions are published (4) as the single effective source. Publication automatically assigns required training (5), and employees confirm reading, understanding, and competency (6) through acknowledgements and assessments.

With competent people and current procedures, the organization executes operational activities (7) while the system monitors quality indicators (8). When monitoring, audits, customers, or daily work identify deviations, incidents, complaints, risks, or nonconformities (9), the responsible person records and classifies the issue (10). Containment (11) protects the customer and operations immediately; investigation and root-cause analysis (12) follow for significant issues. The team then defines corrective and preventive actions (13), assigns owners and due dates (14), and the system monitors implementation (15) with reminders and escalations. After implementation, an independent verifier verifies effectiveness (16) against predefined criteria, and the record is closed (17). Closure feeds back into the system of work: related documents, risks, training, and controls are updated (18). Periodically, audits and management reviews (19) evaluate the whole system and generate decisions and action items, and the improvement cycle continues (20).

9.3 Cross-Cutting Exceptions and Escalations

  • Approver absence: time-bound delegation or acting assignment applies (IAM); if none exists, escalation to the role's manager after a configurable waiting period.
  • Overdue activity: reminder → owner's manager → quality manager → quality director, at configurable intervals; every escalation is audited.
  • Rejected approval: record returns to its author with mandatory rejection reason; rework re-enters the same route from the configured step.
  • Ineffective CAPA: closure is blocked; a successor CAPA or escalation to management review is mandatory.
  • Regulatory-reportable event: complaint/NCR classification can trigger a compliance notification path (configurable per tenant).

10 Solution Architecture & Technical Baseline

The following technical baseline is an approved, binding solution constraint for NT.QMS. It bounds all design decisions; deviations require formal change control. Requirements in this section carry IDs GEN-TC-### (technical constraints).

10.1 Architecture Constraints

IDConstraint
GEN-TC-001The initial implementation shall be a modular monolith structured by Clean Architecture and Domain-Driven Design, with clear bounded contexts per module group, enabling later extraction of services without redesign.
GEN-TC-002Command/query handling shall follow CQRS using MediatR-based handlers; input validation shall use FluentValidation or an equivalent declarative framework executed before handlers.
GEN-TC-003All state-changing operations shall run in explicit transactions with idempotency controls (client-supplied idempotency keys on externally triggered commands) and optimistic concurrency (row version tokens; conflicting updates rejected with a recoverable error).
GEN-TC-004Cross-module and external messaging shall use the Outbox/Inbox patterns so that domain events, notifications, and integration messages are delivered at-least-once with deduplication, and never lost on failure.
GEN-TC-005Audit logging shall be immutable and append-only; no API or administrative function may modify or delete audit events (see Section 18.6).
GEN-TC-006Background jobs (schedules, reminders, escalations, report generation) shall run under tenant-scoped identities, be observable, retry-safe, and never bypass authorization or RLS.
GEN-TC-007The platform shall be API-first: every UI capability is served by documented, versioned APIs usable for integration.

10.2 Backend Constraints

IDConstraint
GEN-TC-008The backend shall be implemented on .NET with three separate logical API surfaces: (a) platform administration, (b) tenant administration, (c) tenant operational functions — separately routable and separately authorizable.
GEN-TC-009Authorization shall be enforced in the backend for every operation, deny-by-default; the frontend may hide controls but is never the enforcement point.
GEN-TC-010Tenant context shall be derived only from trusted authentication claims or validated routing. Tenant identifiers received in an untrusted request body shall never be used to resolve tenant context; any mismatch is rejected and security-logged.

10.3 Frontend Constraints

IDConstraint
GEN-TC-011The frontend shall be an Angular monorepo with two independent applications: (1) Platform Administration Portal, (2) Client/Tenant QMS Portal.
GEN-TC-012Shared libraries are limited to: design system, localization utilities, authentication utilities, and generated API contracts.
GEN-TC-013The two applications shall NOT share business state, tenant-sensitive caches, permission decisions, or tenant-specific workflow orchestration.

10.4 Database Constraints

IDConstraint
GEN-TC-014The database shall be PostgreSQL accessed via Entity Framework Core, with schema-per-module ownership where appropriate; no module writes to another module's schema directly.
GEN-TC-015Every tenant-owned record shall carry the tenant identifier, and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security shall enforce tenant isolation at the database layer in addition to application-level filters.
GEN-TC-016Queries, background jobs, caches, and real-time communication groups shall all be tenant-aware/tenant-partitioned; cross-tenant denial tests are a mandatory part of every release's test suite (Section 23).

Sections 11.1–11.13 currently provide deep specifications for the core QMS modules; deep chapters for the analytical-quality suite and the remaining laboratory-specific modules (impartiality/COI, organizational context, reference standards, environmental monitoring, suppliers, authorizations, compliance ledger) are page-specified in §11A and are scheduled to receive full 19-part chapters in a subsequent revision.

11.1 Platform Administration PLT

11.1.1 Module Overview
Module namePlatform Administration
Module codePLT
PurposeProvide the platform-operator control plane of the NT.QMS multi-tenant SaaS: tenant provisioning and onboarding, tenant lifecycle management (Trial, Active, Suspended, Terminated), subscription plans and module entitlements, platform-level configuration, platform health monitoring, platform-operator user management, announcement broadcasts, tenant data export on termination, and a platform-level audit trail.
Business valueEnables National Technology to onboard client organizations rapidly and safely, enforce commercial entitlements, keep every tenant strictly isolated, and demonstrate to clients and inspectors that platform operators can never read tenant quality records.
In scopeTenant CRUD and lifecycle, subscription plan catalogue, per-tenant module entitlements and seat limits, activation invitations, tenant suspension/termination with data export, platform configuration and feature flags, platform-operator accounts, tenant usage/health metadata dashboards, maintenance announcements, immutable platform audit.
Out of scopeBilling/invoicing engine (external system — see Section 14), tenant-internal user management (see 11.3 IAM), tenant organization structure (see 11.2 TEN), any read or write access to tenant quality-record content.
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §7.5 (documented information integrity), 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(d)/(g) (system access limited to authorized individuals), GxP data-integrity (ALCOA+) principles applied to platform operations.
Related modulesTEN, IAM, NFRs, E-Signatures, Data Retention
Primary personasP-01 Platform Administrator, P-32 System Support User, P-31 Integration Service Account; P-02 Tenant Administrator as the external invitation recipient.

11.1.2 Business Problem

NT.QMS serves multiple client organizations from one deployment. Without a governed operator plane, tenant creation becomes a manual database exercise: isolation policies may be applied inconsistently, commercial entitlements drift from contracts, suspended clients retain access, and terminated clients cannot receive their data in a defensible, complete package. Each of these failures is simultaneously a commercial risk and a compliance risk, because clients in regulated industries must prove to auditors that their quality records are isolated and that the SaaS operator cannot alter them.

The Platform Administration module makes every operator action a first-class, validated, audited transaction. Provisioning is automated and verified; lifecycle transitions follow enforced rules (including a two-person rule for termination); entitlement changes propagate without data loss; and the platform operator is technically prevented — not merely instructed — from reading tenant quality-record content.

11.1.3 Business Objectives
  • BUS-OBJ-015 — Tenant data protection: hard isolation at provisioning time (row-level security, tenant-scoped storage) and operator-access denial by design.
  • BUS-OBJ-008 — Immutable audit trails: every platform-operator action is recorded in an append-only platform audit log.
  • BUS-OBJ-016 — Configurable workflows: plans and module entitlements switch capabilities per tenant without code changes.
  • BUS-OBJ-014 — Multilingual/multi-site support: tenant default language, time zone, and data-residency region are set at provisioning.
  • BUS-OBJ-013 — Management reporting: platform usage and adoption reporting based exclusively on metadata and counters, never record content.

11.1.5 Preconditions
  • The platform environment is deployed and healthy (database, storage, email gateway operational).
  • The acting Platform Administrator is authenticated with mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA).
  • The subscription plan catalogue (plans, module bundles, seat tiers) is defined and active.
  • A signed subscription agreement or an approved trial request exists and is referenced by its commercial reference number.
  • The designated Tenant Administrator's name and business email address are known.

11.1.6 Trigger Events
  • New subscription agreement signed (paid tenant) or trial request approved (trial tenant).
  • Plan upgrade/downgrade or module entitlement change requested by the commercial team.
  • Non-payment, contractual breach, or security incident requiring suspension.
  • Contract expiry or client termination notice requiring offboarding and data export.
  • Scheduled maintenance requiring a broadcast announcement to tenants.
  • Trial end date reached (system-generated trigger).

11.1.11 Functional Requirements
PLT-FR-001 Automated, verified tenant provisioning with hard isolation MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provision a new tenant as an automated, step-verified job that creates the tenant identifier, applies PostgreSQL row-level-security policies to all tenant-owned tables, creates default tenant roles, creates a tenant-scoped file-storage container, and seeds default reference data. Activation shall be blocked until an automated isolation self-test (cross-tenant query returns zero rows; storage ACL denies foreign tenant) passes.
Rationale
Isolation applied at provisioning time, verified by test, is the foundation of BUS-OBJ-015.
Actor
P-01 Platform Administrator; System
Preconditions / Trigger
Draft tenant record complete; "Provision" action invoked.
Validation & Exceptions
Any failed step triggers compensating rollback of all completed steps and returns the record to Draft with a failure report.
Audit
ProvisioningStarted, ProvisioningStepCompleted per step, ProvisioningVerified or ProvisioningFailed with error detail.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-01
Related
PLT-BR-001, Section 18
PLT-FR-002 Subscription plan and module entitlement assignment MustCore
Requirement
The system shall maintain a subscription plan catalogue (plan name, allowed modules, seat tiers, feature limits) and shall allow the Platform Administrator to assign exactly one plan per tenant plus an entitlement set that is a subset of that plan's allowed modules. Entitlement enforcement shall take effect within 5 minutes of the change without tenant restart.
Rationale
Aligns delivered capabilities with the commercial contract (BUS-OBJ-016).
Actor
P-01
Preconditions / Trigger
Active plan catalogue; tenant in any non-terminated state.
Validation & Exceptions
Entitlements outside the plan are rejected with a per-module explanation; seat limit below current active users is rejected.
Audit
EntitlementsAssigned / EntitlementsChanged with before/after values.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-05
Related
PLT-FR-012, PLT-BR-003
PLT-FR-003 Trial lifecycle with automatic expiry handling MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support trial tenants with a mandatory trial end date. It shall notify the Tenant Administrator and Platform Administrator 7 days and 1 day before expiry, and shall automatically transition the tenant to Suspended at 00:00 tenant local time on the day after the trial end date, preserving all data.
Rationale
Controlled trials support sales without risking uncontrolled free usage or data loss on conversion.
Actor
System; P-01
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant in Trial status; scheduler evaluates daily.
Validation & Exceptions
Conversion to Active before expiry cancels pending expiry actions; extension requires a new documented commercial reference.
Audit
TrialExpiryWarning, TrialExpired (automatic suspension), TrialConverted.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-07
Related
PLT-BR-004
PLT-FR-004 Tenant suspension without data loss MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow a Platform Administrator to suspend a tenant with a mandatory documented reason. Suspension shall immediately (within 60 seconds) terminate active tenant sessions, block all tenant logins and API access with a configurable suspension message, stop scheduled tenant jobs, and preserve all tenant data unchanged. Reinstatement shall restore access without any data migration.
Rationale
Commercial and security enforcement must never destroy client quality records.
Actor
P-01
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant Active or Trial; non-payment, breach, or security trigger.
Validation & Exceptions
Suspension without a reason is rejected; in-flight tenant transactions complete or roll back atomically.
Audit
TenantSuspended (actor, reason, timestamp), TenantReinstated.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-03
Related
PLT-BR-004
PLT-FR-005 Tenant termination with complete data export MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall support tenant termination only after confirmation by a second, distinct Platform Administrator account. On termination the system shall generate a complete export package of the tenant's data: all records in machine-readable form (JSON/CSV), all file attachments in original format, the full tenant audit trail, and a signed manifest with checksums. The package shall be delivered through a secure, expiring download link issued to the verified tenant contact; the download event shall be logged.
Rationale
Regulated clients must retain their quality records after leaving the platform; the operator must be able to prove complete hand-over.
Actor
P-01 (initiator) + P-01 (confirmer); System
Preconditions / Trigger
Termination notice recorded; tenant Active or Suspended.
Validation & Exceptions
Initiator and confirmer must be different accounts (SoD); export failure blocks the Archived transition and alerts P-01.
Audit
TerminationInitiated, TerminationConfirmed, ExportGenerated (manifest hash), ExportDownloaded, TenantArchived.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-04, AC-PLT-06
Related
PLT-BR-002, PLT-BR-005, Section 21
PLT-FR-006 Platform operators cannot read tenant quality-record content MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall technically prevent all platform-operator roles (including Platform Administrator and System Support User) from reading, creating, editing, or deleting the content of tenant quality records (documents, NCRs, CAPAs, complaints, audits, training, equipment, risk, and management-review records) and tenant file attachments. Platform roles shall see only tenant metadata and aggregate usage counters (record counts, storage volume, active users, module usage). Any attempt to access tenant record content from a platform context shall be denied and written to the security log.
Rationale
Core trust and compliance commitment (BUS-OBJ-015); required for client audits and 21 CFR Part 11 access-limitation expectations.
Actor
All platform roles (as denied subjects); System (enforcer)
Preconditions / Trigger
Any platform-context request targeting tenant record content.
Validation & Exceptions
No override or "support access" bypass exists in scope. Out of Scope A consent-based, tenant-approved support-access mechanism is out of scope for v1.0.
Audit
CrossBoundaryAccessDenied security event: actor, endpoint, target tenant, timestamp.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-02
Related
PLT-BR-006, Section 18
PLT-FR-007 Platform configuration and feature-flag management MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall provide a platform configuration registry (global defaults for password policy baseline, session timeout baseline, supported languages and regions, email gateway settings, feature flags) with typed values, validation rules per key, an effective/previous value history, and per-tenant override visibility (which tenants deviate from the default and why).
Rationale
Central, audited configuration prevents environment drift and undocumented changes.
Actor
P-01
Preconditions / Trigger
Authenticated platform session; configuration change request.
Validation & Exceptions
Type/range validation per key; changes that weaken a security baseline below the platform minimum are rejected.
Audit
PlatformConfigChanged with key, before/after value, actor, reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-05
Related
PLT-BR-008
PLT-FR-008 Platform monitoring and tenant health dashboard MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide a platform dashboard showing, per tenant and in aggregate: status, active user count vs. seat limit, storage consumption vs. quota, API error rate, background-job backlog, and last-activity timestamp — computed exclusively from metadata and counters. Threshold breaches (storage ≥ 90% of quota, job backlog > 30 minutes) shall raise alerts to platform operators.
Rationale
Proactive operations without inspecting tenant content (BUS-OBJ-013).
Actor
P-01, P-32 (read-only)
Preconditions / Trigger
Metering pipeline active; dashboard opened or scheduled evaluation.
Validation & Exceptions
Metric collection failure is itself surfaced as a health alert; stale metrics are flagged with data age.
Audit
AlertRaised, AlertAcknowledged (who/when).
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-02
Related
RPT-PLT-02
PLT-FR-009 Platform-operator user management with mandatory MFA MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall manage platform-operator accounts separately from tenant users: creation, role assignment (Platform Administrator, System Support User), deactivation, and periodic access review lists. MFA shall be mandatory and non-disableable for all platform accounts; platform sessions shall time out after 15 minutes of inactivity (proposed target — pending business confirmation).
Rationale
Operator accounts are the highest-privilege attack surface of the platform.
Actor
P-01
Preconditions / Trigger
Operator joiner/mover/leaver events.
Validation & Exceptions
The last active Platform Administrator account cannot be deactivated; self-deactivation is blocked.
Audit
PlatformUserCreated/RoleChanged/Deactivated; all platform logins and failures.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-06
Related
11.3 IAM, PLT-BR-007
PLT-FR-010 Announcement broadcasts to tenants ShouldCore
Requirement
The system shall let a Platform Administrator publish announcements (planned maintenance, new releases, incidents) with title, body, severity, display window, and target audience (all tenants or a selected subset). Announcements shall appear as in-app banners to tenant users during the display window and optionally as email to Tenant Administrators. Announcements shall support English, Arabic, and French variants.
Rationale
Predictable operator-to-tenant communication for maintenance and incidents.
Actor
P-01
Preconditions / Trigger
Maintenance schedule or incident declared.
Validation & Exceptions
Announcement content must not include any tenant-specific data (PLT-BR-009); display window end must be after start.
Audit
AnnouncementPublished/Updated/Withdrawn with audience and window.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-05
Related
RPT-PLT-07
PLT-FR-011 Immutable platform audit trail MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall record every platform-operator action (tenant lifecycle changes, entitlement changes, configuration changes, operator user management, announcement actions, export generation and download, denied access attempts) in an append-only platform audit log capturing actor, action, target, UTC timestamp, before/after values, reason where mandated, and origin IP. Audit entries shall be tamper-evident (hash-chained) and shall not be editable or deletable by any role, including Platform Administrators.
Rationale
BUS-OBJ-008; operator accountability is a contractual commitment to tenants.
Actor
System (recorder); P-01, P-32 (viewers)
Preconditions / Trigger
Any auditable platform action.
Validation & Exceptions
Audit-write failure causes the business action to fail (no unaudited platform action).
Audit
Self-referential: audit-log queries and exports are themselves audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-06
Related
11.1.19, Section 18
PLT-FR-012 Entitlement change propagation without data loss MustCore
Requirement
When a module entitlement is disabled for a tenant, the system shall hide the module's UI and block its APIs for tenant users while preserving all module data, cross-module references, and audit history intact. Re-enabling the module shall restore full access to the preserved data with no migration step. Disabling a module shall present the Platform Administrator with an impact summary (record counts, open records) before confirmation.
Rationale
Downgrades are commercial events; they must never destroy quality records.
Actor
P-01; System
Preconditions / Trigger
Entitlement change saved (PLT-FR-002).
Validation & Exceptions
Confirmation required when the module contains open (non-closed) records; cross-module links render as read-only stubs while the module is disabled.
Audit
ModuleDisabled/ModuleEnabled with impact-summary snapshot.
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-05
Related
PLT-BR-003
PLT-FR-013 Activation invitation lifecycle (expiry, resend, revoke) MustCore
Requirement
The system shall issue single-use activation invitation tokens valid for 14 calendar days. It shall allow the Platform Administrator to resend (invalidating the prior token) or revoke an invitation, shall automatically expire unused tokens, and shall escalate to the Platform Administrator when an invitation expires unused.
Rationale
Stale activation links are a credential-theft vector and an onboarding stall signal.
Actor
System; P-01
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant in Invited status.
Validation & Exceptions
Use of an expired, revoked, or already-used token is rejected with a neutral message and security-logged.
Audit
InvitationSent/Resent/Revoked/Expired/Accepted with token identifier (not value).
Acceptance criteria
AC-PLT-01
Related
PLT-BR-010

11.1.16 Integration Requirements
  • Inbound — commercial/billing system: subscription events (new contract, plan change, non-payment, termination notice) arrive via the integration API as proposals for Platform Administrator action; they never change tenant state directly. See Section 14.
  • Outbound — usage metering: daily per-tenant usage counters (active users, storage, module usage) published to the commercial system; metadata only.
  • Outbound — email gateway (SMTP): invitations, lifecycle notices, alerts; delivery status captured per 11.1.14.
  • Outbound — monitoring/observability: platform health metrics and alert events exported to the operations monitoring stack.
  • Outbound — secure export delivery: termination export packages delivered via expiring signed URLs; download events logged.
Note: Integration endpoint contracts, authentication, and error-handling standards are specified centrally in Section 14; PLT consumes the platform integration identifiers defined there.

11.1.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-PLT-01 — Provisioning creates a verified, isolated tenant

  • Given a complete Draft tenant record with an assigned plan,
  • When the Platform Administrator invokes "Provision",
  • Then the system creates the tenant with RLS policies, default roles, and storage, passes the isolation self-test, moves the tenant to Invited, and sends a single-use 14-day activation invitation — and if any step fails, all completed steps are rolled back and the record returns to Draft with a failure report.

AC-PLT-02 — Platform operator cannot read tenant record content

  • Given an authenticated Platform Administrator session,
  • When the administrator attempts to open any tenant quality record or attachment via UI navigation or direct API call,
  • Then the request is denied, no record content or attachment bytes are returned, a CrossBoundaryAccessDenied security event is logged, and only metadata/usage counters remain visible.

AC-PLT-03 — Suspension blocks access and preserves data

  • Given an Active tenant with logged-in users,
  • When a Platform Administrator suspends the tenant with a documented reason,
  • Then within 60 seconds all tenant sessions are terminated, new logins and API calls are rejected with the suspension message, scheduled tenant jobs stop, and after reinstatement all data and configuration are byte-identical to the pre-suspension state.

AC-PLT-04 — Termination produces a complete verifiable export

  • Given a tenant terminated with two-person confirmation,
  • When the export package is generated,
  • Then the package contains all tenant records in JSON/CSV, all attachments, the full tenant audit trail, and a signed manifest whose checksums validate against the package contents, and the download by the verified contact is logged.

AC-PLT-05 — Module disablement hides but preserves data

  • Given a tenant with 250 CAPA records and an entitlement change disabling the CAPA module,
  • When the change takes effect,
  • Then tenant users can no longer open CAPA UI or APIs, cross-module references render as read-only stubs, and after re-enabling the module all 250 records and their audit history are fully accessible with no data change.

AC-PLT-06 — Two-person termination and audit immutability

  • Given a termination initiated by Platform Administrator A,
  • When the same account A attempts to confirm the termination,
  • Then the confirmation is rejected with an SoD violation message, the attempt is written to the platform audit log, and no role — including Platform Administrator — can edit or delete that audit entry.

AC-PLT-07 — Trial expiry suspends automatically

  • Given a Trial tenant whose trial end date is yesterday,
  • When the daily lifecycle scheduler runs,
  • Then the tenant transitions to Suspended automatically, all data is preserved, the expiry notifications sent at T−7 and T−1 days are traceable in the notification log, and the transition is audited as TrialExpired.

11.2 Tenant & Organization Administration TEN

11.2.1 Module Overview
Module nameTenant & Organization Administration
Module codeTEN
PurposeGive each tenant self-service, audited control over its own operating environment: organization structure (companies, regions, branches, departments, laboratories, sites), numbering schemes, working calendars and holidays, tenant-level settings (languages including Arabic RTL, date/time formats, e-signature policy enablement per 21 CFR Part 11), workflow configuration (approval routes and escalation rules), notification templates, lookup/reference data, and tenant branding.
Business valueLets multi-site, multilingual organizations model their real structure and rules without vendor involvement, so that ownership, routing, numbering, and due-date behavior across all quality modules reflect the organization as it actually operates.
In scopeOrganizational-unit hierarchy with effective-dated, approval-controlled changes; numbering scheme definition per record type; working calendars/holidays; tenant locale and language settings; e-signature policy enablement per module; approval-route and escalation-rule configuration; notification template management (multilingual); lookup/reference data with versioning; branding (logo, colors, report header/footer).
Out of scopeUser accounts, roles, and permission assignment (11.3 IAM); plan/entitlement management (11.1 PLT); content of quality records governed by the functional modules; translation of user-entered content.
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §4.3/§4.4 (scope and processes of the QMS), §5.3 (organizational roles), §7.5 (documented information); ISO/IEC 17025:2017 §5 (structural requirements for laboratories); 21 CFR Part 11 (where the e-signature policy is enabled).
Related modulesPLT, IAM, DOC, NCR, CAPA, E-Signatures; all modules consume TEN configuration.
Primary personasP-02 Tenant Administrator, P-03 Organization Administrator, P-05 Quality Manager (approver of structural changes), P-04 Quality Director (approver of e-signature policy changes).

11.2.2 Business Problem

Client organizations are rarely flat: a holding company may operate regions, branches, laboratories, and departments, each with its own managers, calendars, and record-numbering conventions. When a QMS cannot model this structure, users compensate with naming conventions and spreadsheets — ownership becomes ambiguous, approval routing breaks on reorganizations, and record numbers stop being trustworthy identifiers.

Organization structure is itself quality-critical configuration: moving a department or deactivating a laboratory changes who owns open NCRs, where documents apply, and how KPIs aggregate. Such changes must therefore be validated for impact, approved before they take effect, applied on a declared effective date, and fully audited. The TEN module provides this governed configuration layer, together with the tenant-level settings (languages including Arabic RTL, calendars, numbering, workflow routes, templates, lookups, branding) that every other module consumes.

11.2.3 Business Objectives
  • BUS-OBJ-001 — Standardize processes: shared approval routes, numbering schemes, and calendars across all sites.
  • BUS-OBJ-004 — Enforce approvals/SoD: structural and policy changes require an approver distinct from the requester.
  • BUS-OBJ-014 — Multilingual/multi-site: full organizational hierarchy with per-unit calendars; English, Arabic (RTL), and French UI settings.
  • BUS-OBJ-016 — Configurable workflows: approval routes, escalation rules, and notification templates maintained by the tenant without code changes.
  • BUS-OBJ-005 — Traceability: every configuration value is versioned and its change history retained.
  • BUS-OBJ-008 — Immutable audit trails: all configuration changes captured with before/after values.

11.2.4 Actors & Personas
RolePersonaResponsibility in this module

Primary actorP-02 Tenant AdministratorOwns tenant-level settings (languages, locale, branding, e-signature policy request), approves structural changes, manages configuration scopes.

11.2.5 Preconditions
  • The tenant is Active (or Trial) and the initial setup wizard has been completed (11.1).
  • The acting user holds the Tenant Administrator or Organization Administrator role for the affected scope (11.3 IAM).
  • At least one root organizational unit (company) exists.
  • An approver distinct from the requester is available for approval-controlled changes.

11.2.6 Trigger Events
  • Corporate reorganization: new branch, laboratory, or department; merge, move, rename, or closure of a unit.
  • New site or laboratory brought into QMS scope.
  • Annual holiday calendar publication or ad-hoc holiday declaration.
  • Decision to enable 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures for one or more modules.
  • Process-owner request to change an approval route, escalation rule, or notification template.
  • New or amended lookup values (e.g. defect categories, complaint sources) required by a functional module.
  • Corporate rebranding requiring logo/report header updates.

11.2.11 Functional Requirements
TEN-FR-001 Organizational hierarchy management MustCore
Requirement
The system shall maintain a tenant-scoped organizational hierarchy of typed units (Company, Region, Branch, Department, Laboratory, Site) with configurable placement rules per type, multilingual names (English base; Arabic and French optional), unit managers, and per-unit working calendars. The hierarchy shall be versioned: every applied change produces a new hierarchy version with an effective date, and prior versions remain queryable for historical reporting.
Rationale
Every module scopes ownership, routing, and reporting by organizational unit (BUS-OBJ-014).
Actor
P-03, P-02
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant active; root company unit exists.
Validation & Exceptions
Cycles rejected; sibling-name and unit-code uniqueness enforced; deactivated parents cannot receive children.
Audit
All unit create/move/rename/deactivate events with before/after values and hierarchy version.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TEN-01
Related
TEN-FR-002, TEN-BR-001
TEN-FR-002 Approval-controlled, effective-dated structure changes MustCore
Requirement
The system shall require all organization-structure changes to be made as change sets that pass automated impact analysis (affected open records, users, routes, numbering scopes), carry a reassignment plan when units are deactivated or moved, and are approved by a user distinct from the requester before being applied atomically on their effective date, per the workflow in 11.2.7.
Rationale
Reorganizations silently break ownership and routing unless impact is analyzed and changes are approved (BUS-OBJ-004).
Actor
P-03 (requester); P-05/P-02 (approver); System (applier)
Preconditions / Trigger
Draft change set submitted.
Validation & Exceptions
Submission blocked while any open record or active user of a deactivated unit is unmapped; failed apply rolls back completely and alerts the Tenant Administrator.
Audit
Full change-set trail: drafted, submitted, reviewed, approved/rejected/returned, applied, closed.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TEN-01, AC-TEN-02
Related
TEN-BR-002, TEN-BR-003
TEN-FR-003 Numbering scheme configuration per record type MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall let the Tenant Administrator define one numbering scheme per record type (document, NCR, CAPA, complaint, audit, risk, equipment, training) using a pattern of tokens: fixed text, record-type code, organizational-unit code, year (YY/YYYY), month, and a zero-padded sequence with configurable width and reset policy (never / yearly / per unit-year). Generated numbers shall be unique per tenant and record type, assigned atomically at record creation, and never reissued — including for deleted or cancelled records.
Rationale
Trustworthy record identifiers are a prerequisite for traceability (BUS-OBJ-005) and inspection readiness.
Actor
P-02; consuming modules (generation)
Preconditions / Trigger
Record type exists; scheme changes apply to future numbers only.
Validation & Exceptions
Pattern preview with sample output before save; scheme change never renumbers existing records; sequence gaps caused by rolled-back transactions are permitted and documented.
Audit
SchemeCreated/Changed with before/after pattern; every generated number traceable to its scheme version.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TEN-03
Related
TEN-BR-004
TEN-FR-004 Working calendars and holidays MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall support multiple named working calendars per tenant, each defining weekly working days (e.g. Sunday–Thursday), daily working hours, and dated holidays. Each organizational unit references exactly one calendar (inherited from its parent by default). All due-date and SLA computations in consuming modules shall use the calendar of the record's owning unit; calendar changes shall affect only due dates computed after the change.
Rationale
Multi-country operation (e.g. Friday/Saturday vs. Saturday/Sunday weekends) makes a single hard-coded calendar produce wrong due dates (BUS-OBJ-006).
Actor
P-03, P-02
Preconditions / Trigger
Annual holiday publication or ad-hoc declaration.
Validation & Exceptions
At least one working day per week; holiday dates unique per calendar; a calendar referenced by units cannot be deleted, only superseded.
Audit
CalendarCreated/Changed with before/after entries.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TEN-04
Related
TEN-BR-005
TEN-FR-005 Tenant language settings including Arabic RTL MustCore
Requirement
The system shall let the Tenant Administrator enable any subset of the supported UI languages (English, Arabic, French) and set the tenant default. When Arabic is active for a user, the entire UI shall render right-to-left (layout mirroring, text alignment, navigation) while embedded left-to-right values (codes, numbers, email addresses) remain readable. Users may override the tenant default with a personal language preference from the enabled subset.
Rationale
BUS-OBJ-014; Arabic-first client organizations are a primary market.
Actor
P-02 (settings); all users (preference)
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant active.
Validation & Exceptions
The tenant default must be one of the enabled languages; disabling a language in use switches affected users to the tenant default at next login with an explanatory notice.
Audit
LanguageSettingsChanged with before/after values.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TEN-05
Related
TEN-FR-010, Section 18
TEN-FR-006 Locale, date, and time format settings MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall provide tenant-level settings for date format (e.g. DD/MM/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD), time format (12/24-hour), first day of week, and default time zone. All timestamps shall be stored in UTC and rendered in the viewer's effective time zone and format; printed reports shall state the rendering time zone.
Rationale
Unambiguous dates are essential for record integrity across regions.
Actor
P-02
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant active.
Validation & Exceptions
Only formats from the supported list; changes affect rendering only, never stored values.
Audit
LocaleSettingsChanged with before/after values.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TEN-05
Related
TEN-BR-006
TEN-FR-007 E-signature policy enablement per 21 CFR Part 11 MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall provide a tenant-level e-signature policy that can be enabled per module (e.g. DOC approvals, CAPA closure, MRV sign-off). Enablement or any change shall require approval by the Quality Director with a recorded justification. Once enabled for a module, signature capture (re-authentication, signature meaning, signer name, date/time) shall conform to Section 19; disabling the policy shall apply only to future signatures and shall never invalidate or alter previously captured signatures.
Rationale
Part 11 applicability varies per client; the policy must be a controlled, auditable configuration decision, not a code branch.
Actor
P-02 (requester); P-04 Quality Director (approver)
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant decision to operate a module under Part 11 controls.
Validation & Exceptions
Policy change without Quality Director approval is rejected; retroactive application is technically impossible.
Audit
ESignPolicyChangeRequested/Approved/Applied with module list, before/after state, justification.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TEN-06
Related
TEN-BR-007, Section 19
TEN-FR-008 Approval-route configuration MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall let authorized administrators define named approval routes per module and record type: ordered steps, each resolved to a role, a named user, or the owning unit's manager; sequential or parallel steps; optional quorum for parallel steps; and applicability conditions (record type, organizational unit, category). Routes shall be versioned; in-flight approvals continue on the route version they started with, while new submissions use the latest active version.
Rationale
BUS-OBJ-016; approval topology differs per client and per site.
Actor
P-02, P-03 (scoped)
Preconditions / Trigger
Module entitlement active; roles defined in IAM.
Validation & Exceptions
A route must have at least one step; steps resolving to no eligible user at runtime trigger the unresolved-approver exception (11.2.17); deleting a route in use is blocked — deactivate instead.
Audit
RouteCreated/Changed/Deactivated with version diff.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TEN-07
Related
TEN-FR-009, TEN-BR-008
TEN-FR-009 Escalation-rule configuration MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall let authorized administrators define escalation rules per module: trigger (task overdue by N working days, record idle in status for N working days), escalation target (manager of assignee, named role, named user), repeat interval, maximum escalation levels, and stop conditions. Working-day computation shall use the owning unit's calendar (TEN-FR-004).
Rationale
Overdue visibility (BUS-OBJ-006) requires tenant-tunable escalation rather than fixed intervals.
Actor
P-02, P-03 (scoped)
Preconditions / Trigger
Module active; notification templates available.
Validation & Exceptions
Escalation loops prevented by maximum-level cap; rules with unresolvable targets are flagged at save time.
Audit
EscalationRuleCreated/Changed/Deactivated; each fired escalation recorded in the consuming module.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TEN-07
Related
TEN-FR-010
TEN-FR-010 Notification template management (multilingual) MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall provide editable notification templates per event type (subject and body for email; body for in-app), with language variants for each enabled tenant language and a defined fallback order (recipient preference → tenant default → English). Templates shall support typed placeholders validated at save time (unknown placeholders rejected) and a rendered preview with sample data. System-critical templates may be customized but not deleted.
Rationale
Notifications drive workflow participation; wording and language must match the organization.
Actor
P-02, P-03 (scoped)
Preconditions / Trigger
Event catalogue installed with default templates.
Validation & Exceptions
Placeholder validation per event context; empty mandatory variant falls back per the defined order and is flagged in the template list.
Audit
TemplateChanged with before/after content hash and language.

TEN-FR-011 Lookup and reference data management MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall manage tenant lookup lists (e.g. NC categories, complaint sources, root-cause categories, document types, risk categories) with per-value code, multilingual labels, sort order, and active flag. Values referenced by existing records shall never be hard-deleted: deactivation removes them from selection lists while historical records continue to display them. Value merges (replace A with B on future use) shall be supported with an audited mapping.
Rationale
Reference-data hygiene without breaking historical records (BUS-OBJ-002, BUS-OBJ-005).

P-02, P-03 (scoped)

The system shall let the Tenant Administrator upload a tenant logo (PNG/SVG, max 1 MB), select a primary accent color from an accessibility-checked palette, and define report header/footer text. Branding shall apply to the tenant UI shell and to generated reports and printouts; it shall never alter record content or controlled-document layouts already approved.

TEN-FR-013 Unit deactivation with mandatory reassignment MustCore
Requirement
The system shall permit deactivation of an organizational unit only through an approved change set whose reassignment plan maps every open record, active user assignment, route binding, and numbering scope of that unit (and its descendants) to active target units. Deactivated units shall remain visible in historical records, filters, and reports, clearly marked as deactivated with their deactivation date.
Rationale
Closures and mergers must not orphan open quality records or hide history.
Actor
P-03 (planner); P-05/P-02 (approver); System (executor)
Preconditions / Trigger
Change set deactivating a unit.

Submission blocked while any item is unmapped; execution is transactional — partial reassignment is impossible.

11.2.16 Integration Requirements
  • Inbound — HR/ERP organizational sync (optional): organizational units and manager assignments may be imported as draft change sets via the integration API; imported changes still pass impact analysis and approval — no direct write to the published hierarchy. See Section 14.
  • Outbound — configuration read API: published hierarchy, calendars, numbering schemes, and lookup values exposed read-only to authorized tenant integrations, versioned with as-of-date queries.
  • Internal — all functional modules: DOC, NCR, CAPA, CMP, AUD, TRN, EQP, RSK, and MRV consume TEN configuration (units, routes, calendars, numbering, templates, lookups) through the shared configuration services; TEN publishes change events so consuming modules refresh caches within 60 seconds.
  • Outbound — email gateway: template-rendered notifications per 11.2.14.
Optional future scope: automated bidirectional HR synchronization with conflict resolution is deferred; v1.0 supports import-as-draft only.

11.2.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-TEN-01 — Structure change requires approval and applies on effective date

  • Given an Organization Administrator's change set moving a laboratory to a new branch with effective date next Monday, submitted and approved by the Quality Manager,
  • When the effective date is reached,
  • Then the system publishes a new hierarchy version atomically, the laboratory appears under the new branch, records created before Monday still report against the historical structure for their period, and the full change trail (draft, submit, approve, apply) is in the audit log.

AC-TEN-02 — Deactivation blocked without complete reassignment

  • Given a change set deactivating a department that owns 12 open NCRs and 5 active users,
  • When the administrator attempts to submit with 2 NCRs unmapped,
  • Then submission is blocked listing the unmapped records, and after mapping all items and approval, applying the change reassigns all 12 NCRs and 5 users transactionally with one audited reassignment event each.

AC-TEN-03 — Numbering scheme change affects future records only

  • Given an NCR numbering scheme NCR-{UNIT}-{YYYY}-{SEQ:4} with existing record NCR-LAB1-2026-0042,
  • When the Tenant Administrator changes the pattern to {UNIT}/NCR/{YY}-{SEQ:5} and a new NCR is created,
  • Then the new record receives a number in the new pattern with the sequence continued (not reset unless the reset policy says so), record NCR-LAB1-2026-0042 keeps its number unchanged, and the scheme change is audited with before/after patterns.

AC-TEN-04 — Due dates follow the owning unit's calendar

  • Given a unit on a Sunday–Thursday calendar with a declared holiday on Thursday,
  • When a task with a 3-working-day SLA is created on Wednesday,
  • Then the computed due date skips Thursday (holiday), Friday, and Saturday (weekend) and falls on the following Monday, and a later calendar change does not alter this already-computed due date.

AC-TEN-05 — Arabic RTL rendering and template language fallback

  • Given a tenant with English and Arabic enabled and a user whose preference is Arabic,
  • When the user logs in and triggers an event whose template has no Arabic variant,
  • Then the UI renders fully right-to-left with mirrored layout, embedded codes and numbers remain left-to-right readable, and the notification is delivered using the tenant-default variant with the missing Arabic variant flagged in the administrator's template list.

AC-TEN-06 — E-signature policy enablement is approval-gated and non-retroactive

  • Given a Tenant Administrator request to enable Part 11 e-signatures for the DOC module,
  • When the Quality Director approves the request with justification,
  • Then subsequent DOC approvals require signature capture per Section 19, approvals completed before enablement remain valid and unmodified, and an attempt to enable the policy without Quality Director approval is rejected and audited.

AC-TEN-07 — Route versioning pins in-flight approvals

  • Given a document submitted on approval route version 3,
  • When the Tenant Administrator publishes route version 4 adding an extra step,
  • Then the in-flight document completes on version 3, a document submitted afterwards uses version 4, and both records reference their route version in the audit trail.

11.3 Identity & Access Management IAM

11.3.1 Module Overview
Module nameIdentity & Access Management
Module codeIAM
PurposeManage the full lifecycle of user identities, authentication, and authorization within each tenant: invitation, activation, role and permission assignment scoped by organizational structure, delegation, deactivation, and offboarding.
Business valueEnsures only authorized, verifiable individuals can create, review, approve, or sign quality records; provides the access-control foundation for approvals, segregation of duties, and audit-defensible attribution across every module (BUS-OBJ-004, BUS-OBJ-008, BUS-OBJ-015).
ScopeUser lifecycle (invite, activate, deactivate, offboard); local credential authentication; SSO via OIDC and SAML 2.0; MFA; password policy; session management and device revocation; role management (RBAC with attribute-based restrictions); permission assignment scoped by organization/branch/department/site; time-bound delegation and acting assignments; segregation-of-duties constraints; access reviews/recertification; account lockout and brute-force protection; security event logging.
Out of scopePlatform-operator identities (see 11.1 PLT); creation of tenants and organizational structure (see 11.2 TEN); HR employee master-data management (integration only, see Section 14); physical access control.
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 cl. 7.1.6, 7.2, 7.5.3 (access control to documented information); ISO/IEC 17025:2017 cl. 5.6, 8.4; 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(d),(g),(i), §11.300 (where enabled); GxP data-integrity (ALCOA+) attribution principles.
Related modulesPLT, TEN, Personas & Permissions, E-Signatures; consumed by every functional module for authorization decisions.
Primary personasP-02 Tenant Administrator, P-03 Organization Administrator, P-07 Department Manager, P-05 Quality Manager, P-20 Employee, P-31 Integration Service Account.

11.3.2 Business Problem

Quality management processes are defined by who may act: who may release a controlled document, who may disposition a nonconformance, who may verify CAPA effectiveness. In paper-based and fragmented electronic environments, access is granted informally, shared accounts obscure attribution, leavers retain access for weeks, and no one can produce an authoritative answer to the auditor's question "who can approve this record, and why?". These gaps translate directly into audit findings, data-integrity risk, and regulatory exposure.

The organization requires a single, backend-enforced access-control layer in which every grant of authority is explicit, scoped to the correct part of the organization (organization, branch, department, site), time-bound where temporary, constrained by segregation-of-duties rules, periodically recertified, and fully audit-trailed. Authorization must never depend on what the client application chooses to display; the server must be the sole enforcement point, and the tenant context must derive exclusively from trusted token claims — never from request parameters.

11.3.3 Business Objectives
  • BUS-OBJ-004 — Enforce approvals and segregation of duties through role- and scope-based authorization that the backend evaluates on every request.
  • BUS-OBJ-005 — Guarantee traceability by attributing every action to a uniquely identified, individually authenticated user.
  • BUS-OBJ-008 — Feed immutable audit trails with reliable identity, session, and security events.
  • BUS-OBJ-010 — Maintain audit readiness through on-demand access matrices and completed recertification evidence.
  • BUS-OBJ-015 — Protect tenant data by binding every session to a single tenant derived from trusted claims and denying all cross-tenant access.
  • BUS-OBJ-016 — Support configurable workflows by exposing roles, scopes, and delegation as configuration rather than code.

11.3.4 Actors & Personas
Role in modulePersona(s)Responsibilities
Primary actorsP-02 Tenant Administrator, P-03 Organization AdministratorInvite users, assign scoped roles, configure authentication policy, run access reviews, deactivate and offboard users.
Supporting actorsP-07 Department ManagerRequest access for team members; certify their access during reviews; set up acting assignments for absences.
ApproversP-02 Tenant Administrator (privileged roles), P-05 Quality Manager (quality roles)Approve access requests and role changes per the approval matrix.
ReviewersP-04 Quality Director, P-15 Internal AuditorReview access matrices, recertification results, and security event reports.
AdministratorsP-01 Platform AdministratorOperate identity-provider federation at platform level only; no access to tenant business records (11.1).

External / systemP-31 Integration Service Account, P-30 External Service ProviderMachine-to-machine authentication with scoped, non-interactive credentials; externally sponsored accounts with mandatory expiry dates.

11.3.5 Preconditions
  • The tenant exists and is active, and its organizational structure (organization, branches, departments, sites) is defined in TEN.
  • Tenant authentication policy is configured (local credentials and/or SSO; MFA settings; password policy).
  • At least one Tenant Administrator account is active in the tenant.
  • Role catalog (system roles plus any tenant-defined roles) is published and mapped to permissions.
  • Where SSO is used, the tenant's identity provider (OIDC or SAML 2.0) is registered and its metadata validated.
  • Notification services (email) are operational for invitation and security notifications.

11.3.6 Trigger Events
  • A manager or administrator submits a new-user access request (hire, transfer, contractor onboarding).
  • A role or scope change is requested (promotion, department transfer, added responsibility).
  • An employee is offboarded (resignation, termination, contract end) — manually or via HR integration event (Section 14).
  • A user requests password reset, MFA re-enrollment, or reports a lost device.
  • A scheduled access-review (recertification) campaign starts.
  • A planned absence requires a time-bound acting assignment or delegation.
  • Security telemetry detects repeated failed logins, an unrecognized device, or a cross-tenant access attempt.
