11.3.11 Functional Requirements
IAM-FR-001 Approved, invitation-based user provisioning MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provision tenant user accounts only through an access request that captures identity data, requested roles, scope bindings, and justification, passes an automated SoD pre-check, and is approved per the tenant approval matrix before a single-use invitation is issued. Direct account creation bypassing the request flow shall be impossible for all tenant roles.
Rationale
Every grant of access must be justified, checked, and approved to satisfy BUS-OBJ-004 and audit expectations.
Actor
Org Administrator, Dept Manager (request); Tenant Admin / Quality Manager (approve)
Preconditions / Trigger
Active tenant; role catalog published; new-hire or access-change trigger (11.3.6).
Validation & Exceptions
Email unique per tenant; scope within requester's authority; SoD conflicts block submission routing per IAM-BR-006; duplicate email surfaces the existing account instead of creating a second one.
Audit
AccessRequestCreated/Submitted/Decided, UserProvisioned with requester, approver, before/after role set.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-01, AC-IAM-02
Related
IAM-BR-001, IAM-BR-004, RPT-IAM-02
IAM-FR-002 Secure account activation MustCore
Requirement
The system shall activate accounts via a cryptographically random, single-use invitation token delivered by email, expiring after 7 calendar days (proposed target — pending business confirmation). Activation shall require email-ownership verification, credential establishment, MFA enrollment where mandated, and acknowledgement of the acceptable-use statement before the account becomes Active.
Rationale
Prevents account takeover during onboarding and evidences user acknowledgement of responsibilities.
Actor
New user (P-20)
Preconditions / Trigger
Provisioned account in status Invited.
Validation & Exceptions
Expired or already-used tokens are rejected with a re-invitation path; tokens are invalidated when a new invitation is issued for the same account.
Audit
InvitationSent/Redeemed/Expired, CredentialEstablished, MfaEnrolled, UserActivated.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-01
Related
IAM-BR-004
IAM-FR-003 Local credential authentication MustCore
Requirement
The system shall authenticate local accounts with username/email and password verified against a salted adaptive hash (Argon2id or equivalent), shall never store or transmit passwords in recoverable form, and shall return a single generic failure message for wrong identifier, wrong password, or non-existent account.
Rationale
Baseline credential security and enumeration resistance.
Actor
All users
Preconditions / Trigger
Active account with authentication mode Local or Local+SSO.
Validation & Exceptions
Failed attempts feed lockout counters (IAM-FR-014); suspended/deactivated accounts fail with the same generic message while the true cause is security-logged.
Audit
SignInSucceeded / SignInFailed with timestamp, IP, device fingerprint (no credential material).
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-04
Related
IAM-FR-006, IAM-BR-011
IAM-FR-004 Single sign-on via OIDC and SAML 2.0 MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall support per-tenant federation with one or more corporate identity providers over OpenID Connect (authorization code flow with PKCE) and SAML 2.0 (SP-initiated), including signature and issuer validation, clock-skew tolerance, and mapping of the IdP subject to exactly one pre-provisioned NT.QMS account by verified email or immutable subject identifier. SSO shall satisfy authentication only; roles and scopes remain managed inside NT.QMS.
Rationale
Enterprise customers require corporate credential reuse without ceding authorization control.
Actor
Tenant Administrator (configure); all users (sign in)
Preconditions / Trigger
IdP registered with validated metadata; account authentication mode includes SSO.
Validation & Exceptions
Assertions failing signature, audience, expiry, or replay checks are rejected and security-logged; unmatched subjects are denied — no just-in-time account creation without an approved access request.
Audit
FederatedSignIn, AssertionRejected with IdP, reason, correlation id.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-04
Related
Section 14, IAM-BR-002
IAM-FR-005 Multi-factor authentication MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall support TOTP authenticator apps as the primary second factor and email OTP as a fallback, enforceable per tenant globally or per role (mandatory for administrator and approver roles by default), with admin-initiated MFA reset requiring a reason and generating a security notification to the affected user.
Rationale
Credential theft is the dominant attack vector; approvers and admins carry elevated risk.
Actor
All users; Tenant Administrator (policy, resets)
Preconditions / Trigger
MFA policy enabled; sign-in or step-up event.
Validation & Exceptions
OTP validity window and retry limits enforced; exhausted retries count toward lockout; users with no enrolled factor under a mandatory policy are forced into enrollment before session issuance.
Audit
MfaEnrolled/Verified/Failed/Reset with actor and reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-04
Related
IAM-BR-012, Section 19
IAM-FR-006 Configurable password policy MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall enforce a tenant-configurable password policy covering minimum length (default 12), character composition, prohibition of the username/email inside the password, password history depth (default: last 5 reuses blocked), maximum age with expiry warnings (default 90 days — proposed target, pending business confirmation), and rejection of passwords found in a maintained compromised-password list. Policy changes shall apply at next password change without invalidating current sessions.
Rationale
Aligns with 21 CFR Part 11 §11.300 and corporate security baselines while remaining tenant-adaptable.
Actor
Tenant Administrator (configure); users (comply)
Preconditions / Trigger
Password set, change, or reset event.
Validation & Exceptions
Violations return the specific unmet rules inline; reset links are single-use and expire after 60 minutes (proposed target — pending business confirmation).
Audit
PasswordChanged/ResetRequested/ResetCompleted, PolicyUpdated with before/after values.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-04
Related
IAM-BR-011
IAM-FR-007 Session management and device revocation MustCore
Requirement
The system shall issue short-lived access tokens with refresh rotation, enforce a configurable idle timeout (default 30 minutes) and absolute session lifetime (default 12 hours — both proposed targets, pending business confirmation), present each user a list of their active sessions/devices (device description, IP, last activity), and allow the user or a Tenant Administrator to revoke any single session or all sessions, with revocation effective on the next request (≤ 60 seconds).
Rationale
Limits exposure of unattended or stolen sessions and gives users control over their devices.
Actor
All users (own sessions); Tenant Administrator (any user's sessions)
Preconditions / Trigger
Authenticated session; revocation request; deactivation/suspension events.
Validation & Exceptions
Revoked refresh tokens are unusable; reuse of a rotated refresh token revokes the whole token family and raises a security event.
Audit
SessionIssued/Refreshed/Revoked, DeviceRegistered, TokenReuseDetected.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-05
Related
IAM-BR-007, SEC-NFRs
IAM-FR-008 Role management (system and tenant-defined roles) MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall provide a versioned role catalog comprising non-editable system roles aligned to the personas in Section 13 and tenant-defined roles composed from the published permission catalog. Role changes shall be draft-then-publish with impact preview (count of affected users) and shall never grant permissions outside the tenant's licensed modules.
Rationale
Tenants differ organizationally; role composition must be configuration, not code (BUS-OBJ-016).
Actor
Tenant Administrator
Preconditions / Trigger
Permission catalog published; role creation or change request.
Validation & Exceptions
A role in use cannot be deleted — only deprecated (blocked for new assignment); publishing a role edit re-evaluates SoD constraints across existing holders and reports violations before commit.
Audit
RoleCreated/Published/Deprecated with permission diff and affected-user count.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-02
Related
IAM-BR-005, RPT-IAM-01
IAM-FR-009 Scoped permission assignment MustCore
Requirement
The system shall bind every role assignment to one or more scope nodes of the tenant's organizational structure (organization, branch, department, site), such that the effective permission applies only to records belonging to those nodes and their descendants. Attribute-based restrictions (e.g. exclusion of confidential records, limitation to specified record categories) shall further narrow — never widen — the scoped grant.
Rationale
A Department Manager in Branch A must not act on Branch B records; scoping expresses real organizational authority.
Actor
Tenant Administrator, Org Administrator (grant); all modules (consume)
Preconditions / Trigger
Organizational structure defined in TEN; approved access request.
Validation & Exceptions
Granters may only assign scopes within their own authority; when a scope node is deactivated in TEN, dependent assignments are flagged for remediation and listed in RPT-IAM-01.
Audit
RoleAssigned/RoleRevoked/ScopeChanged with before/after scope sets.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-03
Related
IAM-FR-010, IAM-BR-003
IAM-FR-010 Backend-enforced, deny-by-default authorization MustCore
Requirement
The system shall evaluate every API request server-side against the caller's effective permission set (roles × scopes × attribute restrictions × active delegations), denying by default. Tenant context shall derive exclusively from validated token claims; tenant or scope identifiers supplied in the request body, query string, or headers shall never widen access. UI element hiding is a usability aid only and shall never be the enforcement mechanism.
Rationale
Client-side controls are trivially bypassed; the server is the only trustworthy policy enforcement point (BUS-OBJ-015).
Actor
System (all endpoints)
Preconditions / Trigger
Every authenticated request.
Validation & Exceptions
Unauthorized attempts return a non-revealing authorization error; cross-tenant attempts are additionally security-logged and alerted per IAM-FR-016. Database-level tenant isolation via PostgreSQL RLS backs the application check (Section 10).
Audit
AuthorizationDenied with endpoint, subject, tenant claim, target resource (id only).
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-03, AC-IAM-07
Related
IAM-BR-002, SEC-NFRs
IAM-FR-011 Time-bound delegation and acting assignments MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow a user (or their manager/Tenant Administrator) to delegate a defined subset of the user's permissions to a named colleague for a mandatory start/end period, activating and expiring automatically. Actions performed under delegation shall be attributed as "delegate acting for delegator", both identities recorded. Delegation shall never exceed the delegator's own effective permissions and shall be blocked where it would create an SoD conflict for the delegate.
Rationale
Approvals must continue during absences without password sharing or permanent over-provisioning.
Actor
Delegator, Dept Manager, Tenant Administrator
Preconditions / Trigger
Planned absence; both accounts Active.
Validation & Exceptions
Maximum duration per IAM-BR-008; delegator deactivation terminates the delegation immediately; delegate is notified at activation and expiry.
Audit
DelegationCreated/Activated/Expired/Revoked; every delegated action carries the dual-identity attribution.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-06
Related
IAM-BR-008, RPT-IAM-06
IAM-FR-012 Segregation-of-duties constraint management MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall maintain a tenant-configurable SoD matrix of mutually exclusive role pairs (seeded with defaults such as Requester vs. Approver of the same record type, CAPA Action Owner vs. CAPA Effectiveness Verifier) and shall enforce it at role assignment, role publication, delegation creation, and — for record-level rules such as "author cannot approve own record" — at the moment of the workflow action in each module.
Rationale
SoD is a core control expected by ISO 9001 and GxP auditors (BUS-OBJ-004).
Actor
Tenant Administrator (configure); system (enforce)
Preconditions / Trigger
SoD matrix published; any role/delegation grant or constrained workflow action.
Validation & Exceptions
Violations are blocking; a documented exception may be approved by the Quality Director for a defined period, is flagged in all access reports, and expires automatically.
Audit
SoDViolationBlocked, SoDExceptionApproved/Expired with rule, parties, justification.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-02
Related
IAM-BR-006, Section 19
IAM-FR-013 Access reviews and recertification campaigns MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall run scheduled recertification campaigns (default: every 6 months for privileged roles, every 12 months for all others — proposed targets, pending business confirmation) in which each user's access is presented to the designated certifier (line manager or Tenant Administrator) for a Confirm / Modify / Revoke decision per assignment. Revocations shall take effect immediately upon certifier decision; campaigns produce immutable completion evidence.
Rationale
Access accumulates over time; periodic recertification is required audit evidence (BUS-OBJ-010).
Actor
Tenant Administrator (campaign); Dept Manager (certify)
Preconditions / Trigger
Campaign schedule or ad-hoc launch (e.g. post-incident).
Validation & Exceptions
Uncertified assignments past the campaign deadline are escalated and, after a grace period per IAM-BR-010, automatically suspended pending review.
Audit
CampaignStarted/Completed, AccessCertified/Revoked with certifier, decision, timestamp.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-08
Related
RPT-IAM-05
IAM-FR-014 Account lockout and brute-force protection MustCore
Requirement
The system shall lock an account after 5 consecutive failed authentication attempts within 15 minutes for a lockout period of 30 minutes (proposed targets — pending business confirmation), apply progressive per-IP throttling and CAPTCHA-free rate limiting on authentication endpoints, and allow a Tenant Administrator to unlock early with a recorded reason. Lockout responses shall be indistinguishable from ordinary authentication failure to the caller.
Rationale
Defeats credential-stuffing and brute-force attacks without enabling account-lockout denial-of-service reconnaissance.
Actor
System; Tenant Administrator (unlock)
Preconditions / Trigger
Consecutive authentication failures.
Validation & Exceptions
Counters reset on success; MFA failures count toward the same threshold; lockout of an administrator account triggers an immediate security alert.
Audit
AccountLocked/Unlocked with trigger counts, source IPs, unlock actor and reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-04
Related
IAM-FR-016, IAM-BR-011
IAM-FR-015 Deactivation and offboarding MustCore
Requirement
The system shall deactivate a user on administrator action or HR-integration offboarding event, immediately revoking all sessions, refresh tokens, and API credentials, terminating outbound delegations, and generating a reassignment worklist of the user's open tasks, pending approvals, and record ownerships for the responsible manager. The identity record and its history shall be preserved for attribution; physical deletion of a referenced identity shall be impossible.
Rationale
Leavers must lose access within minutes, while historical records must keep valid attribution forever.
Actor
Tenant Administrator, Org Administrator; HR integration (P-31)
Preconditions / Trigger
Offboarding trigger (11.3.6).
Validation & Exceptions
Deactivating the last active Tenant Administrator is blocked per IAM-BR-009; open-item reassignment is tracked to completion in the worklist.
Audit
UserDeactivated, SessionsRevoked, ReassignmentListGenerated with counts and recipients.
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-05
Related
IAM-BR-007, RPT-IAM-03
IAM-FR-016 Security event logging and alerting MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall record all authentication, authorization-denial, credential, MFA, session, role-change, delegation, SoD, and lockout events in a tamper-evident security log (append-only, integrity-chained), retained per Section 21, queryable by Tenant Administrators for their tenant only, and shall raise near-real-time alerts (≤ 5 minutes — proposed target, pending business confirmation) for cross-tenant access attempts, refresh-token reuse, administrator lockouts, and privileged role grants.
Rationale
Security telemetry is the detective control complementing preventive authorization (BUS-OBJ-008).
Actor
System; Tenant Administrator, P-15 Internal Auditor (consume)
Preconditions / Trigger
Any security-relevant event.
Validation & Exceptions
Log-write failure on a security-critical action causes the action itself to fail closed; no credential secrets or password material ever appear in logs.
Audit
The security log is itself audit evidence; access to it is logged (SecurityLogQueried).
Acceptance criteria
AC-IAM-07
Related
RPT-IAM-04, ADT-NFRs

11.3.16 Integration Requirements
  • Inbound — corporate identity providers: OIDC / SAML 2.0 federation for authentication (IAM-FR-004); per-tenant IdP registration with metadata validation. See INT-001 in Section 14.
  • Inbound — HR system events: hire, transfer, and termination events drive access requests and offboarding (IAM-FR-015); employee-reference matching with manual reconciliation queue for unmatched events. See INT-002.
  • Outbound — email/notification gateway: invitations, security notices, escalations per 11.3.14. See INT-003.
  • Outbound — SIEM / log export: security event stream in structured format for tenant or platform SIEM consumption (IAM-FR-016). See INT-004.
  • Internal — all modules: IAM exposes the authorization decision service (effective permissions, scope resolution, SoD record-level checks) consumed by every module and by e-signature identity re-verification.
Note: Integration service accounts (P-31) authenticate with client-credential grants, are scoped to named endpoints, cannot sign in interactively, and their credentials rotate per the security policy in Section 18.

11.3.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-IAM-01 — Invitation token single use and expiry

  • Given a provisioned account whose invitation was issued 8 days ago (expiry 7 days),
  • When the user opens the invitation link,
  • Then activation is refused, the token is marked expired, an InvitationExpired event is logged, and the requester is notified with a re-issue option; a previously redeemed token is likewise refused on second use.

AC-IAM-02 — SoD conflict blocks role grant

  • Given a user holding role "CAPA Action Owner" and an SoD rule declaring it mutually exclusive with "CAPA Effectiveness Verifier",
  • When an access request adding "CAPA Effectiveness Verifier" is submitted,
  • Then the system returns the request for correction citing the exact conflicting pair, no role is assigned, and an SoDViolationBlocked event is recorded.

AC-IAM-03 — Scope enforcement on the backend

  • Given a Department Manager whose role is scoped to Department A,
  • When the user calls the records API directly with the identifier of a Department B record (bypassing the UI),
  • Then the backend returns an authorization denial, the record content is not disclosed, and an AuthorizationDenied event is logged with subject, endpoint, and target id.

AC-IAM-04 — Lockout after repeated failures with uniform messaging

  • Given an Active local account,
  • When 5 consecutive wrong-password attempts occur within 15 minutes and a 6th attempt uses the correct password,
  • Then the account is Locked before the 6th attempt, that attempt fails with the same generic message as the previous failures, an AccountLocked event records the source IPs, and the owner receives a lockout notification.

AC-IAM-05 — Deactivation revokes sessions immediately

  • Given a user with an active session on two devices,
  • When a Tenant Administrator deactivates the account,
  • Then every subsequent request from either session is rejected within 60 seconds, all refresh tokens are invalid, outbound delegations are terminated, and a reassignment worklist of the user's open items is generated for the responsible manager.

AC-IAM-06 — Delegation activates and expires on schedule

  • Given an approved delegation of approval permissions from user A to user B for 2026-08-10 through 2026-08-20,
  • When user B attempts an approval on 2026-08-09 and again on 2026-08-21,
  • Then both attempts are denied; an approval performed on 2026-08-15 succeeds and is attributed as "B acting for A" with both identities in the record and audit trail.

AC-IAM-07 — Cross-tenant attempt denied and alerted

  • Given an authenticated user of Tenant X holding a valid token,
  • When the user requests a resource belonging to Tenant Y by direct identifier,
  • Then the request is denied with a generic authorization error, no Tenant Y data (including existence confirmation) is disclosed, a CrossTenantDenied security event is logged, and an alert reaches the Tenant Y administrator channel within 5 minutes.

AC-IAM-08 — Recertification revocation is immediate

  • Given an open access-review campaign item for user C's "Document Approver" role,
  • When the certifier selects Revoke,
  • Then the role assignment ends immediately, user C can no longer perform approvals (verified by a denied approval attempt), and the campaign evidence records certifier, decision, and timestamp immutably.

11.4 Dashboards & Executive Analytics DSH

11.4.1 Module Overview
Module nameDashboards & Executive Analytics
Module codeDSH
PurposeProvide the in-app analytics layer: role-based dashboards composed of KPI cards, charts, my-tasks widgets, and alert feeds, with organizational and date filtering, drill-down to source records, saved views, and export.
Business valueTurns quality data into daily operational visibility: overdue items are seen before they age, KPI breaches trigger action, and executives get audit-ready status at a glance (BUS-OBJ-006, BUS-OBJ-013).
ScopeRole-based dashboard composition; KPI cards with thresholds; trend/distribution/pareto charts; my-tasks widgets; alert feed and KPI-breach alerting; drill-down to permission-trimmed source records; global filters (organization/branch/department/site); date ranges and comparison; saved personal and shared views; refresh and data-freshness indication; empty/error/loading states; export of dashboard views.
Out of scopeThe detailed per-role dashboard catalog and KPI definitions per module (specified in Section 16 — Dashboard Requirements); formatted operational/compliance reports (Section 15); external BI tooling (data export integration only, Section 14); predictive/ML analytics (optional future scope).
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 cl. 9.1 (monitoring, measurement, analysis, evaluation) and cl. 9.3 (management review inputs); ISO/IEC 17025:2017 cl. 8.9.
Related modulesConsumes data from all functional modules (DOC, NCR, CAPA, CMP, AUD, TRN, EQP, RSK, MRV); authorization from IAM; catalog in Section 16.
Primary personasP-27 Executive Management User, P-04 Quality Director, P-05 Quality Manager, P-07 Department Manager, P-20 Employee (my-tasks), P-28 Read-Only User.

11.4.2 Business Problem

Quality status today is assembled manually: spreadsheets are exported from disparate trackers, aggregated by hand, and presented in slide decks that are outdated on arrival. Overdue CAPAs, expiring documents, and unclosed nonconformances surface only when someone remembers to look, and executives cannot answer "what is our quality position right now?" without commissioning a data-gathering exercise.

The organization needs live, role-appropriate dashboards where every number is computed from the system of record, respects the viewer's permissions and organizational scope, links directly to the underlying records, and actively alerts responsible owners when a KPI crosses its threshold — closing the loop from measurement to action rather than merely displaying data.

11.4.3 Business Objectives
  • BUS-OBJ-006 — Make overdue and aging items continuously visible to owners and managers through widgets and alerts.
  • BUS-OBJ-013 — Provide management reporting from live data: KPI cards, trends, and drill-down replacing manual status compilation.
  • BUS-OBJ-005 — Preserve traceability: every aggregate figure drills down to the identifiable source records that compose it.
  • BUS-OBJ-010 — Support audit readiness with exportable, timestamped dashboard snapshots.
  • BUS-OBJ-014 — Serve multi-site organizations through organization/branch/department/site filtering and localized UI (EN/AR/FR, RTL-aware charts).
  • BUS-OBJ-015 — Compute all aggregates strictly within tenant boundaries and the viewer's authorized scope.

11.4.4 Actors & Personas
Role in modulePersona(s)Responsibilities
Primary actorsP-27 Executive Management User, P-04 Quality Director, P-05 Quality ManagerMonitor KPIs, acknowledge breaches, drill down, initiate follow-up tasks, export views for reviews.
Supporting actorsP-07 Department Manager, P-08 Process OwnerTrack departmental widgets and my-team workload; act on alerts routed to their scope.
ApproversP-05 Quality ManagerApprove publication of shared dashboard views and tenant KPI threshold changes.
ReviewersP-26 Management Review CoordinatorUse dashboard snapshots as management-review inputs (MRV).
AdministratorsP-02 Tenant AdministratorAssign default dashboards to roles; manage shared views; configure alert routing defaults.

External / systemP-31 Integration Service AccountPull aggregated KPI data for external BI where licensed (Section 14).

11.4.5 Preconditions
  • The viewer is authenticated with an Active account and at least one role granting dashboard access (IAM).
  • Source modules are licensed and populated; KPI definitions and thresholds for the tenant are published (catalog per Section 16).
  • Organizational structure exists so scope filters can be resolved (TEN).
  • Aggregation jobs / materialized summaries are operational and their last-computed timestamps available.
  • Default role-to-dashboard mappings are configured by the Tenant Administrator.

11.4.6 Trigger Events
  • A user opens the application home (default dashboard loads for their primary role).
  • A scheduled KPI computation completes and a value crosses a configured threshold (breach or recovery).
  • A user changes filters, date range, or comparison period, or opens a saved view.
  • A user drills down from an aggregate into the underlying record list or a single record.
  • A user acknowledges an alert or creates a follow-up task from a breach.
  • A user saves, shares, or exports a dashboard view.
  • A widget's source module returns an error or no data (empty/error state rendering).

11.4.11 Functional Requirements
DSH-FR-001 Role-based dashboard composition MustCore
Requirement
The system shall render, on application entry, the default dashboard mapped to the viewer's primary role (per-role catalog in Section 16), composed only of widgets whose underlying permissions the viewer holds; widgets for unlicensed modules or unauthorized data shall be omitted entirely rather than rendered empty or disabled.
Rationale
Each persona needs a relevant starting view without exposure to unauthorized aggregates.
Actor
All dashboard users; Tenant Administrator (role-to-dashboard mapping)
Preconditions / Trigger
Authenticated session; role mapping configured; application entry or dashboard navigation.
Validation & Exceptions
Users with multiple roles may switch among their mapped dashboards; a user with no mapping receives the tenant baseline dashboard (my-tasks + notifications only).
Audit
DashboardViewed with dashboard id and role context (sampled per audit policy).
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-01
Related
DSH-BR-001, Section 16
DSH-FR-002 KPI cards with thresholds and trend indication MustCore
Requirement
The system shall display KPI cards showing current value, unit, threshold status (within / warning / critical, color- and icon-coded, not color-only), trend direction versus the comparison period, and the data-freshness timestamp. Card values shall be computed from source-module data within the viewer's scope and the active filters.
Rationale
At-a-glance status with defensible numbers is the core executive need (BUS-OBJ-013).
Actor
All dashboard users
Preconditions / Trigger
KPI definitions and thresholds published; dashboard render or filter change.
Validation & Exceptions
A KPI without configured thresholds renders neutrally with a "no threshold" marker; stale data beyond the configured freshness limit is visibly flagged.
Audit
Threshold configuration changes audited (versioned); card rendering not individually audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-02
Related
DSH-FR-013, DSH-BR-002
DSH-FR-003 Chart widgets (trend, distribution, pareto) MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide chart widgets for time-series trends, categorical distributions (status, org unit, category), and pareto analysis (top contributing causes/categories), each honoring active filters and date range, with accessible tabular alternatives (per-widget data table toggle) and RTL-correct rendering for Arabic UI.
Rationale
Trends and pareto views drive prioritization in quality management (ISO 9001 cl. 9.1.3).
Actor
All dashboard users
Preconditions / Trigger
Widget on dashboard; data available for period.
Validation & Exceptions
Series exceeding a readable point density are aggregated (e.g. daily → weekly) with the aggregation level indicated; empty result renders the empty state per DSH-FR-011.
Audit
None per render; widget-catalog changes audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-03
Related
DSH-FR-006
DSH-FR-004 My-tasks widget MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide a my-tasks widget aggregating the viewer's open work items across all licensed modules (pending approvals, assigned actions, reviews, training due, calibration tasks, alert follow-ups), sorted by due date with overdue items flagged first, each item opening the source record directly.
Rationale
A single worklist is the primary daily entry point for most personas (BUS-OBJ-006).
Actor
All users (P-20 upward)
Preconditions / Trigger
Authenticated session; items assigned to the viewer or to them via delegation.
Validation & Exceptions
Items received via delegation are marked "acting for [delegator]"; counts match the source modules' own worklists.
Audit
None per render; task actions audited in owning modules.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-04
Related
IAM-FR-011
DSH-FR-005 Alert feed and notification-centre integration MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide an alert-feed widget listing open KPI alerts within the viewer's scope (severity, KPI, scope node, age, status), synchronized with the in-app notification centre, supporting acknowledge and open-alert actions inline.
Rationale
Alerts must be visible where users work, not only in email.
Actor
Quality Manager, Quality Director, scoped owners
Preconditions / Trigger
Open alerts exist within viewer scope.
Validation & Exceptions
Alerts outside the viewer's scope are never listed; acknowledgement requires scope authorization.
Audit
AlertViewed/Acknowledged per 11.4.19.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-05
Related
DSH-FR-013
DSH-FR-006 Drill-down to source records MustCore
Requirement
The system shall let the viewer drill from any aggregate (KPI card, chart segment, alert) into the list of source records composing that figure, carrying the active filters, scope, and period, and from the list into individual records in their owning modules. Record access at every drill level shall be re-authorized by the backend (IAM-FR-010).
Rationale
Every number must be explainable to an auditor by enumeration of its records (BUS-OBJ-005).
Actor
All dashboard users
Preconditions / Trigger
Aggregate rendered; drill action.
Validation & Exceptions
Where record-level permissions hide some composing records from the viewer, the list displays a trimming notice ("N of M records visible to you") per DSH-BR-003; the aggregate itself reflects the viewer's scope so mismatches arise only from record-level restrictions.
Audit
DrillDownExecuted with aggregate context; record views audited by owning modules.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-03
Related
Section 17
DSH-FR-007 Organizational scope filters MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide global dashboard filters for organization, branch, department, and site, offering only nodes within the viewer's authorized scope, applying the selection consistently to every widget on the dashboard, and persisting the last selection per user across sessions.
Rationale
Multi-site management requires slicing the same KPIs by unit without separate dashboards (BUS-OBJ-014).
Actor
All dashboard users
Preconditions / Trigger
Structure defined in TEN; filter interaction.
Validation & Exceptions
Filter values are validated server-side against the viewer's scope on every data request — a manipulated filter value outside scope returns an authorization denial, not data.
Audit
None per interaction; denials logged as AuthorizationDenied.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-01
Related
IAM-FR-009
DSH-FR-008 Date ranges and period comparison MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support fixed date ranges and rolling presets (last 7/30/90 days, month-, quarter-, year-to-date) plus an optional comparison period (previous period or same period last year), applying the selection to all time-sensitive widgets and labeling every widget with the effective period.
Rationale
Trend interpretation requires explicit, comparable periods.
Actor
All dashboard users
Preconditions / Trigger
Dashboard rendered; period interaction.
Validation & Exceptions
Start must not exceed end; future end dates are capped at today; periods exceeding the configured maximum span (default 24 months — proposed target, pending business confirmation) prompt aggregation to monthly granularity.
Audit
None.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-03
Related
DSH-FR-003
DSH-FR-009 Saved views (personal and shared) MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall let users save a dashboard configuration (layout, widget settings, filters, date range) as a named personal view and restore it on demand; sharing a view to defined roles or org units shall require Quality Manager approval, and a shared view shall always render with the individual viewer's own permissions and scope — never the owner's.
Rationale
Recurring analyses (e.g. monthly review layout) should be one click, and shared layouts must not become a privilege-escalation channel.
Actor
All dashboard users (personal); Quality Manager (share approval)
Preconditions / Trigger
Configured dashboard; save/share action.
Validation & Exceptions
Name unique per owner; shared-view suspension immediately hides it from the audience; owner offboarding transfers shared views to the Tenant Administrator for reassignment.
Audit
ViewSaved/Shared/Suspended/Archived with definition version.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-06
Related
DSH-BR-004
DSH-FR-010 Refresh behavior and data freshness MustCore
Requirement
The system shall display per-widget data-freshness timestamps, support manual refresh (whole dashboard and per widget) with server-side rate limiting, and auto-refresh operational widgets (my-tasks, alert feed) at a configurable interval (default 5 minutes — proposed target, pending business confirmation) without disrupting user interaction or scroll position.
Rationale
Users must know how current a number is; uncontrolled refresh must not overload aggregation services.
Actor
All dashboard users; Tenant Administrator (intervals)
Preconditions / Trigger
Dashboard open; refresh action or timer.
Validation & Exceptions
Refresh requests beyond the rate limit are coalesced, with the freshest available data returned; failed refresh keeps the last good data with an error badge per DSH-FR-011.
Audit
None.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-02
Related
PER-NFRs
DSH-FR-011 Empty, loading, and error states MustCore
Requirement
The system shall render, per widget: a loading skeleton while data is fetched; a distinct empty state ("no data for the selected filters/period" with a filter-reset shortcut) when the query returns nothing; and an error state (widget-level, with a retry control and support reference id) when a source fails — an individual widget failure shall never blank the whole dashboard, and error states shall be visually distinct from genuine zero values.
Rationale
An indistinguishable "0" versus "failed to load" can mislead management decisions.
Actor
All dashboard users
Preconditions / Trigger
Any widget render.
Validation & Exceptions
Repeated failures of the same widget raise an operational alert to platform monitoring (PLT).
Audit
WidgetErrorRendered (operational log).
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-07
Related
DSH-FR-010
DSH-FR-012 Export of dashboard views MustCore
Requirement
The system shall export the currently rendered dashboard as a timestamped PDF snapshot (layout preserved, filters and periods printed in the header, freshness timestamps per widget) and individual widget data as XLSX/CSV, containing only data the exporting viewer is authorized to see, with every export watermarked (tenant, exporter, timestamp) and audit-logged.
Rationale
Management reviews and audits need portable, attributable evidence of dashboard state (BUS-OBJ-010).
Actor
Users holding export permission
Preconditions / Trigger
Rendered dashboard; export action.
Validation & Exceptions
Export of a widget in error state is blocked for that widget with a notice; oversized data exports stream asynchronously with completion notification.
Audit
DashboardExported with format, filters, period, row counts.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-06
Related
Section 15, DSH-BR-006
DSH-FR-013 KPI threshold alerting and subscriptions MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall evaluate published KPI thresholds on every scheduled computation, raise deduplicated alerts per KPI and scope node with severity (warning/critical), deliver them to subscribed roles/users via in-app and email channels, track acknowledgement and follow-up per the workflow in 11.4.7, and escalate unacknowledged critical alerts per 11.4.14.
Rationale
Alerting converts passive dashboards into an active management control loop (BUS-OBJ-006).
Actor
System; Quality Manager (thresholds, subscriptions)
Preconditions / Trigger
Thresholds and subscriptions configured; KPI computation.
Validation & Exceptions
Threshold changes are versioned and take effect from the next computation; an alert already open for a KPI+scope is updated, not duplicated; recovery events are recorded on the open alert.
Audit
AlertRaised/Acknowledged/Closed, ThresholdChanged with before/after.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-05
Related
DSH-FR-014, RPT-DSH-04
DSH-FR-014 Follow-up task creation from alerts MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow an authorized user to create a follow-up task directly from a KPI alert (assignee, due date, instructions, automatic link to the alert and its drill-down context) or to link the alert to an existing NCR/CAPA record; the task shall appear in the assignee's my-tasks widget and its completion shall be reflected on the alert timeline.
Rationale
Closes the measurement-to-action loop without leaving the analytics layer.
Actor
Quality Manager, scoped owners (create); any assignee (execute)
Preconditions / Trigger
Open alert in Acknowledged status.
Validation & Exceptions
Assignee must hold scope access to the alert's node; due date ≥ today; closure of the alert requires linked tasks completed or explicitly waived with reason.
Audit
TaskCreatedFromAlert/TaskCompleted with alert linkage.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSH-05
Related
NCR, CAPA

DSH-BR-001Every dashboard data request is authorized server-side against the viewer's roles and scope; widget visibility in the client is never the control.Backend authorization on each aggregate and drill query (IAM-FR-010).None.

DSH-BR-004Shared views render with the viewer's own permissions, scope, and language — never the owner's; sharing grants layout, not data.View definition stores no data; render pipeline resolves per viewer.None.
DSH-BR-005KPI definitions and threshold sets are versioned; a displayed historical value is always interpretable against the definition version in force at computation time.Version stamp stored with every computed value and alert.Definition corrections apply prospectively; recomputation of history requires Quality Manager approval and is audited.
DSH-BR-006Every export is watermarked with tenant, exporter, and timestamp, and contains only viewer-authorized data.Export service applies watermark and authorization at generation.None.
DSH-BR-007One open alert per KPI + scope node: subsequent breaches update the open alert; a new alert is created only after closure and references its predecessor.Dedupe key enforced at alert creation.None.
DSH-BR-008Closing an alert without corrective action requires a mandatory justification; closed alerts and their timelines are immutable.Closure validation; append-only alert timeline.Corrections recorded as annotations, never edits.
DSH-BR-009Threshold changes require Quality Manager approval and take effect from the next computation; they never retroactively change historical breach records.Draft-then-approve threshold workflow; version stamping.None.
DSH-BR-010Dashboard aggregates are decision-support displays; formal quality records remain in their owning modules — dashboard figures are never the system of record.Exports labeled "analytics snapshot"; no write-back from DSH to source data.None.
DSH-BR-011Widget data older than its configured freshness limit must be visibly flagged as stale wherever displayed or exported.Freshness timestamp compared at render and export time.None.

11.4.16 Integration Requirements
  • Internal — source modules: DSH reads aggregation inputs from all functional modules through their query services; it never writes to source data (DSH-BR-010).
  • Internal — IAM: every aggregate, drill, and export request is authorized via the IAM decision service (IAM-FR-010).
  • Outbound — notification gateway: alert and escalation delivery per 11.4.14. See INT-003 in Section 14.
  • Outbound — BI data export: scheduled, scope-filtered aggregate extracts for external BI platforms via the integration API where licensed, using service accounts (P-31). See INT-005.
  • Outbound — MRV: dashboard snapshots (RPT-DSH-01) attachable as management-review inputs (11.13).
Optional future scope: embedded self-service analytics builder and predictive KPI forecasting are excluded from this release and would be specified as a change to Section 16.

11.4.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-DSH-01 — Scope-trimmed dashboard content

  • Given a Department Manager scoped to Department A in Branch 1,
  • When the user opens the default dashboard and inspects the org filter,
  • Then only Branch 1 / Department A nodes are offered, every KPI and chart value equals the same query filtered to that scope, and a hand-crafted API request for Branch 2 aggregates returns an authorization denial.

AC-DSH-02 — KPI card status and freshness

  • Given a KPI with warning threshold 10 and critical threshold 20 (breach direction: above), current value 14, computed 12 minutes ago,
  • When the KPI card renders,
  • Then it shows value 14 in warning state (color plus icon/text, not color alone), the trend versus the comparison period, and the computation timestamp; if the freshness limit is exceeded the card carries a visible "stale" flag.

AC-DSH-03 — Drill-down consistency

  • Given a KPI card showing 27 overdue CAPAs for the selected scope and period,
  • When the viewer drills down,
  • Then the record list contains exactly the 27 composing records (or displays "N of 27 visible to you" when record-level restrictions apply), carries the same filters and period, and each row opens the source record subject to backend authorization.

AC-DSH-04 — My-tasks aggregation and delegation attribution

  • Given a user with 3 pending approvals in DOC, 2 CAPA actions, and 1 item received via an active delegation,
  • When the my-tasks widget renders,
  • Then all 6 items appear sorted by due date with overdue items first, the delegated item is labeled "acting for [delegator]", and each item opens its source record directly.

AC-DSH-05 — Breach-to-task loop

  • Given a published critical threshold and a scheduled computation producing a breaching value,
  • When the computation completes,
  • Then exactly one alert exists for that KPI and scope node, subscribers are notified within 15 minutes, the Quality Manager can acknowledge, drill down, and create a follow-up task that appears in the assignee's my-tasks widget, and the alert timeline records breach, acknowledgement, task, and closure events immutably.

AC-DSH-06 — Shared view renders with viewer permissions; export is watermarked

  • Given a Quality Director's view shared to Department Managers,
  • When a Department Manager opens the shared view and exports it to PDF,
  • Then every widget shows only that manager's scoped data (not the owner's), and the PDF header carries tenant, exporter identity, timestamp, active filters, and period, with the export recorded in the audit log.

AC-DSH-07 — Widget failure isolation

  • Given a dashboard of six widgets where one source module query fails,
  • When the dashboard renders,
  • Then the failing widget shows an error state with retry control and support reference id, the remaining five widgets render normally, and the error state is visually distinct from a genuine zero/empty result.

11.5 Document & SOP Control DOC

The Document & SOP Control module is the controlled-document backbone of NT.QMS. It governs the complete lifecycle of quality documents — policies, manuals, standard operating procedures (SOPs), work instructions, forms, specifications and controlled external documents — from drafting through review, electronically signed approval, publication, employee acknowledgement, periodic review, revision and final obsolescence. Every other module consumes controlled documents (audit checklists, CAPA procedures, training material, calibration instructions); this module is therefore the flagship module of the platform and the primary vehicle for BUS-OBJ-003 (reduce uncontrolled documents).

11.5.1 Module Overview
Module nameDocument & SOP Control
Module codeDOC
PurposeProvide a single controlled repository and workflow engine for all quality documents so that only reviewed, approved and current documents are available at the point of use, with full revision history and evidence of approval, distribution, acknowledgement and training.
Business valueEliminates uncontrolled paper and shared-drive copies; enforces approval and segregation of duties; produces inspection-ready evidence of document control (approval signatures, distribution, acknowledgement, periodic review); reduces time to publish a revision from weeks to days.
ScopeDocument taxonomy and registers; automatic numbering; controlled templates; drafting with check-out/check-in and co-authoring; review routes; sequential/parallel approvals with electronic signatures (configurable 21 CFR Part 11 mode); effective dating and automatic publication; controlled distribution; read-and-acknowledge; training assignment on publication; printed-copy control with watermarks; periodic review; revision, supersede, withdrawal and obsolescence; controlled external documents; version comparison; confidentiality controls; change impact assessment; related-records linkage.
Out of scopeFull WYSIWYG document authoring (content is authored in Office tools and uploaded/checked in); records management for non-document quality records (handled by each owning module); machine translation of document content; hard-copy physical archive management (register only).
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §7.5 (Documented information), ISO/IEC 17025:2017 §8.2–8.3, ISO 15189 (where applicable), ISO 13485 §4.2.3–4.2.4 (where applicable), 21 CFR Part 11 (when enabled per tenant — see Section 19), GxP good documentation practice.
Related modulesTRN (11.10) — training assignment on publication; IAM (11.3) — roles, delegation, e-signature identity; CAPA (11.7) — document changes as CAPA actions; NCR (11.6) — procedure references on nonconformances; AUD (11.9) — audit criteria documents; RSK (11.12) — change impact assessment inputs; MRV (11.13) — document-control KPIs.
Primary personasP-06 Document Controller, P-08 Process Owner, P-09 Record Owner (document owner), P-10 Reviewer, P-11 Approver, P-05 Quality Manager, P-20 Employee / Trainee; supporting: P-04 Quality Director, P-07 Department Manager, P-28 Read-Only User, P-29 External Auditor.

11.5.2 Business Problem

Today, quality documents are typically authored in Word, circulated for review by e-mail, signed on printed cover pages and stored on shared drives or in binders. The consequences are systematic: multiple conflicting versions exist at points of use; there is no reliable evidence of who reviewed or approved a given revision; superseded copies remain in circulation; and periodic review dates are tracked (if at all) in spreadsheets that silently go stale. During customer and certification audits, retrieving the approval history of a single SOP can take hours, and findings for "uncontrolled documents in use" are among the most frequent audit observations.

Distribution and awareness are equally weak: when a procedure changes, there is no dependable mechanism to confirm that every affected employee has read the new revision or been retrained, and no escalation when they have not. Printed working copies carry no marking that distinguishes them from controlled originals, so obsolete printouts survive on workshop walls for years.

The DOC module replaces this with a single controlled repository in which the current approved version is the only version visible at the point of use, every approval is an attributable electronic signature, every distribution and acknowledgement is recorded, and every periodic review is scheduled, reminded and escalated automatically.

11.5.3 Business Objectives
  • BUS-OBJ-001 — Standardize processes: one controlled workflow for all document types across all sites.
  • BUS-OBJ-002 — Digitize records: electronic drafts, reviews, signatures and distribution replace paper routing slips.
  • BUS-OBJ-003 — Reduce uncontrolled documents: current-version-only publication, watermarked printouts, automatic supersede.
  • BUS-OBJ-004 — Enforce approvals and segregation of duties: configurable routes, sequence enforcement, author-cannot-approve rule.
  • BUS-OBJ-005 — Traceability: complete revision history, version comparison and related-records linkage.
  • BUS-OBJ-006 — Overdue visibility: dashboards and escalations for overdue reviews, approvals, acknowledgements and periodic reviews.
  • BUS-OBJ-008 — Immutable audit trails on every document-control action.
  • BUS-OBJ-010 — Audit readiness: inspection-ready registers and approval evidence on demand.
  • BUS-OBJ-011 — Training & competency: automatic training assignment when a document with training impact becomes effective.
  • BUS-OBJ-016 — Configurable workflows: review/approval routes, numbering schemes and Part 11 mode are tenant-configurable without code change.

11.5.5 Preconditions
  • Tenant and organization structure configured (Section 11.2); departments and sites exist for ownership and distribution scoping.
  • Document types, categories, numbering schemes and at least one approved template are configured per tenant.
  • Review/approval route templates defined, or route-on-the-fly permission granted to the Document Controller.
  • Users provisioned with DOC roles via IAM; approvers have signature credentials enrolled; Part 11 mode setting (on/off) has been decided per tenant (Section 19).
  • Notification channels (in-app, e-mail) operational per Section 14.
  • Retention classes for document categories configured per Section 21.

11.5.6 Trigger Events
  • A new process, product, regulation or standard requires a new controlled document.
  • A CAPA action (Section 11.7), audit finding (Section 11.9) or NCR disposition (Section 11.6) mandates creation or revision of a document.
  • Periodic review date reached (system-scheduled trigger).
  • Owner-initiated revision (process change, organizational change, error correction).
  • Publication of a new revision of a controlled external document (standard, regulation, client specification).
  • Management decision to withdraw or obsolete a document.
  • Migration intake of legacy documents (Section 22).

11.5.8 Workflow Diagram

11.5.9 Record Lifecycle

Controlled documents progress through the following statuses. Only transitions defined in the state-transition table are permitted; every transition is recorded in the audit trail with actor, timestamp, and (where required) reason.

  • Draft — under authoring/co-authoring; editable by author and contributors.
  • Submitted — sent into the review/approval route; locked against content edits.
  • Under Review — with reviewers/approvers at the current route step.
  • Returned for Correction — sent back to the author with mandatory comments.
  • Approved — all approvals (and signatures, if configured) obtained; awaiting effective date.
  • Effective / Active — the single current controlled version at points of use.
  • Superseded — replaced by a newer effective version; retained, read-only, watermarked.
  • Obsolete / Withdrawn — no longer valid for use; retained for the retention period.
  • Cancelled — a draft/submitted version abandoned before becoming effective.
  • Archived — moved to long-term retention storage after the active retention window.

11.5.11 Functional Requirements
DOC-FR-001 Controlled document creation from approved templates MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow authorized users to create a controlled document by selecting a document category and an approved template, automatically reserving a document number from the applicable numbering scheme and pre-populating mandatory metadata.
Rationale
Standardizes structure and guarantees controlled numbering from creation.
Actor
Document Controller; authorized author
Preconditions / Trigger
Category, template, and numbering scheme configured (TEN); user has Create permission for the category and org scope.
Validation & Exceptions
Category and template must be active; if no template exists the action is blocked with guidance; reserved numbers not consumed on cancellation follow DOC-BR-002.
Audit
DocumentCreated with template, number, actor, timestamp.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DOC-01
Related
DOC-BR-001, TEN numbering, RPT-DOC-02
DOC-FR-002 Co-authoring with check-out / check-in control ShouldCore
Requirement
The system shall permit multiple contributors on a draft while preventing conflicting edits through check-out/check-in (exclusive edit lock) or equivalent optimistic concurrency, preserving a per-save change history within the draft.
Rationale
Enables collaboration without lost updates.
Actor
Author; contributors
Preconditions / Trigger
Document in Draft; user has Edit permission.
Validation & Exceptions
A second concurrent editor is offered read-only or wait; stale check-in is rejected with a concurrency error (GEN-TC-003).
Audit
CheckedOut / CheckedIn with actor and timestamp.

Related

The system shall route a submitted document through the approval route configured for its category and org unit, supporting sequential steps, parallel steps, and conditional steps, and shall enforce the defined order — an approver at a later step cannot act before earlier steps complete.
Rationale
Enforces governance and approval sequence (BUS-OBJ-004).
Actor
Reviewer; Approver; system
Preconditions / Trigger
Document submitted; route resolvable to active users.

The system shall restrict visibility and actions on each document according to its confidentiality classification and the user's permissions and organizational scope, excluding restricted documents (including their titles) from search results for unauthorized users.

Protects confidential quality information (BUS-OBJ-015).

System
Preconditions / Trigger
Any access or search request.
Validation & Exceptions
Unauthorized direct access is denied and security-logged; search results are permission-trimmed (Section 17).
Audit
AccessDenied with actor, document, reason.

11.5.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-DOC-01 — Controlled creation from template

  • Given an authorized author and an active SOP template with a numbering scheme,
  • When the author creates a new SOP,
  • Then the system reserves the next scheme number, applies the template, sets status Draft, and records DocumentCreated.

AC-DOC-03 — Approval sequence enforced

  • Given a document in Under Review with a two-step sequential route,
  • When the second approver attempts to approve before the first,
  • Then the action is rejected with a sequence-violation message and the attempt is audited.

AC-DOC-04 — Signed approval

  • Given signed approval is enabled for the category,
  • When the approver approves and enters valid credentials,
  • Then an electronic signature with meaning, reason, and UTC timestamp is bound to the version and shown on the record and printouts.

AC-DOC-05 — Single effective version

  • Given version 2.0 is Approved with today's effective date and version 1.0 is Effective,
  • When the publication job runs,
  • Then version 2.0 becomes Effective, version 1.0 becomes Superseded, and only one effective version exists.

AC-DOC-06 — Acknowledgement tracking

  • Given a published training-relevant SOP distributed to a department,
  • When the acknowledgement due date approaches with recipients outstanding,
  • Then reminders are sent and, if still outstanding, the recipients' manager is escalated, all audited.

AC-DOC-08 — Watermarked print

  • Given a user with Print permission,
  • When they export the effective document to PDF,
  • Then every page bears "UNCONTROLLED WHEN PRINTED" with number, version, date/time, and user, and DocumentPrinted is recorded.

AC-DOC-14 — Confidential search trimming

  • Given a Restricted document and a user without access,
  • When the user searches for its title,
  • Then no result (including the title) is returned, and any direct access attempt is denied and security-logged.
Note: Acceptance criteria AC-DOC-02, AC-DOC-07, AC-DOC-09 through AC-DOC-13 follow the same Given/When/Then structure for their respective requirements and are maintained in the test-case repository referenced by the RTM (Section 24).

11.6 Nonconformance Management NCR

11.6.1 Module Overview
Module nameNonconformance Management
Module codeNCR
PurposeCapture, classify, contain, investigate, disposition and close nonconformances (NCs) from any source, with full traceability from detection to closure and to any resulting CAPA.
Business valueReplaces paper/spreadsheet NC logs with a controlled, auditable process; enforces containment and root-cause discipline; provides recurrence and trend visibility that drives systemic improvement.
ScopeNC recording from internal detection, audit findings, complaints, supplier issues and equipment out-of-tolerance events; severity classification; immediate correction and containment; impact assessment; investigation and root-cause analysis; risk linkage; CAPA initiation decision; approval, closure, reopening; recurrence monitoring and trend analysis.
Out of scopeExecution of the CAPA action plan (see 11.7 CAPA); customer complaint intake and customer communication (see 11.8 CMP); supplier scorecard management; MRB/inventory disposition transactions in ERP (integration only, see Section 14).
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §8.7 (control of nonconforming outputs), §10.2 (nonconformity and corrective action); ISO/IEC 17025:2017 §7.10; ISO 13485 §8.3 (where applicable); 21 CFR Part 11 (e-signatures, where enabled).
Related modulesCAPA (11.7), Complaints (11.8), Audits (11.9), Equipment & Calibration (11.11), Risk (11.12), Dashboards (11.4), Management Review (11.13).
Primary personasP-20 Employee (initiator), P-05 Quality Manager, P-09 Record Owner (NCR owner/investigator), P-11 Approver, P-12 CAPA Coordinator, P-04 Quality Director.

11.6.2 Business Problem

Nonconformances are today recorded inconsistently across paper forms, e-mails and departmental spreadsheets. Severity is assigned subjectively, containment actions are frequently undocumented, and there is no reliable link between a nonconformance, the affected products or services, the root-cause analysis and any corrective action taken. As a result, the organization cannot demonstrate to auditors that nonconforming outputs were controlled, and repeated problems are discovered only anecdotally.

Because NC records are fragmented, management has no trustworthy view of open items, overdue investigations or recurring failure categories. The lack of enforced workflow means records are closed without root-cause analysis or without a documented decision on whether a CAPA is required, weakening the entire improvement loop required by ISO 9001:2015 §10.2.

11.6.3 Business Objectives
  • Standardize a single controlled NC process across all sites and departments (BUS-OBJ-001, BUS-OBJ-016).
  • Digitize NC records with immutable audit trails and controlled attachments (BUS-OBJ-002, BUS-OBJ-008).
  • Enforce approvals, segregation of duties and closure prerequisites (BUS-OBJ-004).
  • Provide end-to-end traceability from NC source to CAPA and management review (BUS-OBJ-005, BUS-OBJ-009).
  • Give managers real-time visibility of open, overdue and recurring NCs (BUS-OBJ-006, BUS-OBJ-013).
  • Support inspection and certification audits with retrievable, complete NC evidence (BUS-OBJ-007, BUS-OBJ-010).

11.6.4 Actors & Personas
RolePersonasResponsibility in this module
Initiator (primary)P-20 Employee, P-15 Internal Auditor, P-14 Complaint Coordinator, P-21/P-22 Equipment/Calibration CoordinatorDetect and report the nonconformance with initial evidence.
Triage / classifierP-05 Quality ManagerValidate the report, classify category, set severity, assign the NCR owner.
NCR owner / investigator (primary)P-09 Record Owner, P-08 Process OwnerExecute containment, impact assessment, investigation and root-cause analysis; propose disposition and CAPA decision.
ApproverP-11 Approver, P-05 Quality Manager, P-04 Quality Director (critical NCs)Approve disposition, CAPA decision and closure; approve reopening.
SupportingP-12 CAPA Coordinator, P-24 Risk Manager, P-25 Supplier Quality ManagerReceive CAPA initiation; maintain risk linkage; handle supplier-sourced NCs.
AdministratorP-03 Organization AdministratorConfigure categories, severity matrix, RCA methods, numbering, routes, SLAs.
Read-only / externalP-28 Read-Only User, P-27 Executive, P-29 External Auditor (time-boxed scoped access)View records, trends and reports within granted scope.

11.6.5 Preconditions
  • Tenant and organization structure configured (11.2); users provisioned with NCR roles (11.3).
  • NC category catalog, severity matrix (critical/major/minor definitions) and source list configured and active.
  • At least one root-cause analysis method (5-Why, fishbone) enabled for the tenant.
  • Approval route(s) for disposition/closure configured, including the critical-NC route.
  • Notification templates and escalation SLAs for NCR events configured (11.6.14).
  • Where 21 CFR Part 11 mode is enabled: e-signature policy configured (Section 19).

11.6.6 Trigger Events
  • Internal detection during production, service delivery, inspection or testing (manual entry).
  • Audit finding classified as nonconformity is converted to an NCR from 11.9 Audit Management.
  • Complaint investigation confirms a nonconforming output — NCR created from 11.8 Complaint Management.
  • Supplier-delivered material or service found nonconforming at receipt or in use.
  • Equipment found out of tolerance at calibration — NCR auto-proposed from 11.11 Equipment & Calibration covering potentially affected results/products.
  • Reopening of a previously closed NCR after recurrence or failed verification.

11.6.11 Functional Requirements
NCR-FR-001 Multi-source nonconformance recording with source linkage MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow creation of an NCR from direct entry (internal detection) and from source modules — audit finding (11.9), complaint (11.8), supplier issue, equipment out-of-tolerance event (11.11) — automatically storing an immutable bidirectional link to the source record.
Rationale
End-to-end traceability from detection channel to resolution.
Actor
Initiator; source-module users; System
Preconditions / Trigger
Source catalogs configured; source record exists for module-initiated NCRs.
Validation & Exceptions
Source record must belong to the same tenant; broken links prevented by referential integrity; source field locked after submission (QM may correct with audit reason).
Audit
Creation event with source type, source record id, creator, timestamp.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-01
Related
NCR-BR-001, RPT-NCR-06
NCR-FR-002 Tenant-unique automatic numbering MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall assign each NCR a tenant-unique number on creation using a tenant-configurable mask (e.g. NCR-{YYYY}-{SEQ5}); numbers shall never be reused, including for cancelled records.
Rationale
Unambiguous referencing in audits, reports and external correspondence.
Actor
System
Preconditions / Trigger
Numbering mask configured; NCR saved for the first time.
Validation & Exceptions
Sequence generation must be concurrency-safe; gaps caused by aborted transactions are tolerated and never backfilled.
Audit
Number assignment logged with mask version used.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-01
Related
NCR-BR-013
NCR-FR-003 Classification and severity with configurable severity matrix MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall require the Quality Manager to classify each submitted NCR with a category from the tenant catalog and a severity of Critical, Major or Minor, and shall display the tenant-configured severity matrix guidance during classification. Severity shall drive approval routing, containment obligations and SLA timers.
Rationale
Consistent, defensible prioritization and effort proportional to risk.
Actor
Quality Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
NCR in Submitted status; severity matrix configured.
Validation & Exceptions
Severity change after classification requires reason and is audited; downgrade of a Critical NCR requires Quality Director approval.
Audit
Severity set/changed with before/after values and reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-02
Related
NCR-BR-002, RPT-NCR-03
NCR-FR-004 Immediate correction and containment recording MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide a structured containment log (action, performer, date/time, scope such as segregated quantity or stopped process) and shall block progression to approval for Critical and Major NCRs until at least one containment action is recorded or a containment waiver is co-signed by the Quality Manager.
Rationale
ISO 9001 §8.7 requires nonconforming outputs to be controlled before disposition.
Actor
NCR Owner; Quality Manager (waiver)
Preconditions / Trigger
NCR classified (Under Review).
Validation & Exceptions
Waiver requires justification text and QM identity distinct from owner.
Audit
Each containment entry and waiver logged immutably.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-03
Related
NCR-BR-003
NCR-FR-005 Product / service impact assessment MustCore
Requirement
The system shall capture a structured impact assessment identifying affected products/services, lots/batches or service instances, quantities, whether affected output was already delivered, affected customers, and whether regulatory or customer notification is required, and shall flag the record when delivered product is affected.
Rationale
Determines containment scope, recall/notification needs and disposition options.
Actor
NCR Owner
Preconditions / Trigger
Containment step reached.
Validation & Exceptions
At least one impact dimension must be completed before approval; "impact unknown" allowed only with a mandatory review date.
Audit
Impact assessment saved/changed with before/after snapshot.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-03
Related
NCR-BR-005, CMP module
NCR-FR-006 Investigation and root-cause analysis with configurable methods MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall provide structured root-cause analysis templates for at least 5-Why and fishbone (Ishikawa) methods, tenant-configurable per severity (which methods are available and whether RCA is mandatory), storing the analysis as structured data (not free text only) with identified root cause(s) and contributing factors.
Rationale
Structured RCA enables recurrence analytics and demonstrates method discipline to auditors.
Actor
NCR Owner
Preconditions / Trigger
Impact assessment recorded.
Validation & Exceptions
RCA mandatory for Critical/Major; a Minor NCR may skip RCA only via QM-approved waiver with reason.
Audit
RCA method selection, completion and edits logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-04
Related
NCR-BR-007, CAPA-FR-003
NCR-FR-007 Risk assessment linkage ShouldCore
Requirement
The system shall allow linking an NCR to one or more risk register entries (11.12) or creating a new risk from the NCR context, and shall require a risk link or a documented "no risk impact" statement for Critical NCRs before approval.
Rationale
Feeds operational failures back into risk-based thinking (ISO 9001 §6.1).
Actor
NCR Owner; Risk Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
RCA completed; Risk module enabled for tenant.
Validation & Exceptions
Cross-tenant risk links rejected; if Risk module is disabled the step is skipped and the skip is logged.
Audit
Risk link created/removed with actor and reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-04
Related
NCR-BR-006
NCR-FR-008 CAPA initiation decision with enforced justification MustCore
Requirement
The system shall require an explicit CAPA decision ("CAPA required" or "CAPA not required") with mandatory justification before an NCR can be submitted for approval. When "CAPA required" is selected, the system shall create a linked CAPA record pre-populated with the NCR context (problem summary, root cause, source link) in 11.7 CAPA Management.
Rationale
Closes the ISO 9001 §10.2 loop; prevents silent closure of systemic problems.
Actor
NCR Owner; System; CAPA Coordinator (recipient)
Preconditions / Trigger
Disposition step; RCA recorded or waived.
Validation & Exceptions
"Not required" for Critical NCRs additionally requires Quality Director endorsement at approval; CAPA creation failure blocks submission and alerts the CAPA Coordinator.
Audit
Decision, justification, decider, timestamp and created CAPA id logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-05
Related
NCR-BR-008, CAPA-FR-001
NCR-FR-009 Severity-driven approval workflow MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall route the completed NCR (disposition + CAPA decision) through a tenant-configurable approval route selected by severity — at minimum Quality Manager approval for Minor/Major and Quality Director approval for Critical — capturing approve/return decisions with comments and, where Part 11 mode is enabled, an electronic signature per Section 19.
Rationale
Proportionate governance and regulatory signature compliance.
Actor
Approver(s)
Preconditions / Trigger
Owner submits for approval.
Validation & Exceptions
Approver must differ from initiator and owner (SoD); out-of-sequence approval rejected; return requires comments.
Audit
Each decision with route step, identity, timestamp, signature manifest.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-06
Related
NCR-BR-004, NCR-BR-011
NCR-FR-010 Closure with enforced checklist MustCore
Requirement
The system shall permit closure only when all checklist conditions are satisfied: containment recorded or waived, impact assessment complete, RCA complete or waived, disposition approved and execution evidence attached, and CAPA decision recorded (with linked CAPA created where required). The failed condition(s) shall be displayed when closure is blocked.
Rationale
Prevents premature closure — a recurrent external-audit finding.
Actor
Quality Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
NCR Approved.
Validation & Exceptions
Closure does not require the linked CAPA to be closed — the CAPA lifecycle continues independently in 11.7 and remains traceable.
Audit
Closure with checklist snapshot, closer, timestamp.

AC-NCR-05
Related

NCR-FR-011 Controlled reopening MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow reopening a Closed NCR only by the Quality Manager (plus Quality Director approval for Critical NCRs) with a mandatory documented reason from a configurable reason list (recurrence, failed CAPA effectiveness, audit challenge, new evidence). Reopening shall create a new record revision preserving the closed revision read-only.
Rationale
Data integrity: closed evidence must remain intact while allowing corrective reprocessing.
Actor
Quality Manager; Quality Director
Preconditions / Trigger
NCR Closed and not yet archived under a retention lock.
Validation & Exceptions
Reopen attempts on Archived records are denied with guidance to create a new NCR referencing the archived one.
Audit
Reopen event with reason, approvals, prior revision id.
Acceptance criteria
AC-NCR-07
Related
NCR-BR-010
NCR-FR-012 Recurrence monitoring ShouldConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall automatically flag potential recurrence when a new NCR matches a closed NCR on configurable dimensions (category, process, product/service, supplier) within a configurable window (default 12 months — proposed target, pending business confirmation), notify the Quality Manager, and display the recurrence chain on both records.
Rationale
Recurrence is the primary signal that prior correction/CAPA was ineffective.
Actor
System; Quality Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
Recurrence rule enabled; new NCR classified.
Validation & Exceptions
QM may dismiss a false-positive flag with reason (audited); a confirmed recurrence prompts CAPA escalation review.
Audit
Flag raised/dismissed/confirmed with matching criteria snapshot.

AC-NCR-07
Related
RPT-NCR-05, CAPA-FR-010
NCR-FR-013 Trend analysis and Pareto reporting ShouldCore
Requirement
The system shall provide trend views of NCR volume, severity mix, closure cycle time and top categories (Pareto) filterable by period, site, department, process, source and supplier, exportable for management review (11.13) and surfaced on dashboards (Section 16).
Rationale
Converts NC data into improvement decisions and management-review input.
Actor
Quality Manager; Executive Management User
Preconditions / Trigger
Historical NCR data present.
Validation & Exceptions
Views respect tenant and department-level visibility scopes.
Audit
Report generation/export logged per Section 15.

AC-NCR-08
Related
RPT-NCR-03, RPT-NCR-04
NCR-FR-014 Evidence attachments MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support attaching evidence files (images, PDF, office documents) to the NCR and to individual containment/disposition entries, enforcing tenant-configured allowed types and maximum size, virus scanning on upload, and immutable storage of attachment versions.
Rationale
Objective evidence is required for audits and disposition justification.
Actor
Initiator; NCR Owner
Preconditions / Trigger
Record editable by the acting user.
Validation & Exceptions
Rejected uploads (type/size/scan) reported with reason; deletion of attachments is soft (hidden, retained, audited) — never physical while the record is retained.
Audit
Upload/replace/hide events with file hash.

11.6.16 Integration Requirements
  • Inbound: NCR creation from Audit findings (11.9), Complaints (11.8) and Equipment out-of-tolerance events (11.11) via internal module APIs; optional creation from ERP quality inspection results (INT-002, see Section 14).
  • Outbound: CAPA shell creation into 11.7; risk links into 11.12; KPI feeds to Dashboards (11.4) and Management Review data packs (11.13); e-mail/notification gateway (INT-001).
  • Identity: All actors resolved through IAM (11.3); no local user store.
  • All integration calls carry tenant context from trusted claims; cross-tenant payloads are rejected and security-logged.

11.6.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-NCR-01 — Source linkage and numbering on creation from a module

  • Given an audit finding classified as a nonconformity in module 11.9,
  • When the auditor converts it to an NCR,
  • Then the system creates a Draft NCR with a tenant-unique number per the configured mask, source = "Audit finding", an immutable link to the finding, and the finding shows a reciprocal link to the NCR.

AC-NCR-02 — Severity is mandatory and drives routing

  • Given a Submitted NCR being triaged,
  • When the Quality Manager attempts to accept it without selecting a severity,
  • Then the system blocks acceptance with a validation message, and after severity "Critical" is selected the approval route is set to the Quality Director route and the critical alert is dispatched.

AC-NCR-03 — Containment gate for a Major NCR

  • Given a Major NCR with no containment entry and no containment waiver,
  • When the owner submits it for approval,
  • Then the system rejects the submission, lists "containment action required" as the blocking condition, and records the blocked attempt in the audit trail.

AC-NCR-04 — Structured RCA capture

  • Given a Critical NCR at the investigation step with 5-Why and fishbone enabled for the tenant,
  • When the owner completes a 5-Why analysis,
  • Then the system stores each "why" level as structured data, requires at least one identified root cause, and prevents approval submission if the RCA is absent.

AC-NCR-05 — CAPA decision enforced before approval and closure

  • Given an NCR with disposition proposed but no CAPA decision recorded,
  • When the owner submits for approval,
  • Then the submission is blocked; and when "CAPA required" is later selected, then a linked CAPA record is created in 11.7 pre-populated with the NCR problem summary and root cause, and the CAPA Coordinator is notified.

AC-NCR-06 — Segregation of duties at approval

  • Given an NCR whose initiator is also configured as an approver on the selected route,
  • When that user attempts to approve the NCR,
  • Then the system rejects the decision with an SoD violation message, routes to the alternate approver, and logs the attempt.

AC-NCR-07 — Reopening creates a new revision

  • Given a Closed Major NCR flagged as recurring,
  • When the Quality Manager reopens it with reason "recurrence",
  • Then the system creates revision 2 in status Under Review, preserves revision 1 read-only, links the recurrence chain, and records the reopen event with reason and actor.

AC-NCR-08 — Trend report scoping

  • Given a Department Manager whose visibility scope is Department A,
  • When they run the Severity & Volume Trend report,
  • Then the report contains only Department A records, and the export is watermarked and logged with the user identity and filter set.
