11.7 CAPA Management CAPA

11.7.1 Module Overview
Module nameCorrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Management
Module codeCAPA
PurposeManage the full lifecycle of corrective and preventive actions — from initiation, root-cause analysis, and action planning through implementation, effectiveness verification, and closure — with enforced ownership, due dates, escalation, and evidence.
Business valueTurns problems into verified, sustained improvements; prevents recurrence; provides objective evidence of corrective action for audits and inspections (BUS-OBJ-009).
ScopeCAPA records; problem statements; root-cause analysis; multi-action plans with owners and dates; evidence; extension requests; effectiveness verification; closure; reopening; overdue escalation.
Out of scopeThe originating investigation of a nonconformance (owned by NCR); complaint handling (CMP); audit finding capture (AUD). CAPA links to these as sources.
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §10.2 (nonconformity & corrective action); ISO/IEC 17025:2017 §8.7; 21 CFR Part 11 (where signed).
Related modulesNCR, CMP, AUD, RSK, MRV, DOC, TRN
Primary personasP-12 CAPA Coordinator, P-13 CAPA Action Owner, P-05 Quality Manager, P-11 Approver, P-04 Quality Director
ClassificationCore Must

11.7.2 Business Problem

In manual quality systems, corrective actions are recorded on forms or in meeting minutes but not reliably tracked to completion. Action owners forget due dates, plans are implemented without confirming they addressed the true root cause, and effectiveness is rarely verified. As a result the same problems recur, and auditors find open or ineffective CAPAs during inspections. There is no consolidated view of overdue actions or CAPA performance across the organization.

NT.QMS makes the CAPA a controlled, workflow-driven record: it forces a problem statement and root-cause analysis before actions are approved, tracks each action owner and due date with reminders and escalation, requires objective evidence, and blocks closure until an independent verifier confirms effectiveness against predefined criteria.

11.7.3 Business Objectives
  • Ensure every significant issue has a root-cause-based action plan (BUS-OBJ-009).
  • Improve on-time closure of CAPA actions and eliminate silent overdue actions (BUS-OBJ-006).
  • Verify effectiveness before closure and prevent recurrence (BUS-OBJ-009).
  • Provide full traceability from source record to closed, verified CAPA (BUS-OBJ-005).
  • Supply CAPA performance data to management review (BUS-OBJ-013).

11.7.4 Actors & Personas
CategoryPersonasRole in module
Primary actorsP-12 CAPA Coordinator, P-13 CAPA Action OwnerInitiate/coordinate CAPAs; execute assigned actions with evidence
Supporting actorsP-08 Process Owner, P-09 Record Owner, P-15 Internal AuditorProvide investigation input; raise CAPA from source records
ApproversP-05 Quality Manager, P-11 ApproverApprove action plan and closure
Reviewers / verifiersIndependent Verifier (P-05/assigned), P-10 ReviewerVerify effectiveness independently of implementers
AdministratorsP-02 Tenant Admin, P-04 Quality DirectorConfigure root-cause methods, effectiveness criteria, escalation
Read-onlyP-27 Executive, P-28 Read-Only, P-29 External AuditorView CAPA status and evidence (scoped)

11.7.5 Preconditions
  • Root-cause methods, effectiveness-criteria templates, and escalation rules are configured for the tenant.
  • A source record exists (nonconformance, complaint, audit finding, risk, or management-review decision) or a standalone preventive-action justification is provided.
  • The initiating user has Create permission for CAPA in the relevant organizational scope.

11.7.6 Trigger Events
  • A nonconformance meets the criteria for CAPA initiation (NCR).
  • A complaint investigation concludes systematic action is required (CMP).
  • An audit finding (major/minor nonconformity) requires corrective action (AUD).
  • A risk mitigation action or management-review decision creates a CAPA (RSK, MRV).
  • A CAPA action reaches its due date, or a CAPA effectiveness-review date is reached.
  • An effectiveness verification fails, requiring a successor CAPA.

  • Cancelled — abandoned before approval, with reason.
  • Archived — moved to long-term retention.

11.7.11 Functional Requirements
CAPA-FR-001 CAPA initiation from a source record MustCore

The system shall allow a CAPA to be initiated from a nonconformance, complaint, audit finding, risk, or management-review decision, automatically linking the source, copying relevant context, and assigning a unique CAPA number; standalone preventive CAPAs shall require a documented justification.

Guarantees traceability from problem to action (BUS-OBJ-005).

The system shall provide configurable root-cause methods (e.g. 5-Why, fishbone/Ishikawa) and require at least one documented root cause, with method and supporting evidence, before an action plan can be approved.

Prevents actions that treat symptoms rather than causes.

Rationale
Reflects that most CAPAs require several coordinated actions.

The system shall detect actions approaching or past their due date, send reminders, and escalate overdue actions through a configurable chain (owner → owner's manager → Quality Manager → Quality Director), surfacing overdue CAPAs on dashboards within one working day.

CAPA-FR-008 Effectiveness verification against predefined criteria MustCore
Requirement
The system shall require effectiveness verification against criteria defined in the plan, performed by a verifier independent of the implementers, at or after a scheduled effectiveness-review date, recording the verdict and supporting evidence.
Rationale
Confirms the CAPA actually resolved the root cause (BUS-OBJ-009).
Actor
Independent Verifier
Preconditions / Trigger
Implementation complete; criteria defined; review date reached.
Validation & Exceptions
Verifier ≠ implementer enforced (CAPA-BR-008); premature verification blocked until review date.
Audit
EffectivenessVerified with verdict.
Acceptance criteria
AC-CAPA-08
Related
RPT-CAPA-03
CAPA-FR-009 Ineffective-CAPA handling MustCore
Requirement
Where effectiveness verification fails, the system shall prevent closure, mark the CAPA ineffective, and require either a revised action plan or a linked successor CAPA, optionally escalating to management review.
Rationale
Prevents closing problems that are not actually solved.
Actor
Quality Manager; Coordinator
Preconditions / Trigger
Effectiveness verdict = ineffective.
Validation & Exceptions
Closure blocked while ineffective (CAPA-BR-009); successor CAPA inherits source linkage.
Audit
CapaIneffective; SuccessorLinked.

The system shall permit closure only when effectiveness is confirmed and all actions are complete, requiring Quality Manager approval and, where configured, an electronic signature per Section 19.

Ensures disciplined, evidenced closure.

Quality Manager

Status Effective.

11.7.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-CAPA-01 — Initiation from source

  • Given a nonconformance eligible for CAPA,
  • When the coordinator initiates a CAPA from it,
  • Then the CAPA is created with the source linked, a unique number, status Draft, and CapaInitiated is audited.

AC-CAPA-04 — SoD on plan approval

  • Given a CAPA plan authored solely by user A with SoD enabled,
  • When user A attempts to approve the plan,
  • Then the approval is blocked with an SoD message and the attempt is audited.

AC-CAPA-05 — Evidence required

  • Given an assigned action requiring evidence,
  • When the owner marks it complete without attaching evidence,
  • Then completion is blocked and the owner is prompted to attach evidence.

AC-CAPA-06 — Overdue escalation

  • Given an action past its due date,
  • When the escalation schedule runs,
  • Then the owner's manager is notified, the CAPA appears on the overdue dashboard within one working day, and Escalated is audited.

AC-CAPA-08 — Independent effectiveness verification

  • Given a CAPA Pending Verification with defined effectiveness criteria,
  • When a verifier who is not an implementer records the result at/after the review date,
  • Then the verdict and evidence are stored and EffectivenessVerified is audited.

AC-CAPA-09 — Ineffective blocks closure

  • Given a CAPA verified ineffective,
  • When the QM attempts to close it,
  • Then closure is blocked until a revised plan or successor CAPA is linked.

AC-CAPA-10 — Controlled closure

  • Given a CAPA marked Effective with all actions complete and signed closure configured,
  • When the QM closes it and applies a valid signature,
  • Then status becomes Closed with the signature bound and CapaClosed audited.
Note: AC-CAPA-02, AC-CAPA-03, AC-CAPA-07, AC-CAPA-11, AC-CAPA-12 follow the same Given/When/Then structure for their requirements and are maintained in the test repository (RTM, Section 24).

11.8 Complaint Management CMP

11.8.1 Module Overview
Module nameComplaint Management
Module codeCMP
PurposeProvide a controlled, end-to-end process for receiving, registering, classifying, investigating, responding to, and closing customer complaints, with regulatory-reportability assessment and full traceability to corrective action.
Business valueEnsures no complaint is lost or handled informally, enforces acknowledgement and response SLAs, protects customer personal data, supports regulatory reporting obligations, and converts complaint data into trend intelligence that drives improvement.
ScopeComplaint intake (portal, email, manually logged phone calls), customer and product/service detail capture, severity classification, regulatory-reportability assessment, acknowledgement, investigation, linkage to NCR/CAPA, response drafting and approval, resolution, closure, customer notification, and trend analysis.
Out of scopeWarranty/financial claims settlement, CRM sales-pipeline management, field-service dispatch and spare-parts logistics, submission of regulatory reports to authority portals (the system tracks the obligation and evidence; submission itself is performed in the authority's system).
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 clauses 8.2.1, 9.1.2, 10.2; ISO/IEC 17025:2017 clause 7.9 (complaints); ISO 15189 clause 7.7 / complaint handling (where applicable); ISO 13485 clause 8.2.2 and 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures (where enabled, tenant-configurable).
Related modules11.6 Nonconformance Management (NCR), 11.7 CAPA Management (CAPA), 11.5 Document & SOP Control (DOC), 11.4 Dashboards & Analytics (DSH), 11.12 Risk Management (RSK), 11.13 Management Review (MRV)
Primary personasP-14 Complaint Coordinator, P-05 Quality Manager, P-08 Process Owner, P-12 CAPA Coordinator, P-04 Quality Director; external complainant (customer) via portal/email.

11.8.2 Business Problem

Complaints today typically arrive through unmanaged channels — personal email inboxes, phone calls noted on paper, and verbal messages relayed between departments. There is no single register, so complaints are lost, acknowledged late, or answered by different staff with inconsistent content and no approval. Customer personal data is copied into spreadsheets without access control, and no one can reliably state how many complaints are open, how old they are, or which required a regulatory report.

Because complaints are not linked to nonconformances or corrective actions, the same failure recurs and each recurrence is handled as a new, unrelated event. Management cannot see complaint trends by product, site, or severity, and audit or inspection requests for complaint-handling evidence take days of manual reconstruction. The organization needs a controlled complaint process with enforced SLAs, privacy-aware customer records, a documented reportability decision for every complaint, and automatic traceability from complaint to investigation, correction, and customer response.

11.8.3 Business Objectives
  • BUS-OBJ-001 — standardize a single complaint-handling process across all sites and channels.
  • BUS-OBJ-002 — digitize the complaint register, replacing spreadsheets and paper phone logs.
  • BUS-OBJ-004 — enforce approval of every outgoing customer response before release.
  • BUS-OBJ-005 — guarantee traceability from complaint to NCR, CAPA, and customer response.
  • BUS-OBJ-006 — give managers real-time visibility of overdue acknowledgements, responses, and open complaints.
  • BUS-OBJ-007 — produce inspection-ready complaint files, including the reportability decision record.
  • BUS-OBJ-008 — capture an immutable audit trail of every complaint action.
  • BUS-OBJ-013 — supply complaint trend data to dashboards and management review.
  • BUS-OBJ-015 — protect customer personal data with tenant isolation and field-level privacy controls.
  • BUS-OBJ-016 — allow tenants to configure severity matrices, SLAs, and reportability checklists per compliance profile.

11.8.4 Actors & Personas
RolePersonaResponsibility in this module
Primary actorP-14 Complaint CoordinatorRegisters and triages complaints, performs reportability checklist, sends acknowledgements, coordinates investigation, drafts responses, manages closure.
InvestigatorP-08 Process Owner / P-09 Record OwnerInvestigates assigned complaints, documents findings, proposes corrections, raises or links NCR/CAPA.
ApproverP-05 Quality ManagerConfirms severity/reportability decisions for critical complaints, approves customer responses, approves closure.
OversightP-04 Quality DirectorReviews trends, handles escalations for overdue or critical complaints.
SupportingP-12 CAPA CoordinatorReceives complaint-sourced CAPA requests; maintains linkage (Section 11.7).
Read-onlyP-27 Executive Management User, P-28 Read-Only UserView dashboards, registers, and reports; no record modification.
ExternalComplainant (customer contact); P-29 External AuditorCustomer submits via portal/email and receives acknowledgement/response; external auditor views complaint files during audits under controlled access.
AdministrationP-03 Organization AdministratorConfigures categories, severity matrix, SLA timers, reportability checklists, templates.

11.8.5 Preconditions
  • Tenant is active with the CMP module enabled and complaint numbering scheme configured.
  • Complaint categories, severity matrix, priority rules, and SLA timers (acknowledgement, response, closure) are configured by the Organization Administrator.
  • Reportability checklist(s) for the tenant's applicable compliance profile(s) are configured and published (compliance-specific, tenant-configurable).
  • Acknowledgement and response e-mail/portal templates exist in the approved template library.
  • Users hold the roles defined in 11.8.13; the customer portal and/or e-mail intake integration is configured where those channels are used (Section 14).

11.8.6 Trigger Events
  • A customer submits a complaint through the customer portal (auto-registered as Draft/Submitted).
  • An e-mail arrives in a monitored complaint mailbox and is ingested as a draft complaint.
  • A phone call, letter, meeting note, or social-media report is received and logged manually by any authorized user.
  • A field return, service report, or survey response is judged by the Complaint Coordinator to constitute a complaint.
  • An internal user identifies customer dissatisfaction that meets the tenant's complaint definition.

11.8.11 Functional Requirements
CMP-FR-001 Multi-channel complaint intake MustCore
Requirement
The system shall accept complaints from (a) the customer portal as self-service submissions, (b) monitored e-mail mailboxes via the e-mail intake integration, and (c) manual entry for phone calls, letters, and other channels, stamping each record with its channel and received date/time.
Rationale
All complaints must enter one controlled register regardless of how they arrive.
Actor
Customer (portal), System (e-mail), Complaint Coordinator (manual)
Preconditions / Trigger
Channels configured; complaint received.
Validation & Exceptions
Channel and description mandatory; e-mail intake failures queue for manual triage without data loss.
Audit
Creation event with channel, source address, and timestamp.
Acceptance criteria
AC-CMP-01
Related
CMP-BR-001, Section 14
CMP-FR-002 Registration with unique ID and duplicate detection MustCore
Requirement
The system shall assign each complaint a unique tenant-scoped identifier on creation and, before registration, shall present potential duplicates matched on customer, product/batch, and a configurable date window, allowing the Coordinator to merge or cancel duplicates with cross-references.
Rationale
Prevents double-counting and fragmented investigation of the same issue.
Actor
Complaint Coordinator
Preconditions / Trigger
Draft complaint exists.
Validation & Exceptions
Registration blocked until duplicate candidates are dispositioned; merged records retain both audit trails.
Audit
Registration, merge, and duplicate-cancellation events with linked IDs.
Acceptance criteria
AC-CMP-01
Related
CMP-BR-002
CMP-FR-003 Customer data privacy controls MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall store customer identity and contact details as privacy-classified fields, masking them (e.g. "A***** — a****@***.com") for all roles without the "View confidential" permission, excluding them from exports by default, and never placing them in URLs or notification subject lines.
Rationale
Complaint records contain personal data subject to privacy regulation and tenant data-protection commitments (BUS-OBJ-015).
Actor
All users; enforcement by system
Preconditions / Trigger
Any read, export, or notification containing customer fields.
Validation & Exceptions
Unmasked access requires the permission and is itself audited; export of unmasked data requires explicit selection plus permission.
Audit
Every unmasked view/export logged with user, time, and record.
Acceptance criteria
AC-CMP-02
Related
CMP-BR-011, Section 18 (PRI-NFR)
CMP-FR-004 Configurable severity classification MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall classify each complaint using a tenant-configurable severity matrix (default levels Critical / Major / Minor) that derives priority and SLA deadlines; changing severity shall recompute deadlines and record the before/after values with reason.
Rationale
Risk-proportionate handling and consistent SLAs across coordinators.
Actor
Complaint Coordinator; Quality Manager (override)
Preconditions / Trigger
Registered complaint awaiting classification.
Validation & Exceptions
Severity mandatory before acknowledgement; Critical selection triggers immediate QM escalation.
Audit
Classification and every change (before/after, reason, user).
Acceptance criteria
AC-CMP-03
Related
CMP-BR-003
CMP-FR-005 Regulatory-reportability assessment MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall require a documented reportability assessment for every complaint using a tenant-configurable checklist per compliance profile (e.g. medical-device vigilance, accredited-laboratory obligations); a "reportable" outcome shall require Quality Manager countersignature and shall create a regulatory-report task with a tracked compliance deadline.
Rationale
Regulated tenants must evidence that every complaint was evaluated for reporting obligations; needs differ per regulation, so the checklist is compliance-specific and configurable.
Actor
Complaint Coordinator, Quality Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
Checklist published for the tenant profile; complaint registered.
Validation & Exceptions
All checklist questions must be answered; "Undetermined" is allowed only with a re-assessment task and deadline; investigation cannot close while the decision is Undetermined.
Audit
Checklist answers, decision, rationale, countersignature — all immutable once countersigned.
Acceptance criteria
AC-CMP-04
Related
CMP-BR-004, RPT-CMP-05
CMP-FR-006 Customer acknowledgement with SLA MustCore
Requirement
The system shall generate a customer acknowledgement from an approved template containing the complaint reference, send it through the intake or preferred channel, timestamp the send against the configured acknowledgement SLA (default 2 business days — proposed target, pending business confirmation), and escalate when the SLA is breached.
Rationale
Timely acknowledgement is a customer commitment and an ISO/IEC 17025 clause 7.9 expectation.
Actor
System; Complaint Coordinator (manual channels)
Preconditions / Trigger
Severity classified; customer contact available.
Validation & Exceptions
Send failure retries then raises a manual-send task; anonymous complaints record an acknowledgement waiver with reason.
Audit
Acknowledgement content version, send time, channel, delivery status.
Acceptance criteria
AC-CMP-05
Related
CMP-BR-005, RPT-CMP-03
CMP-FR-007 Investigation workspace MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide an investigation workspace per complaint where the assigned investigator records the investigation plan, findings, root cause (where identifiable), attachments, and conclusion, with a due date derived from the response SLA and overdue tracking.
Rationale
Structured, evidenced investigation is the basis of the customer response and any corrective action.
Actor
Process Owner (investigator)
Preconditions / Trigger
Complaint assigned; status Under Review.
Validation & Exceptions
Conclusion mandatory before response drafting; reassignment preserves prior entries.
Audit
Assignment, each findings edit (versioned), conclusion.

Related

CMP-FR-008 NCR / CAPA linkage MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow creation of a pre-populated NCR (Section 11.6) or CAPA request (Section 11.7) directly from a complaint, maintaining bidirectional links and surfacing linked-record status on the complaint; for Critical or reportable complaints a link or a QM-approved waiver justification shall be mandatory before closure.
Rationale
Closes the loop between customer dissatisfaction and systemic correction (BUS-OBJ-009).
Actor
Process Owner, Complaint Coordinator, CAPA Coordinator
Preconditions / Trigger
Investigation identifies a nonconformity or systemic cause.
Validation & Exceptions
Links restricted to same-tenant records; unlink requires reason and QM approval.
Audit
Link/unlink events with both record IDs and reason.

Related

CMP-FR-009 Response drafting and approval MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support versioned drafting of the customer response from approved templates and shall route each draft for approval; the approver must differ from the drafter, reportable complaints additionally require Quality Director approval, and where the tenant's 21 CFR Part 11 profile is enabled the approval shall capture an electronic signature per Section 19.
Rationale
Every outgoing statement to a customer is a controlled, approved communication.
Actor
Complaint Coordinator (drafter), Quality Manager / Quality Director (approvers)
Preconditions / Trigger
Investigation concluded.
Validation & Exceptions
Rejection requires reason and returns status to Returned for Correction; approved version is locked.
Audit
Each version, approval/rejection with reason, e-signature manifest where applicable.

CMP-FR-010 Resolution and customer notification MustCore
Requirement
The system shall release only the approved response version to the customer through the recorded channel, timestamp the resolution against the response SLA, and record delivery status; manual-channel dispatch shall be confirmed by the Coordinator with date and method.
Rationale
Guarantees the customer receives exactly the approved content and provides SLA evidence.
Actor
System, Complaint Coordinator

Validation & Exceptions

Requirement
The system shall enforce a closure checklist (response delivered, reportability decision final, linked NCR/CAPA closed or waived, closure reason recorded) approved by the Quality Manager, and shall permit reopening only by the Quality Manager within the configured reopen window with mandatory reason, resuming the record at Under Review.
Rationale
Prevents premature closure and provides a controlled path for customer rebuttals.

Preconditions / Trigger

Validation & Exceptions

The system shall continuously monitor acknowledgement, response, and closure SLA clocks per complaint, issue reminders at configurable thresholds (e.g. 75% elapsed), and escalate breaches up the configured chain (Coordinator → Quality Manager → Quality Director) with all escalations audited.

System

11.8.16 Integration Requirements
  • Inbound — customer portal: portal submissions create Draft complaints with channel "Portal" and the submitter's contact details; see Section 14.
  • Inbound — e-mail intake: monitored mailbox ingestion creates Draft complaints with the original message and attachments preserved as evidence; failures queue for manual triage (Section 14).
  • Outbound — notification service: acknowledgements, responses, reminders, and escalations dispatched via the platform notification integration (Section 14).
  • Internal — NCR / CAPA: record creation and status synchronization with Section 11.6 and Section 11.7 via bidirectional links.
  • Internal — analytics: anonymized complaint metrics published to dashboards (Section 11.4) and management review inputs (Section 11.13).
  • Optional — ERP/CRM product master: product and customer lookups where the tenant enables the ERP/CRM integration.
    Optional future scope: automatic filing of vigilance reports into authority portals is not in the current scope; the system tracks the obligation, deadline, and evidence only.

11.8.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-CMP-01 — Multi-channel intake produces one registered record

  • Given a complaint arriving by portal, by monitored e-mail, and by a phone call logged manually,
  • When each is processed through registration,
  • Then each becomes exactly one complaint with a unique tenant-scoped ID, correct channel stamp, and received timestamp, and duplicate candidates were presented before registration.

AC-CMP-02 — Customer data masking enforced

  • Given a user without the "View confidential" permission opening a complaint,
  • When the record, list views, exports, and notifications are inspected,
  • Then customer name and contact details appear masked everywhere, and an unmasked view by an authorized user is recorded in the audit trail with user and time.

AC-CMP-03 — Critical severity escalates immediately

  • Given a registered complaint,
  • When the Coordinator classifies it as Critical,
  • Then the Quality Manager and Quality Director receive an immediate notification, SLA deadlines are computed from the Critical row of the severity matrix, and the classification with justification is audited.

AC-CMP-04 — Reportability decision gated and countersigned

  • Given a complaint whose reportability checklist yields "reportable",
  • When the Coordinator records the decision without Quality Manager countersignature,
  • Then the decision remains pending, closure is blocked, and after QM countersignature a regulatory-report task with the configured compliance deadline is created automatically.

AC-CMP-05 — Acknowledgement SLA breach escalates

  • Given a classified complaint whose acknowledgement SLA reaches 75% elapsed and then breaches,
  • When no acknowledgement has been sent or waived,
  • Then the Coordinator receives the at-risk reminder, the Quality Manager receives the breach escalation, and both events appear in RPT-CMP-03 and the audit trail.

AC-CMP-06 — Complaint-to-CAPA linkage enforced for critical complaints

  • Given a Critical complaint with a concluded investigation and no linked NCR or CAPA,
  • When the Quality Manager attempts closure,
  • Then closure is rejected until either a linked NCR/CAPA exists or a waiver justification is approved by the Quality Manager, and the chosen path is audited.

AC-CMP-07 — Only the approved response reaches the customer

  • Given a response draft approved by the Quality Manager (approver different from drafter),
  • When the response is dispatched,
  • Then the transmitted content matches the approved version exactly, the version is locked against edits, and an attempt by the drafter to self-approve an earlier draft was rejected and audited.

AC-CMP-08 — Controlled closure and reopening

  • Given a resolved complaint passing the closure checklist and closed by the Quality Manager,
  • When the customer submits a rebuttal within the reopen window,
  • Then the Quality Manager can reopen it with a mandatory reason, the record returns to Under Review, and trend datasets reflect the reopening.

11.9 Audit Management AUD

11.9.1 Module Overview
Module nameAudit Management
Module codeAUD
PurposePlan, schedule, conduct, report, and follow up internal, supplier, and external/regulatory audits, from a risk-based annual programme through findings, corrective actions, and verified closure.
Business valueProvides objective, systematic assessment of the QMS; produces defensible audit evidence; reduces audit-preparation effort and improves audit readiness (BUS-OBJ-010).
ScopeAnnual audit programme; audit types; auditor assignment with independence; checklists/criteria; opening meeting; evidence; findings classification; finding-to-CAPA linkage; follow-up & verification; audit report and closure; external audit/inspection tracking.
Out of scopeThe corrective actions themselves (owned by CAPA); nonconformance investigation (NCR). Findings link to these.
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §9.2 (internal audit); ISO 19011 (auditing guidelines); ISO/IEC 17025:2017 §8.8; 21 CFR Part 11 (signed reports where configured).
Related modulesNCR, CAPA, DOC, RSK, MRV
Primary personasP-16 Lead Auditor, P-15 Internal Auditor, P-17 Auditee, P-05 Quality Manager, P-04 Quality Director, P-29 External Auditor
ClassificationCore Must

11.9.2 Business Problem

Audit programmes managed on spreadsheets and documents suffer from inconsistent planning, lost checklists, findings tracked in disconnected files, and follow-up that fails silently. Auditor independence is difficult to demonstrate, and linking findings to corrective actions and verifying their closure is manual. During certification and regulatory audits, organizations struggle to produce a complete, chronological record of their own audit activity.

NT.QMS makes the audit lifecycle a controlled workflow: a risk-based programme drives scheduled audits; auditors are assigned with an enforced independence rule; checklists and evidence are captured in the record; findings are classified and automatically drive nonconformances and CAPAs; and follow-up, verification, and reporting are tracked to closure with a full audit trail.

11.9.3 Business Objectives
  • Deliver a risk-based annual audit programme with complete execution tracking (BUS-OBJ-010).
  • Enforce auditor independence and objectivity (BUS-OBJ-004).
  • Link every finding to corrective action and verify closure (BUS-OBJ-009, BUS-OBJ-005).
  • Produce audit reports and evidence on demand for inspections (BUS-OBJ-007).
  • Track external audits and regulatory inspections centrally.

11.9.4 Actors & Personas
CategoryPersonasRole in module

Supporting actorsP-17 Auditee, P-07 Department Manager, P-08 Process OwnerProvide evidence; respond to findings
ApproversP-04 Quality Director, P-05 Quality ManagerApprove programme & audit report
AdministratorsP-02 Tenant Admin, P-04 Quality DirectorConfigure audit types, checklists, classifications

11.9.5 Preconditions
  • Audit types, checklist templates, finding classifications, and criteria (standard clauses) are configured.
  • Auditor competency records exist (from TRN) to support qualified assignment.
  • The organizational structure is defined so audit scope can target units/processes/sites.

11.9.6 Trigger Events
  • Annual audit programme planning cycle begins.
  • A scheduled audit's start date approaches.
  • A risk, complaint trend, or repeated nonconformance triggers an ad-hoc/for-cause audit.
  • An external audit or regulatory inspection is announced.
  • A finding's corrective-action verification date is reached.

11.9.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-AUD-01 — Programme coverage

  • Given an annual programme being drafted,
  • When a standard-required area is not scheduled within the cycle,
  • Then the system warns of the coverage gap before the programme can be approved.

AC-AUD-02 — Independence enforced

  • Given an auditor who belongs to the department in scope,
  • When the lead auditor attempts to assign them,
  • Then the assignment is blocked unless a documented exception is approved by the Quality Director, and the decision is audited.

AC-AUD-05 — Finding classification

  • Given an auditor recording a finding,
  • When they attempt to save it without a classification,
  • Then the save is blocked until a classification from the configured list is selected.

AC-AUD-06 — Finding drives CAPA

  • Given a finding classified as a major nonconformity,
  • When it is confirmed,
  • Then a linked nonconformance/CAPA is created with the finding context and bidirectional traceability, audited as FindingLinkedToCapa.

AC-AUD-08 — Closure requires verified findings

  • Given an audit with one finding whose CAPA is not yet effective,
  • When the QM attempts to close the audit,
  • Then closure is blocked until the finding's corrective action is verified effective.

AC-AUD-10 — Controlled closure feeds MRV

  • Given an audit with an approved report and all findings verified,
  • When the QM closes the audit,
  • Then status becomes Closed and the audit result becomes available as a management-review input.
Note: AC-AUD-03, AC-AUD-04, AC-AUD-07, AC-AUD-09 follow the same Given/When/Then structure and are maintained in the test repository (RTM, Section 24).

11.10 Training & Competency TRN

11.10.1 Module Overview
Module nameTraining & Competency Management
Module codeTRN
PurposePlan, assign, execute, assess, and evidence all workforce training and competency activities so that every employee performing quality-relevant work is demonstrably qualified for the tasks assigned to them.
Business valueEliminates paper training files, provides inspection-ready evidence of competency, closes the loop between document revisions and workforce awareness, and gives managers real-time visibility of training gaps and overdue items.
ScopeEmployee training profiles and job roles; required competencies per role; training matrix; annual training plan; course catalog; training assignments (read & understand, classroom, online/LMS); attendance; assessments with pass scores and retakes; practical observation; supervisor sign-off; competency expiry and retraining; training triggered by document revision; effectiveness evaluation; certificates; complete training history.
Out of scopeAuthoring of e-learning content (SCORM/xAPI packages are hosted in the external LMS); HR payroll, leave, and performance-appraisal processes; recruitment qualification screening.
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §7.2 (Competence), §7.3 (Awareness); ISO/IEC 17025:2017 §6.2; ISO 15189 §6.2 (where applicable); ISO 13485 §6.2 (where applicable); 21 CFR Part 11 (e-signatures on sign-offs, where enabled); GxP training-record principles.
Related modules11.5 Document & SOP Control (revision-triggered training), 11.7 CAPA (training as corrective action), 11.9 Audit Management (auditor competency evidence), 11.3 IAM (user/role provisioning), 11.4 Dashboards.
Primary personasP-18 Training Coordinator, P-19 Trainer, P-20 Employee / Trainee, P-07 Department Manager, P-05 Quality Manager

11.10.2 Business Problem

Training records in most quality organizations are fragmented across paper sign-off sheets, departmental spreadsheets, and e-mail confirmations. When a procedure is revised, there is no reliable mechanism to identify every employee who must be retrained before the new revision becomes effective, and no proof that they actually read and understood it. During external audits, assembling the training file for a single employee can take hours, and gaps are discovered only when an inspector asks.

Competency is equally opaque: organizations cannot answer, at any moment, "who is currently qualified to perform this task?" Expired competencies go unnoticed, retraining is reactive, and training effectiveness is rarely evaluated. The TRN module replaces this with a role-driven training matrix, automated assignment and escalation, evidenced assessments and sign-offs, and a complete, tamper-evident training history per employee.

11.10.3 Business Objectives
  • BUS-OBJ-011 — Manage training and competency with demonstrable, inspection-ready evidence.
  • BUS-OBJ-002 — Digitize all training records, attendance sheets, assessments, and certificates.
  • BUS-OBJ-005 — Provide end-to-end traceability from role requirement to competency evidence.
  • BUS-OBJ-006 — Give managers visibility of overdue and expiring training before it becomes a finding.
  • BUS-OBJ-008 — Keep immutable audit trails of every training and sign-off event.
  • BUS-OBJ-010 — Sustain permanent audit readiness for competency requirements of ISO 9001 §7.2.

11.10.4 Actors & Personas
Role typePersonaResponsibility in TRN
Primary actorP-18 Training CoordinatorMaintains course catalog, competency definitions, training matrix, annual plan; creates and monitors assignments; issues certificates.
Primary actorP-20 Employee / TraineeCompletes assigned training, confirms read & understand, takes assessments.
SupportingP-19 TrainerDelivers classroom sessions, records attendance, marks assessments, conducts practical observations.
ApproverP-07 Department Manager (Supervisor)Signs off practical competency; approves departmental training plans; handles escalations for failed retakes.
ReviewerP-05 Quality ManagerApproves annual training plan; reviews effectiveness evaluations; reviews competency-gap reports.

ExternalP-31 Integration Service AccountLMS result callbacks; HR employee-master synchronization.

11.10.5 Preconditions
  • Tenant and organization structure (sites, departments) are configured (11.2).
  • Employee accounts exist and are mapped to job roles in IAM (11.3) or synchronized from HR.
  • Competency definitions and the course catalog have been created and approved by the Training Coordinator.
  • Controlled documents that require read & understand training are managed in DOC (11.5).
  • Notification channels (in-app, e-mail) are configured for the tenant.
  • Where 21 CFR Part 11 mode is enabled, e-signature policy is configured (Section 19).

11.10.6 Trigger Events
  • A new employee is hired or an existing employee changes job role (matrix gap detected automatically).
  • A controlled document linked to a competency is revised and approved in DOC (automatic retraining trigger).
  • A competency reaches its expiry window (automatic retraining assignment at configured lead time).
  • The approved annual training plan releases a scheduled course occurrence.
  • A CAPA action plan (11.7) specifies training as a corrective action.
  • A supervisor or Quality Manager manually requests ad-hoc training for an individual or group.
  • An audit finding (11.9) identifies a competency gap.

11.10.11 Functional Requirements
TRN-FR-001 Employee training profile and job-role assignment MustCore
Requirement
The system shall maintain a training profile for every active employee, including employee ID, department, site, one or more job roles, hire date, and status, synchronized from IAM or HR integration, and shall recompute required competencies whenever a role assignment changes.
Rationale
The training matrix and all automatic assignments derive from role membership; stale profiles cause missed training.
Actor
Training Coordinator; P-31 Integration Service Account
Preconditions / Trigger
Employee created/updated in IAM or HR feed; manual role change by coordinator.
Validation & Exceptions
Role must exist in the competency matrix; deactivated employees are excluded from new assignments but retain history.
Audit
Profile and role changes logged with before/after values and source (manual vs. sync).
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-01
Related
TRN-FR-003, TRN-BR-001
TRN-FR-002 Competency definitions per job role MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow the Training Coordinator to define competencies (name, description, linked documents, required assessment, observation checklist, validity period in months, criticality) and map each competency as mandatory or optional to one or more job roles, with versioned definitions.
Rationale
ISO 9001 §7.2 requires determined competence per role; the mapping is the master data behind the matrix.
Actor
Training Coordinator; Quality Manager (approval)
Preconditions / Trigger
Role exists; competency definition submitted for approval before activation.
Validation & Exceptions
Validity period 0 (never expires) to 60 months; a competency in use cannot be deleted, only superseded.
Audit
Definition versions and role-mapping changes audited with reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-01
Related
TRN-BR-002, RPT-TRN-01
TRN-FR-003 Training matrix with gap detection MustCore
Requirement
The system shall generate a live training matrix (employees × required competencies) showing per cell: Compliant, In progress, Overdue, Expiring within lead time, Expired, or Not required, and shall automatically create draft assignments for every gap detected.
Rationale
Provides the single answer to "who is qualified for what, right now" and drives proactive assignment.
Actor
System; Training Coordinator (review)
Preconditions / Trigger
Role mappings active; recomputed on role change, competency change, completion, or expiry.
Validation & Exceptions
Matrix filterable by site, department, role, competency, status; export respects permissions.
Audit
Auto-created assignments logged with triggering event.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-02
Related
RPT-TRN-01, TRN-FR-010
TRN-FR-004 Annual training plan MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support an annual training plan per organization: planned courses, target audiences, planned quarter/month, budget note, and owner; the plan shall follow a Draft → Under Review → Approved lifecycle and shall report planned-vs-actual execution.
Rationale
Management review and audits require evidence of planned, resourced training.
Actor
Training Coordinator (author); Quality Manager (approver)
Preconditions / Trigger
Course catalog populated; planning cycle opened.
Validation & Exceptions
Plan items must reference catalog courses; changes to an approved plan require a new approved version.
Audit
Plan versions, approvals, and item changes audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-02
Related
RPT-TRN-04, Section 11.13
TRN-FR-005 Course catalog MustCore
Requirement
The system shall maintain a versioned course catalog: course code, title, description, delivery type(s), duration, competencies delivered, linked controlled documents, assessment definition, pass mark, retake limit, qualified trainers, validity period, and active/retired status.
Rationale
Assignments and plans must reference controlled course definitions, not free text.
Actor
Training Coordinator
Preconditions / Trigger
Competencies defined; linked documents effective in DOC.
Validation & Exceptions
Course code unique per tenant; retiring a course does not affect closed assignments; open assignments on a retired course are flagged to the coordinator.
Audit
Catalog changes versioned and audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-03
Related
TRN-FR-006
TRN-FR-006 Assignment types: read & understand, classroom, online/LMS MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support three assignment delivery types: (a) document-based read & understand with in-app presentation of the effective revision and a confirmation action; (b) classroom sessions with scheduling, invitations, and attendance; (c) online courses launched in an integrated LMS with completion/score returned via integration (Section 14).
Rationale
One workflow must cover all delivery modes used across the organization.
Actor
Employee; Trainer; System
Preconditions / Trigger
Assignment created with a delivery type permitted by the course.
Validation & Exceptions
R&U confirmations bind to the exact document revision presented; LMS callbacks must be authenticated and idempotent.
Audit
Confirmation, attendance, and LMS result events audited with timestamps.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-03, AC-TRN-04
Related
TRN-FR-007, TRN-BR-004
TRN-FR-007 Attendance recording for classroom sessions MustCore
Requirement
The system shall let the assigned Trainer record per-trainee attendance (present, absent, partial with reason) for each session occurrence, locking the attendance record 5 working days after the session (proposed target — pending business confirmation), after which corrections require coordinator approval with reason.
Rationale
Attendance is primary evidence of classroom training delivery.
Actor
Trainer; Training Coordinator (corrections)
Preconditions / Trigger
Session occurred; trainee was invited.
Validation & Exceptions
Only invited trainees can be marked; absentee assignments remain open and re-enter the reminder cycle.
Audit
Attendance entries and post-lock corrections audited with before/after and reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-04
Related
TRN-BR-005
TRN-FR-008 Assessments with pass score and limited retakes MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support course assessments (question bank, randomized selection optional, auto-scored objective questions and trainer-marked open questions), enforce the course pass mark, record every attempt with score and timestamp, and block further attempts once the configured retake limit is reached, raising an escalation task to the trainee's supervisor.
Rationale
Understanding must be verified, not assumed; uncontrolled retries devalue the assessment.
Actor
Employee; Trainer; System
Preconditions / Trigger
Training activity completed; assessment attached to course.
Validation & Exceptions
Pass mark 0–100%; retake limit 1–5 (default 3); attempts are immutable once submitted.
Audit
Each attempt audited (score, duration, questions served, result).
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-05
Related
TRN-BR-006
TRN-FR-009 Practical observation and supervisor sign-off MustCore
Requirement
Where a competency requires practical demonstration, the system shall present the observation checklist to the observer, require all mandatory items to be answered, and require final competency sign-off by the trainee's supervisor (or recorded delegate), applying an e-signature with meaning "Competency confirmed" where Part 11 mode is enabled.
Rationale
Knowledge tests alone do not prove ability to perform the task.
Actor
Trainer/observer; Department Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
Assessment passed (where defined); observation checklist configured on competency.
Validation & Exceptions
Signer must not be the trainee (SoD); refusal returns the assignment with mandatory reason.
Audit
Checklist results and signature manifest audited immutably.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-05
Related
TRN-BR-007, Section 19
TRN-FR-010 Competency expiry and retraining triggers MustCore
Requirement
The system shall compute a competency expiry date from the validity period at completion, automatically create a retraining assignment at a configurable lead time before expiry (default 60 days — proposed target, pending business confirmation), and set the competency to Suspended if expiry passes without renewal, notifying the employee, supervisor, and coordinator.
Rationale
Competency decays; renewal must be systematic, not remembered.
Actor
System; Training Coordinator
Preconditions / Trigger
Competency has a non-zero validity period.
Validation & Exceptions
Manual expiry extension requires coordinator role and reason and is audited.
Audit
Expiry computations, suspensions, and extensions audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-06
Related
TRN-FR-003, TRN-BR-008
TRN-FR-011 Training triggered by document revision MustCore
Requirement
When a controlled document linked to a competency or course is approved with a new revision in DOC (Section 11.5), the system shall automatically create read & understand assignments for all employees whose roles require that document, with a due date aligned to the document's effective date, and shall report completion status to the Document Controller before effectiveness where configured.
Rationale
Employees must be trained on the revision they will work to, before it becomes effective.
Actor
System; Document Controller; Training Coordinator
Preconditions / Trigger
Document-to-competency/course link exists; revision approved.
Validation & Exceptions
If a trainee has an open assignment on the prior revision, it is superseded and re-pointed with notification.
Audit
Trigger event, affected population, and created assignments audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-04
Related
TRN-BR-004, RPT-TRN-05
TRN-FR-012 Training effectiveness evaluation ShouldConfigurable
Requirement
For courses flagged as requiring effectiveness evaluation, the system shall create an evaluation task for the supervisor at a configurable interval after completion (default 90 days — proposed target, pending business confirmation), capturing a verdict (Effective / Not effective) with justification; a Not-effective verdict shall automatically create a new training need.
Rationale
ISO 9001 §7.2(d) requires evaluating the effectiveness of actions taken to acquire competence.
Actor
Department Manager; Quality Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
Assignment closed on a flagged course.
Validation & Exceptions
Verdict requires justification text; overdue evaluations escalate to the Quality Manager.
Audit
Evaluation task lifecycle and verdicts audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-07
Related
RPT-TRN-06
TRN-FR-013 Certificate generation ShouldConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall generate a completion certificate (PDF) upon closure of an assignment, using a tenant-configurable template containing trainee name, course, competency, completion date, expiry date, verifying signatory, and a unique verification number; certificates shall be downloadable by the trainee and visible in the training history.
Rationale
Certificates are frequently requested by customers, regulators, and employees.
Actor
System; Employee (download)
Preconditions / Trigger
Assignment closed; template configured.
Validation & Exceptions
Certificate number unique per tenant; regenerated certificates keep the same number with a reissue counter.
Audit
Generation and reissue events audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-07
Related
RPT-TRN-03
TRN-FR-014 Complete employee training history MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide, per employee, a complete chronological training history — assignments, delivery evidence, assessment attempts and scores, observations, sign-offs, certificates, effectiveness results, and competency status changes — retained for the full retention period and exportable as a single inspection-ready package (PDF).
Rationale
The "employee training file" is the most requested artifact in external audits.
Actor
Training Coordinator; External Auditor (read-only)
Preconditions / Trigger
Employee exists; history accumulates automatically.
Validation & Exceptions
History is append-only; departed employees' histories remain accessible per retention policy.
Audit
History exports audited (who exported whose file, when).
Acceptance criteria
AC-TRN-08
Related
RPT-TRN-02, Section 21

11.10.16 Integration Requirements
  • Inbound — HR employee master: scheduled synchronization of employees, departments, and job-role mappings from the tenant's HR system; conflicts flagged to the coordinator (see Section 14).
  • Inbound — LMS results: authenticated callback/API returning completion status, score, and completion date per launched course; idempotent processing with a retry queue (see Section 14).
  • Inbound — DOC events: document-revision-approved events from Section 11.5 trigger R&U assignment generation (TRN-FR-011).
  • Outbound — LMS launch: single-sign-on launch links for online courses mapped in the catalog.
  • Outbound — CAPA and Audit: training-completion status exposed to CAPA action verification and Audit evidence collection.
  • Outbound — Dashboards: matrix compliance, overdue, and expiry KPIs feed Section 11.4 and Section 16.
Pending business confirmation: the specific LMS product and HR system in scope for integration, and whether SCORM/xAPI hosting is required, are to be confirmed during the discovery phase; integration identifiers will be assigned in Section 14.

11.10.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-TRN-01 — Role change recomputes required competencies

  • Given an employee whose job role is changed from "Technician" to "Senior Technician" with two additional mandatory competencies,
  • When the role change is saved,
  • Then the training matrix shows two new gap cells for that employee within one processing cycle and two draft assignments are created and logged with the triggering role-change event.

AC-TRN-02 — Matrix statuses and plan approval gate

  • Given an annual training plan in status Draft,
  • When the Training Coordinator attempts to release a planned course occurrence to trainees,
  • Then the system blocks the release until the plan is Approved by the Quality Manager, and the blocked attempt is recorded in the audit trail.

AC-TRN-03 — Read & understand binds to the presented revision

  • Given a trainee with an open R&U assignment for SOP-014 revision C,
  • When revision D of SOP-014 is approved before the trainee confirms,
  • Then the assignment is re-pointed to revision D, the trainee is re-notified, and any later confirmation records revision D — never revision C.

AC-TRN-04 — Attendance restricted to the assigned trainer

  • Given a completed classroom session with an assigned trainer,
  • When a different trainer attempts to record attendance for that session,
  • Then the action is denied with a permission message and the attempt is security-logged.

AC-TRN-05 — Retake limit enforcement with escalation

  • Given a course with pass mark 80% and retake limit 3, and a trainee who has failed three attempts,
  • When the trainee attempts a fourth assessment attempt,
  • Then the attempt is blocked, the assignment moves to Returned for Correction, and an escalation task is created for the trainee's supervisor with the attempt history attached.

AC-TRN-06 — Competency expiry triggers retraining and suspension

  • Given a competency with a 24-month validity completed on a known date and a 60-day lead time,
  • When the lead-time date is reached without renewal, and later the expiry date passes,
  • Then a retraining assignment is auto-created at the lead-time date, and at expiry the competency status becomes Suspended with notifications to trainee, supervisor, and coordinator, all events audited.

AC-TRN-07 — Not-effective verdict creates a new need

  • Given a closed assignment on a course flagged for effectiveness evaluation,
  • When the supervisor records a verdict of Not effective with justification,
  • Then a new training need is created referencing the original assignment, and the verdict appears in RPT-TRN-06.

AC-TRN-08 — Inspection-ready employee file export

  • Given an employee with closed assignments, assessment attempts, sign-offs, and certificates,
  • When an authorized user exports the Employee Training File,
  • Then a single PDF containing the complete chronological history is produced within 30 seconds, and the export event (who, whose file, when) is recorded in the audit trail.

11.11 Equipment, Calibration & Maintenance EQP

11.11.1 Module Overview
Module nameEquipment, Calibration & Maintenance Management
Module codeEQP
PurposeRegister and control all quality-relevant equipment through its full lifecycle — acquisition, qualification, calibration, preventive and corrective maintenance, status control, and decommissioning — with complete service history and out-of-tolerance handling.
Business valuePrevents use of unfit equipment, eliminates missed calibrations, provides instant certificate retrieval during inspections, and connects out-of-tolerance events to product/result impact assessment and NCR handling.
ScopeEquipment master with unique IDs; location/department assignment; manufacturer/model/serial; criticality classification; qualification status (IQ/OQ/PQ where applicable); calibration schedules and certificates; preventive maintenance schedules; corrective maintenance; service history; downtime recording; out-of-tolerance handling with impact assessment and automatic NCR creation; equipment status control; external service providers; certificate expiry alerts; decommissioning workflow.
Out of scopeReal-time condition monitoring / IoT telemetry ingestion; spare-parts inventory and procurement; fixed-asset financial accounting and depreciation.
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §7.1.5 (Monitoring and measuring resources); ISO/IEC 17025:2017 §6.4, §6.5 (equipment, metrological traceability); ISO 15189 §6.4 (where applicable); ISO 13485 §6.3, §7.6 (where applicable); 21 CFR Part 11 (e-signatures, where enabled); GxP qualification principles (IQ/OQ/PQ).
Related modules11.6 Nonconformance Management (auto-NCR on out-of-tolerance), 11.7 CAPA, 11.12 Risk Management (impact assessment input), 11.5 Document & SOP Control (operating/calibration procedures), 11.10 Training (operator competency), 11.4 Dashboards.
Primary personasP-21 Equipment Coordinator, P-22 Calibration Coordinator, P-23 Maintenance Technician, P-05 Quality Manager, P-30 External Service Provider

11.11.2 Business Problem

Equipment records are typically split between a fixed-asset register, calibration spreadsheets, and paper service files kept beside each instrument. Calibration due dates are tracked manually, certificates from external providers arrive by e-mail and are filed inconsistently, and there is no enforced link between an instrument's calibration state and whether staff may use it. When a calibration comes back out of tolerance, the critical question — "what did we measure, test, or release with this instrument since its last good calibration?" — is answered slowly and incompletely, if at all.

The EQP module establishes a single controlled equipment master with automated calibration and maintenance scheduling, enforced status control that blocks use of unfit equipment, structured out-of-tolerance handling with mandatory impact assessment and automatic NCR creation (Section 11.6), and a complete, retrievable service history per asset.

11.11.3 Business Objectives
  • BUS-OBJ-012 — Control equipment and calibration with automated scheduling and evidence.
  • BUS-OBJ-005 — Trace every measurement-critical asset from acquisition to decommissioning.
  • BUS-OBJ-006 — Surface overdue calibrations and expiring certificates before they become findings.
  • BUS-OBJ-007 — Support inspections with instant retrieval of calibration certificates and service history.
  • BUS-OBJ-008 — Maintain immutable audit trails for all equipment lifecycle events.
  • BUS-OBJ-004 — Enforce approvals and segregation of duties on release, out-of-tolerance disposition, and decommissioning.

11.11.4 Actors & Personas
Role typePersonaResponsibility in EQP
Primary actorP-21 Equipment CoordinatorMaintains the equipment master, classifications, statuses, provider register, and decommissioning requests.
Primary actorP-22 Calibration CoordinatorOwns calibration schedules, reviews results and certificates, releases equipment to service, initiates out-of-tolerance handling.
SupportingP-23 Maintenance TechnicianExecutes preventive and corrective maintenance, records downtime, and logs service entries.

11.11.5 Preconditions
  • Sites, buildings/locations, and departments are configured (11.2).
  • Criticality classes, calibration interval policies, and alert lead times are configured per tenant.
  • Approved calibration and maintenance procedures exist in DOC (11.5).
  • External service providers are registered with approval status and scope.
  • NCR module (11.6) is active to receive auto-created nonconformances.
  • Technicians performing work hold the required competencies (11.10).

11.11.6 Trigger Events
  • New equipment is acquired and must be registered and qualified before first use.
  • A calibration or preventive-maintenance due date reaches its alert lead time (automatic).
  • An equipment failure, damage, or abnormal behavior is reported (corrective maintenance).
  • A calibration result is recorded out of tolerance.
  • An external provider's calibration certificate or accreditation approaches expiry.
  • Equipment is relocated, transferred between departments, or requested for decommissioning.
  • An audit finding or NCR (11.6) requires equipment quarantine or investigation.

11.11.11 Functional Requirements
EQP-FR-001 Equipment master with unique identification MustCore
Requirement
The system shall maintain an equipment master where each asset receives a unique, immutable, tenant-scoped equipment ID and records name, manufacturer, model, serial number, site/location, owning department, acquisition date, and linked operating/calibration procedures from DOC (Section 11.5).
Rationale
A single controlled register is the foundation for scheduling, traceability, and inspection retrieval.
Actor
Equipment Coordinator
Preconditions / Trigger
New asset acquired or legacy asset migrated (Section 22).
Validation & Exceptions
Duplicate manufacturer+model+serial triggers a warning with link to the existing record; IDs are never reused, including after decommissioning.
Audit
Creation and every master-data change logged with before/after values.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-01
Related
EQP-BR-001, RPT-EQP-01
EQP-FR-002 Criticality classification MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall classify each asset into a tenant-configurable criticality class (default set: Critical, Major, Minor) that drives default calibration/PM interval policies, alert lead times, and escalation urgency; downgrading criticality shall require Quality Manager approval with reason.
Rationale
Control effort must be proportional to the asset's impact on product/result quality.
Actor
Equipment Coordinator; Quality Manager (downgrades)
Preconditions / Trigger
Classes configured by the Organization Administrator.
Validation & Exceptions
Class changes recompute schedule defaults prospectively only; historical records unchanged.
Audit
Classification changes logged with approver and reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-01
Related
EQP-BR-002
EQP-FR-003 Qualification status (IQ/OQ/PQ) ShouldCompliance
Requirement
For tenants operating under GxP/ISO 13485 requirements, the system shall record qualification stages per asset (IQ, OQ, PQ as applicable): protocol reference, execution date, result, evidence attachments, and approver; equipment flagged as requiring qualification shall not enter In Service status until all applicable stages are approved.
Rationale
Regulated environments must evidence that equipment is installed and operates as intended before use.
Actor
Equipment Coordinator; Quality Manager (approval)
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant compliance profile enables qualification; asset flagged as requiring it.
Validation & Exceptions
Stage order IQ → OQ → PQ enforced where all three apply; requalification may be triggered after major repair or relocation per tenant policy.
Audit
Stage results and approvals logged immutably with e-signature where enabled.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-02
Related
EQP-BR-003, Section 19
EQP-FR-004 Calibration scheduling MustCore
Requirement
The system shall compute the next calibration due date from the last passed calibration and the configured interval, automatically create a calibration work item at the configured lead time (default 30 days — proposed target, pending business confirmation), and escalate per 11.11.14 if the due date passes without completion.
Rationale
Missed calibrations are among the most common audit findings; scheduling must not depend on memory.
Actor
System; Calibration Coordinator
Preconditions / Trigger
Asset has calibration-required flag and interval.
Validation & Exceptions
Interval changes require reason and recompute the due date; overdue equipment is visually flagged everywhere the asset appears.
Audit
Due-date computations, alerts, and escalations logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-03
Related
EQP-BR-004, RPT-EQP-02
EQP-FR-005 Calibration execution and certificate management MustCore
Requirement
The system shall record calibration executions with as-found and as-left values per measurement point, the reference standard used (with its own traceability validity), performer (internal technician or external provider), and an attached certificate with unique number, issuer, issue date, and validity; release to service shall be blocked until the certificate is attached and results reviewed by someone other than the performer.
Rationale
Metrological traceability (ISO/IEC 17025 §6.5) requires complete, reviewable calibration evidence.
Actor
Maintenance Technician / External Provider; Calibration Coordinator (review/release)
Preconditions / Trigger
Open calibration work item; equipment Under Calibration.
Validation & Exceptions
Entry blocked if the reference standard's validity has expired; certificate numbers unique per issuer.
Audit
Result entry, certificate attachment, review, and release logged with SoD identities.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-03, AC-EQP-04
Related
EQP-BR-005
EQP-FR-006 Out-of-tolerance handling with impact assessment and automatic NCR MustCore
Requirement
When a calibration result is evaluated out of tolerance, the system shall automatically and non-bypassably set the equipment to Quarantined, block its use, open an OOT case identifying the usage period since the last passed calibration, require a documented impact assessment (affected measurements, tests, or products and their disposition), and automatically create a pre-populated NCR in Section 11.6 linked bidirectionally to the OOT case.
Rationale
ISO 9001 §7.1.5.2 requires assessing the validity of previous results when equipment is found unfit.
Actor
System; Quality Manager; Process Owner
Preconditions / Trigger
Tolerance evaluation returns OOT (automatic or coordinator-confirmed).
Validation & Exceptions
Exactly one NCR per OOT case (idempotent creation); the OOT case cannot close until the impact assessment is complete, the NCR is at least contained, and a passed recalibration exists.
Audit
Quarantine, NCR creation, assessment, disposition, and closure logged immutably.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-04, AC-EQP-05
Related
EQP-BR-006, Section 11.12
EQP-FR-007 Preventive maintenance schedules MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support preventive maintenance plans per asset (task list, frequency, estimated duration, required competency), automatically generate PM work orders at the configured lead time, and record completion with performed tasks, parts used, performer, and date.
Rationale
Planned maintenance reduces failures, downtime, and out-of-tolerance events.
Actor
Equipment Coordinator (plan); Maintenance Technician (execution)
Preconditions / Trigger
PM plan active on the asset.
Validation & Exceptions
Overdue PM work orders escalate like calibrations; skipping a PM occurrence requires coordinator approval with reason.
Audit
Work-order lifecycle and completions logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-06
Related
RPT-EQP-04
EQP-FR-008 Corrective maintenance MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow any authorized user to report an equipment failure, creating a corrective work order that sets the asset Out of Service, starts the downtime clock, and routes to a Maintenance Technician; completion shall record diagnosis, work performed, parts, and — for measuring equipment that was adjusted or repaired — enforce recalibration before return to service.
Rationale
Uncontrolled repairs of measuring equipment silently invalidate results.
Actor
Any authorized reporter; Maintenance Technician; Calibration Coordinator
Preconditions / Trigger
Failure, damage, or abnormal behavior observed.
Validation & Exceptions
Return to service without required recalibration is blocked; irreparable assets route to decommissioning (EQP-FR-013).
Audit
Report, assignment, work performed, and status transitions logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-06
Related
EQP-BR-007
EQP-FR-009 Service history and downtime recording MustCore
Requirement
The system shall maintain an append-only service history per asset — calibrations, PM, corrective work, relocations, status changes, provider interventions — and record downtime periods (start, end, reason class) automatically from status transitions, computing availability and mean-time-between-failure indicators per asset and class.
Rationale
History underpins reliability decisions, provider evaluation, and replacement planning.
Actor
System; Maintenance Technician
Preconditions / Trigger
Any service or status event on the asset.
Validation & Exceptions
History entries cannot be edited or deleted; corrections are appended as amendment entries with reason.
Audit
All entries carry actor, timestamp, and source event.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-06
Related
RPT-EQP-05
EQP-FR-010 Equipment status control and usage blocking MustCore
Requirement
The system shall enforce the equipment status set — In Service, Out of Service, Under Calibration, Quarantined, Suspended, Decommissioned — permitting only the transitions defined in 11.11.9, displaying the current status and next calibration due date wherever the asset is referenced, and exposing a status API so other modules can prevent recording work performed with unfit equipment.
Rationale
Status control is the mechanism that actually prevents use of unfit equipment.
Actor
System; all module actors
Preconditions / Trigger
Any lifecycle event.
Validation & Exceptions
Manual override of Quarantined status is not available to any role; release requires the defined closure workflow.
Audit
Every status transition logged with trigger and actor.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-05
Related
EQP-BR-006, EQP-BR-008
EQP-FR-011 External service provider register MustCore
Requirement
The system shall maintain a register of external calibration/maintenance providers with approval status, service scope, accreditation details (e.g., ISO/IEC 17025 scope) and accreditation expiry; only approved, unexpired providers may be assigned to work items, and each provider's interventions shall be traceable in the service history.
Rationale
Externally provided calibration is only as trustworthy as the provider's demonstrated competence.
Actor
Equipment Coordinator; Quality Manager (approval)
Preconditions / Trigger
Provider onboarding or accreditation renewal.
Validation & Exceptions
Assignment to an expired/unapproved provider is blocked; existing open work items are flagged when a provider's accreditation lapses.
Audit
Provider approvals, scope changes, and expiry events logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-07
Related
EQP-BR-009, Section 14
EQP-FR-012 Certificate and accreditation expiry alerts MustCore
Requirement
The system shall monitor validity dates of calibration certificates and provider accreditations and raise alerts at configurable lead times (default 60/30/7 days — proposed target, pending business confirmation) to the Calibration Coordinator and Equipment Coordinator, listing affected assets and open work items.
Rationale
Expired certificates discovered during an audit are avoidable findings.
Actor
System
Preconditions / Trigger
Certificates/accreditations carry expiry dates.
Validation & Exceptions
Alerts repeat per schedule until resolved; suppression requires reason and is audited.
Audit
Alert generation and acknowledgments logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-07
Related
RPT-EQP-03
EQP-FR-013 Decommissioning workflow MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide a decommissioning workflow: coordinator request with reason and final disposition (scrapped, sold, returned, transferred), completion of a configurable checklist (data/label removal, open-item verification), Quality Manager approval with e-signature where enabled, and final transition to Decommissioned with the full record retained read-only for the retention period.
Rationale
Uncontrolled disposal breaks traceability and can hide unresolved quality issues.
Actor
Equipment Coordinator; Quality Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
Asset no longer required or irreparable.
Validation & Exceptions
Blocked while open work items, NCRs, or CAPAs reference the asset; the equipment ID is never reused.
Audit
Request, checklist, approval, and final transition logged immutably.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-08
Related
EQP-BR-010, Section 21
EQP-FR-014 Equipment labels and inventory verification ShouldConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall generate printable calibration/status labels (equipment ID, status, last and next calibration date, QR code resolving to the equipment record) and support periodic physical inventory verification campaigns where each asset's presence and label state are confirmed, with discrepancies routed to the Equipment Coordinator.
Rationale
Bench-level visibility of calibration state and periodic verification keep the register aligned with reality.
Actor
Equipment Coordinator; Maintenance Technician
Preconditions / Trigger
Label template configured; verification campaign scheduled.
Validation & Exceptions
QR resolution respects authentication and tenant isolation; unresolved discrepancies escalate after 10 working days.
Audit
Label prints and verification results logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-EQP-08
Related
RPT-EQP-01

11.11.16 Integration Requirements
  • Outbound — NCR creation: automatic, idempotent NCR creation from OOT cases into Section 11.6 with bidirectional linkage (EQP-FR-006).
  • Outbound — status API: equipment fitness status exposed to other modules (e.g., audit evidence, risk assessments) to prevent recording work with unfit equipment (EQP-FR-010).
  • Inbound — DOC links: operating and calibration procedures referenced from Section 11.5; revision events surface on the equipment record.
  • Inbound — training status: technician competency checks against Section 11.10 before work-item assignment.
  • Optional — asset/ERP synchronization: import of asset master data from a fixed-asset or ERP system (see Section 14).
  • Outbound — Dashboards: calibration compliance, overdue counts, OOT rate, and downtime KPIs feed Section 11.4 and Section 16.
Optional future scope: a limited external-provider portal allowing approved providers (P-30) to upload certificates directly, and IoT/condition-monitoring ingestion for predictive maintenance.

11.11.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-EQP-01 — Unique, immutable equipment ID

  • Given a registered asset with equipment ID EQP-00123,
  • When any user, including an administrator, attempts to change or reuse that ID for another asset,
  • Then the system rejects the change, the ID remains bound to the original asset permanently, and the attempt is recorded in the audit trail.

AC-EQP-02 — Qualification gate before first use

  • Given an asset flagged as requiring IQ/OQ/PQ with only IQ approved,
  • When the Equipment Coordinator attempts to set the asset to In Service,
  • Then the transition is blocked with a message naming the outstanding qualification stages, and the attempt is audited.

AC-EQP-03 — Automatic scheduling and overdue escalation

  • Given an asset with a 12-month calibration interval, a last passed calibration date, and a 30-day lead time,
  • When the lead-time date is reached, and later the due date passes without a released calibration,
  • Then a work item is created at the lead-time date, the asset is flagged Overdue at due date + 1 day, and escalation notifications reach the Quality Manager at +7 days per the escalation chain, all events audited.

AC-EQP-04 — Release requires certificate and SoD review

  • Given a calibration performed and recorded by technician T with no certificate attached,
  • When technician T attempts to release the equipment to service,
  • Then the release is blocked both for the missing certificate and because the reviewer must differ from the performer, and both violations are reported and audited.

AC-EQP-05 — Out-of-tolerance quarantine and automatic NCR

  • Given a calibration result with one measurement point outside its acceptance limit,
  • When the tolerance evaluation is confirmed,
  • Then the equipment status becomes Quarantined immediately and non-bypassably, an OOT case identifying the usage period since the last passed calibration is opened, exactly one pre-populated NCR is created in the NCR module with a bidirectional link, and the Quality Manager is notified — all within one minute of confirmation.

AC-EQP-06 — Repair enforces recalibration; history is append-only

  • Given a measuring instrument set Out of Service and adjusted during corrective maintenance,
  • When the technician attempts to return it to In Service without a passed recalibration,
  • Then the transition is blocked, and the completed service entry appears in the asset history as an immutable, append-only record with downtime start/end computed from the status transitions.

AC-EQP-07 — Provider approval and expiry alerts enforced

  • Given an external provider whose accreditation expires in 25 days and another provider whose approval has lapsed,
  • When the Calibration Coordinator assigns new calibration work,
  • Then assignment to the lapsed provider is blocked, assignment to the expiring provider succeeds with a warning, and the 30-day and 7-day expiry alerts fire on schedule to the coordinators.

AC-EQP-08 — Decommissioning blocked by open items

  • Given an asset with an open NCR referencing it,
  • When the Equipment Coordinator submits a decommissioning request,
  • Then the request is blocked with a list of the open items, and after the NCR is closed the same request proceeds through checklist and Quality Manager approval to the terminal Decommissioned status with the record retained read-only.
