11.12 Risk Management RSK

11.12.1 Module Overview
Module nameRisk Management
Module codeRSK
PurposeProvide a tenant-configurable risk register in which quality-related risks are identified, scored, mitigated, accepted at the correct authority level, and periodically reviewed, with full traceability to the records that evidence each risk.
Business valueSatisfies risk-based thinking obligations of ISO 9001:2015 (clauses 6.1, 9.1.3, 10.2), converts scattered risk knowledge into a governed register, and ensures mitigation actions are executed and verified rather than merely recorded.
ScopeRisk register; configurable categories and scoring models (likelihood × severity, optional detectability for FMEA-style scoring); risk matrix and heat map; existing controls; mitigation plans and actions (including creation of CAPA / improvement tasks); residual risk; risk acceptance with authority levels; periodic review scheduling; linkage to audits, CAPA, complaints, equipment, suppliers, and documents.
Out of scopeEnterprise financial risk management, insurance management, project schedule risk, and quantitative Monte-Carlo risk simulation. Opportunity management beyond a simple "opportunity" flag on register entries is optional future scope.
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §6.1, §9.1.3, §9.3.2, §10.2; ISO/IEC 17025:2017 §8.5; ISO 13485 §4.1.2/§7.1 (where applicable); GxP quality risk management principles (ICH Q9 alignment as guidance).
Related modulesCAPA (11.7), Audit (11.9), Nonconformance (11.6), Complaints (11.8), Equipment (11.11), Document Control (11.5), Management Review (11.13), Dashboards (11.4).
Primary personasP-24 Risk Manager, P-08 Process Owner, P-09 Record Owner, P-05 Quality Manager, P-04 Quality Director, P-27 Executive Management User.

11.12.2 Business Problem

Most organizations record risks in disconnected spreadsheets owned by individual departments. Scoring scales differ between sheets, mitigation actions are noted but never tracked to completion, and there is no defensible record of who accepted a residual risk or on what authority. When an external auditor asks how risk-based thinking is applied, the organization must reconstruct evidence manually.

Because risks are not linked to the operational records that reveal them — audit findings, nonconformances, complaints, equipment failures, supplier issues — recurring problems are treated as isolated events, and the risk register drifts out of date. Periodic review is left to memory, so high risks can remain unexamined for years.

NT.QMS resolves this by providing a single tenant-configurable register with enforced scoring models, authority-controlled acceptance, action tracking through the CAPA engine, mandatory review cycles, and bidirectional links to the QMS records that constitute the evidence base for each risk.

11.12.3 Business Objectives
  • Standardize risk identification and scoring across sites and departments on tenant-configured scales (BUS-OBJ-001, BUS-OBJ-016).
  • Digitize the risk register and eliminate uncontrolled departmental spreadsheets (BUS-OBJ-002, BUS-OBJ-003).
  • Enforce acceptance approvals at the correct authority level with segregation of duties (BUS-OBJ-004).
  • Provide end-to-end traceability from risk to mitigation actions, CAPA records, and source evidence (BUS-OBJ-005, BUS-OBJ-009).
  • Give management visibility of overdue reviews and overdue mitigation actions (BUS-OBJ-006, BUS-OBJ-013).
  • Maintain immutable audit trails proving how each risk was assessed, treated, and accepted (BUS-OBJ-008, BUS-OBJ-010).

11.12.4 Actors & Personas
Role in modulePersona(s)Responsibilities
Primary actorP-24 Risk ManagerOwns the register configuration usage, triages submitted risks, facilitates assessments, monitors review cycles and the heat map.
Risk ownerP-08 Process Owner, P-07 Department Manager, P-09 Record OwnerAccountable for an individual risk: assessment input, mitigation plan execution, residual assessment, periodic review.
ContributorsP-20 Employee, P-15 Internal Auditor, P-14 Complaint Coordinator, P-21 Equipment Coordinator, P-25 Supplier Quality ManagerIdentify and submit candidate risks from operational context (findings, complaints, equipment failures, supplier issues).
Acceptance authoritiesP-05 Quality Manager (low/medium), P-04 Quality Director (high), P-27 Executive Management User (critical)Approve risk acceptance decisions at the authority level mapped to the risk level (tenant-configurable mapping).
ReviewersP-05 Quality Manager, P-24 Risk ManagerReview assessments and mitigation plans before acceptance routing.
AdministratorsP-03 Organization Administrator, P-02 Tenant AdministratorConfigure categories, scoring scales, matrix thresholds, acceptance-authority mapping, review frequencies.
Read-onlyP-28 Read-Only User, P-29 External AuditorView register, heat map, and evidence within granted scope; external auditors see time-boxed, scoped views only.
ExternalP-30 External Service ProviderNo direct access; supplier-related risk content is managed internally by P-25.

11.12.5 Preconditions
  • Tenant and organization structure exist and are active (11.2); users hold RSK roles via IAM (11.3).
  • Risk categories are configured (defaults provisioned: Process, Product, Supplier, Equipment, Compliance, Information; tenant may add or rename).
  • A scoring model is activated for the tenant: 2-factor (likelihood × severity) or 3-factor FMEA-style (likelihood × severity × detectability), with scale definitions (labels, values 1–5 by default) and matrix thresholds mapping scores to risk levels (Low / Medium / High / Critical).
  • Acceptance-authority mapping (risk level → minimum approving role) is configured.
  • Review-frequency defaults per risk level are configured (e.g. Critical quarterly, High semi-annually, Medium/Low annually — proposed defaults, pending business confirmation).
  • CAPA module is active if mitigation actions are to be delegated to CAPA (11.7); otherwise native mitigation tasks are used.

11.12.6 Trigger Events
  • Manual identification of a risk by any authorized user (planned risk workshops or ad-hoc).
  • "Raise risk" action from a linked record context: audit finding (11.9), nonconformance (11.6), complaint (11.8), equipment failure or calibration out-of-tolerance (11.11), supplier performance issue, or document change impact assessment (11.5).
  • Scheduled periodic review date reached for an existing risk (system-triggered).
  • Management review output requesting risk register updates (11.13).
  • Change in context (new process, site, product line, regulation) prompting a risk assessment campaign.
  • Escalation: mitigation action overdue or residual risk exceeding appetite after treatment.

11.12.9 Record Lifecycle

Applicable statuses: Draft, Submitted, Under Review (assessment), Rejected, Mitigation In Progress, Pending Acceptance, Accepted – Monitoring (Active), Closed, Archived. "Mitigation In Progress", "Pending Acceptance", and "Accepted – Monitoring" are module-specific refinements of the canonical Active state.

11.12.11 Functional Requirements
RSK-FR-001 Tenant-configurable risk register and categories MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall provide a tenant-scoped risk register whose categories, sub-categories, sources, and treatment strategies are configurable per tenant, provisioned with the default categories Process, Product, Supplier, Equipment, Compliance, and Information. Deactivating a category shall be blocked while open risks reference it.
Rationale
Different industries structure risk differently; configuration avoids code changes (BUS-OBJ-016).
Actor
Tenant / Organization Administrator
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant active; administrator opens RSK configuration.
Validation & Exceptions
Category names unique per tenant; deactivation with open references rejected with the list of blocking risks.
Audit
Every configuration change logged with before/after values.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-06
Related
RSK-BR-001
RSK-FR-002 Risk identification from any linked module context MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow authorized users to create a risk directly and from the context of an audit finding, nonconformance, complaint, equipment record, supplier record, or document, automatically creating a bidirectional link and pre-filling source, scope, and description from the source record.
Rationale
Risks surface inside operational processes; capture at source preserves traceability (BUS-OBJ-005).
Actor
Any authorized user; contributors per 11.12.4
Preconditions / Trigger
User has create permission in RSK and read permission on the source record.
Validation & Exceptions
Source record must belong to the same tenant; duplicate-title warning offers linking to an existing risk instead.
Audit
RiskCreated event includes source record reference.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-04
Related
RSK-FR-009, Sec. 11.9
RSK-FR-003 Configurable scoring model (2-factor or FMEA-style 3-factor) MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall support a tenant-selectable scoring model of likelihood × severity, optionally extended with detectability (FMEA-style RPN). Scale sizes (default 1–5), value labels and descriptions, and the matrix thresholds mapping scores to Low / Medium / High / Critical shall be tenant-configurable. Each assessment shall store the model version used.
Rationale
A single fixed scale does not fit all tenants; FMEA scoring is required in manufacturing contexts.
Actor
Tenant Administrator (configuration); Risk Owner (use)
Preconditions / Trigger
Model configuration exists before first assessment.
Validation & Exceptions
Matrix must cover every likelihood/severity combination; model changes apply to new assessments only — historical assessments retain their captured model version.
Audit
Model configuration changes logged with version increment.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-01
Related
RSK-FR-004, RSK-BR-002
RSK-FR-004 Automatic score computation and matrix-derived risk level MustCore
Requirement
The system shall compute the risk score as the product of the selected factor values and derive the risk level from the configured matrix, for both initial and residual assessments. Scores and levels shall be system-computed only and never manually editable.
Rationale
Removes scoring inconsistency and manipulation; makes levels comparable across the register.
Actor
System (computation); Risk Owner (factor input)
Preconditions / Trigger
All configured factors selected on an assessment.
Validation & Exceptions
Factor values must lie within the configured scale; incomplete factor sets block save of the assessment.
Audit
RiskAssessed / ResidualAssessed events store factor values, score, level, and model version.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-01
Related
RSK-FR-003, RPT-RSK-02
RSK-FR-005 Mitigation plans with tracked actions and CAPA creation MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support mitigation plans containing actions with owner, due date, status, and completion evidence, and shall allow any mitigation action to be created as a linked CAPA or improvement task in the CAPA module (11.7) with automatic bidirectional status synchronization.
Rationale
Mitigation only reduces risk when executed; reusing the CAPA engine gives one action-tracking discipline (BUS-OBJ-009).
Actor
Risk Owner (plan); Action Owners (execution)
Preconditions / Trigger
Treatment strategy = mitigate; initial assessment complete.
Validation & Exceptions
Each action requires owner and due date; overdue actions escalate per 11.12.14; linked CAPA closure updates the risk action automatically.
Audit
MitigationPlanned, MitigationActionCompleted, CapaCreatedFromRisk events.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-03
Related
RSK-BR-004
RSK-FR-006 Residual risk assessment MustCore
Requirement
The system shall require a residual risk assessment on the same scoring model after mitigation completion (or with justification when accepting without mitigation), shall retain the full initial-versus-residual history, and shall flag any residual score that exceeds the initial score.
Rationale
Acceptance decisions must be made on post-treatment exposure, with evidence of improvement.
Actor
Risk Owner
Preconditions / Trigger
All mandatory mitigation actions closed and verified.
Validation & Exceptions
Residual scoring blocked while mandatory actions remain open (RSK-BR-004).
Audit
ResidualAssessed event with before/after values.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-03
Related
RSK-FR-007
RSK-FR-007 Risk acceptance gated by authority level MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall enforce a tenant-configurable mapping of risk level to minimum acceptance authority (default: Low/Medium → Quality Manager; High → Quality Director; Critical → Executive Management) and shall record the acceptance statement, conditions, validity period, and — where the tenant has enabled 21 CFR Part 11 signatures — an electronic signature per Section 19. The approver must differ from the risk owner.
Rationale
Residual risk must be knowingly accepted at a level commensurate with exposure (BUS-OBJ-004).
Actor
Mapped acceptance authority
Preconditions / Trigger
Risk in Pending Acceptance.
Validation & Exceptions
Attempted acceptance below the mapped authority is rejected and audited; return-for-treatment requires a reason.
Audit
RiskAccepted with approver identity, authority check result, signature manifest.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-02
Related
RSK-BR-003
RSK-FR-008 Periodic review scheduling, reminders, and escalation MustCore
Requirement
The system shall schedule the next review date of every accepted risk from tenant-configured frequencies per risk level, send reminders before the due date, escalate overdue reviews to the Risk Manager and Quality Manager, and require a recorded review outcome (no change / re-assess / close proposal).
Rationale
Registers decay without enforced review; overdue visibility is a stated objective (BUS-OBJ-006).
Actor
System (scheduling); Risk Owner (review)
Preconditions / Trigger
Risk accepted; frequency configuration present.
Validation & Exceptions
Owners may shorten the cycle but never extend it beyond the level minimum; review completion without an outcome is blocked.
Audit
RiskReviewed and ReviewEscalated events.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-05
Related
RSK-BR-005, RPT-RSK-03
RSK-FR-009 Linkage of risks to QMS records MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support bidirectional links between a risk and audits, CAPA records, nonconformances, complaints, equipment, suppliers, and controlled documents within the same tenant, displaying linked records permission-trimmed on both sides and preserving links across status changes.
Rationale
Traceability from evidence to risk and treatment is the audit-readiness backbone (BUS-OBJ-005, BUS-OBJ-010).
Actor
Risk Owner, Risk Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
Both records exist in the tenant; user has read access to the target.
Validation & Exceptions
Cross-tenant link attempts are denied and security-logged; deleting links requires a reason.
Audit
RiskLinkAdded / RiskLinkRemoved with target reference and reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-04
Related
Sec. 17
RSK-FR-010 Risk heat map and register analytics MustCore
Requirement
The system shall render an interactive heat map plotting open risks on the configured likelihood/severity matrix (initial or residual view), filterable by category, site, process, owner, and status, with drill-down to the underlying risks, and shall expose the same dataset to dashboards (11.4) and exports.
Rationale
Management needs a one-glance exposure picture for prioritization and management review input (BUS-OBJ-013).
Actor
Risk Manager, Quality Director, Executive Management
Preconditions / Trigger
At least one assessed risk exists in the user's scope.
Validation & Exceptions
Heat map respects record-level permissions; cells with no accessible risks render empty rather than counting hidden records.
Audit
Exports of the heat map / register logged with filter criteria.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-06
Related
RPT-RSK-02, Sec. 16
RSK-FR-011 Risk owner assignment, reassignment, and delegation MustCore
Requirement
The system shall require exactly one accountable risk owner per risk, allow the Risk Manager to reassign ownership with a reason, and honor IAM delegation rules during owner absence, transferring open tasks and notifications to the delegate for the delegation period.
Rationale
Unowned risks are unmanaged risks; absence must not stall reviews or actions.
Actor
Risk Manager; IAM delegation engine
Preconditions / Trigger
Owner leaves role, is deactivated, or delegation window starts.
Validation & Exceptions
Deactivating a user with owned open risks forces a reassignment step; delegate must hold the Risk Owner role.
Audit
RiskOwnerChanged with old/new owner and reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-05
Related
Sec. 11.3
RSK-FR-012 Opportunity flag on register entries ShouldConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall allow a register entry to be flagged as an opportunity (positive risk), reusing the same workflow with "pursue / enhance" treatment labels, so that ISO 9001 §6.1 "risks and opportunities" is evidenced from one register.
Rationale
Auditors expect opportunities to be addressed alongside risks; a second module would duplicate workflow.
Actor
Risk Owner, Risk Manager
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant enables the opportunity flag.
Validation & Exceptions
Opportunity entries are excluded from the risk heat map by default (toggle available).
Audit
Flag changes audited as field changes.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RSK-06
Related
RSK-FR-001

11.12.16 Integration Requirements
  • Inbound: "Raise risk" context actions from Audit (11.9), NCR (11.6), Complaints (11.8), Equipment (11.11), and Document Control (11.5); supplier performance data for supplier-category risks.
  • Outbound: creation of CAPA / improvement tasks with bidirectional status sync (11.7); heat-map and KPI datasets to Dashboards (11.4) and Management Review input compilation (11.13); notification dispatch via the platform notification service (Sec. 14, INT-001 email gateway).
  • Identity & signatures: role, delegation, and e-signature verification via IAM (11.3) and the signature service (Sec. 19).
  • No direct external-system integration is required for RSK in the base scope; register import from legacy spreadsheets is covered by Migration (Sec. 22).

11.12.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-RSK-01 — Score computation follows the configured model

  • Given a tenant configured with the 3-factor FMEA model on 1–5 scales and a matrix mapping scores ≥ 60 to Critical,
  • When a risk owner records likelihood 4, severity 5, detectability 3,
  • Then the system stores score 60, derives level Critical, positions the risk in the correct heat-map cell, and prevents any manual edit of score or level.

AC-RSK-02 — Acceptance authority enforced with SoD

  • Given a High risk pending acceptance and a mapping requiring Quality Director authority,
  • When a Quality Manager (or the risk owner holding Quality Director rights) attempts to accept it,
  • Then the system rejects the action, names the required authority, and writes an AuthorizationDenied audit entry; acceptance by an eligible Quality Director succeeds and records the signature manifest.

AC-RSK-03 — Residual assessment gated by action closure

  • Given a risk in Mitigation In Progress with one open mandatory action linked to a CAPA,
  • When the risk owner attempts residual scoring, and later the linked CAPA action is closed,
  • Then the first attempt is blocked citing the open action, the CAPA closure synchronizes the risk action to closed, and residual scoring then proceeds and moves the risk to Pending Acceptance.

AC-RSK-04 — Risk raised from an audit finding is linked bidirectionally

  • Given an internal auditor viewing a major audit finding,
  • When the auditor uses "Raise risk" from the finding,
  • Then a draft risk is created with source, scope, and description pre-filled, and after submission both records display the link, which survives all later status changes.

AC-RSK-05 — Overdue review escalates

  • Given an accepted Critical risk whose review was due 7 days ago with no recorded outcome,
  • When the daily scheduler runs,
  • Then the system sends an escalation to the Risk Manager, lists the risk in RPT-RSK-03, and records a ReviewEscalated audit event.

AC-RSK-06 — Heat map respects permissions and configuration

  • Given a user scoped to Site A only, and open risks in Sites A and B,
  • When the user opens the heat map filtered to "all sites",
  • Then only Site A risks are counted and drillable; Site B risks are neither shown nor counted, and the export reproduces exactly the visible dataset.

Module nameManagement Review
Module codeMRV
PurposePlan and conduct management reviews of the QMS: compile required inputs from across the system, capture decisions and action items, generate and approve minutes, and track resulting actions to closure.
Business valueProvides top management with a consolidated, evidence-based view of quality performance and produces documented decisions and improvement actions (BUS-OBJ-013); supplies mandatory ISO 9001 §9.3 evidence.
ScopeReview scheduling; agenda templates; participants & quorum; auto-compiled inputs; decisions; action items with owners/dates; minutes generation & approval; follow-up.
Out of scopeThe source data itself (owned by the contributing modules); execution of resulting corrective actions (tracked as CAPAs/tasks).
Related standardsISO 9001:2015 §9.3 (management review); ISO/IEC 17025:2017 §8.9; 21 CFR Part 11 (signed minutes where configured).
Related modulesAUD, NCR, CAPA, CMP, RSK, DSH
Primary personasP-26 Management Review Coordinator, P-27 Executive Management, P-04 Quality Director, P-05 Quality Manager
ClassificationCore Must

11.13.2 Business Problem

Management reviews are a mandatory requirement of quality standards, yet organizations commonly assemble the inputs manually the night before the meeting, capture decisions in loosely structured minutes, and lose track of the resulting action items. Auditors frequently find that management-review actions were never followed up and that required inputs (such as risk status or supplier performance) were not considered.

NT.QMS automates the assembly of management-review inputs directly from the operational modules, provides a standard agenda aligned to ISO 9001 §9.3, records decisions and action items as tracked tasks with owners and due dates, and generates controlled, optionally signed minutes — creating complete, defensible evidence of review.

11.13.3 Business Objectives
  • Ensure every review considers all required inputs (BUS-OBJ-013).
  • Reduce review preparation effort by auto-compiling inputs (BUS-OBJ-010).
  • Track review decisions and actions to verified closure (BUS-OBJ-009).
  • Produce controlled minutes as inspection evidence (BUS-OBJ-007).

11.13.5 Preconditions
  • Agenda templates and input mappings (which modules/metrics feed each agenda item) are configured.
  • Participant roles and quorum rules are defined for the tenant.
  • Contributing modules hold the data to be compiled (audits, CAPA, complaints, risks, KPIs).

11.13.6 Trigger Events
  • A scheduled management review's date approaches (periodic cadence).
  • An ad-hoc review is called (e.g. major incident, significant change, regulatory driver).
  • A review action item reaches its due date.
  • Previous-review actions require status roll-forward into the next review.

11.13.9 Record Lifecycle
  • Scheduled — review created with date, agenda, participants.
  • Inputs Ready — required inputs compiled and pack distributed.
  • In Progress — meeting held; discussion, decisions, and actions being captured.
  • Minutes Draft — minutes generated, awaiting approval.
  • Returned for Correction — minutes returned with comments.
  • Minutes Approved — minutes approved (and signed if configured), locked.
  • Follow-up — action items being implemented and verified.
  • Closed — all actions closed or rolled forward; review complete.
  • Cancelled — review cancelled before it was held.
  • Archived — retained long-term.

11.13.18 Acceptance Criteria

AC-MRV-01 — Standard agenda scheduling

  • Given a configured §9.3 agenda template and quorum rule,
  • When the coordinator schedules a review without a required quorum role invited,
  • Then the system warns before the review can be confirmed.

AC-MRV-02 — Input auto-compilation with gap flag

  • Given a scheduled review with input mappings,
  • When inputs are compiled and supplier performance data is unavailable,
  • Then the pack lists all available inputs and flags supplier performance as a gap requiring resolution or a documented N/A.

AC-MRV-04 — Tracked actions

  • Given a decision requiring follow-up,
  • When the coordinator records an action item with an owner and due date,
  • Then a tracked task is created, the owner is notified, and ActionItemCreated is audited.

AC-MRV-05 — Immutable signed minutes

  • Given generated minutes and signed approval configured,
  • When the chair approves and signs the minutes,
  • Then the minutes are locked, the signature is bound, and any later change requires a new version with reason.

AC-MRV-06 — Action roll-forward

  • Given a review being closed with one open action,
  • When the coordinator closes the review,
  • Then the open action is carried forward as a previous-action input to the next review and ActionRolledForward is audited.
Note: AC-MRV-03 follows the same Given/When/Then structure and is maintained in the test repository (RTM, Section 24).

11A Application Pages & Screens Catalogue

This section inventories every page of the NT.QMS application as delivered, organized by the exact sidebar navigation groups of the product. NT.QMS is a multi-tenant quality-management platform for accredited laboratories (ISO 15189 / ISO IEC 17025, with ISO 9001 and 21 CFR Part 11 support), so alongside the general quality modules it provides a full analytical-quality (statistical QC) suite. The sidebar has nine groups plus the separate Platform Administration area. Each page is specified with a page code, route, a metadata block (purpose, actors, entry points, key permissions, related), layout & regions, a features & actions table, page states, rules & notifications, navigation, and — for record pages — an on-screen lifecycle progress bar (stepper).

Source of truth. The groups, page names, routes, and purpose statements in this section are taken from the delivered application's navigation and route configuration and its permission catalogue (the "Roles & Privileges" privilege matrix). Every functional area provides a list/register screen and a detail screen; most also provide create/edit and data-entry/action screens, described within each page card. Layouts remain illustrative; pixel-level UI design lives in the SDD (§3.5).

11A.1 Conventions, Page-Type Legend & Stepper Notation
Conventions. Page code PG-<GROUP>-## where GROUP is the sidebar group (OVW, IMP, DOC, RSK, RES, PPL, ANL, ADM, PLT). Routes use :id for a record identifier. Every page enforces backend authorization (GEN-TC-009), tenant isolation via RLS (GEN-TC-015), branch/department data-scoping from the user's role restrictions, localization EN/AR-RTL/FR, and audit logging of state changes (GEN-TC-005).
Page typePurposeStandard regions
List / RegisterBrowse and find records of one typeFilter bar, saved views, results grid, bulk actions, pagination, "new" action, export
DetailView a single record and act on itHeader with lifecycle stepper, tabs (details / data / evidence / related / audit), action bar
Create / EditCapture or amend record dataSectioned form, validation, attachment panel, save/submit
Data-entry / ActionEnter measurements/replicates or perform a workflow step (approve, verify, sign, compute)Entry grid, compute panel, verdict, re-authentication for signing
Analytics / DashboardRole-based KPIs, tasks, alertsKPI cards, charts, drill-down, filters
ConfigurationAdminister settings / cataloguesSetting groups, editors, preview; every change audited

Stepper notation. Detail pages highlight the record's current lifecycle stage; done stages teal, current navy, terminal green (red for a rejected/void end). Example — a nonconformance under investigation:

11A.10 Analytical Quality Group (Statistical QC Suite)

The analytical-quality modules support ISO 15189 / ISO IEC 17025 §7 method validation, verification, and ongoing quality control, using recognised CLSI protocols. Except where noted (QC, PT plan, proficiency testing), every study follows the same page pattern — List of studies → Study detail → Data entry (replicates/pairs/readings) → Compute (statistics & verdict) → Sign off & lock — reflected in the shared stepper below. Poor outcomes can raise a nonconformance (PG-IMP-01). Sign-off applies an electronic signature recorded in the Compliance Ledger (PG-ADM-06).

Each functional page's list, detail, create/edit, and data-entry/sign-off screens are covered within its card. Utility controls (My Account, dark-mode/sidebar toggles, Sign Out) live in the top bar. 12 Module Interaction Model

12.1 How Quality Records Flow Between Modules

NT.QMS is a single application composed of the functional modules of Section 11 and Section 11A (nine sidebar groups plus the Platform portal) that share one tenant-scoped database, one workflow engine, one notification service, one evidence store and one immutable audit trail. Modules never call each other's internal services directly and never share write access to each other's tables. Instead, every cross-module effect is produced by an in-process domain event persisted through a transactional outbox: the source module commits its own state change and the outbox row in the same database transaction; a dispatcher then delivers the event to subscribing module handlers, which create or update their own records in a new transaction. This guarantees that a quality record and the downstream record it triggers can never silently diverge — either both exist, or the event remains queued and visible for retry.

The dominant record flow follows the classic quality loop. Operational signals — a customer complaint (CMP), an audit finding (AUD), an out-of-tolerance calibration result (EQP), a process deviation raised on the shop floor (NCR) or a risk assessment outcome (RSK) — converge on the Nonconformance and CAPA modules, which act as the corrective hub of the system. Containment and correction are handled inside NCR; systemic issues escalate to CAPA, where root-cause analysis, action plans and effectiveness verification are managed. Outputs of CAPA in turn fan back out: corrective actions frequently require a controlled document revision (DOC), which itself triggers read-and-understand or classroom retraining (TRN); closed CAPAs with effectiveness results, audit programme status, complaint trends and KPI series are aggregated as inputs to Management Review (MRV), whose decisions are issued as tracked action items back into the operational modules. Dashboards (DSH) subscribe to lifecycle events from every module and maintain KPI aggregates; they never query module tables directly at render time for cross-module figures.

Three shared conventions apply to every interaction listed in Table 12-1:

  • Traceable linkage. The created target record stores a typed, navigable reference to the source record (source type, source ID, tenant ID, link reason). Links are bidirectional and surfaced in the traceability views defined in Section 17.
  • Tenant and scope preservation. The event carries the tenant context of the source record; handlers create target records in the same tenant and default to the same company/branch/ department scope. Cross-tenant event delivery is structurally impossible (single-tenant event payloads validated against PostgreSQL RLS context) and any anomaly is security-logged.
  • Auditable delivery. Event publication, each delivery attempt, handler outcome and any dead-lettering are recorded in the audit trail with correlation IDs, so an inspector can prove that (for example) every confirmed complaint produced its mandated investigation record.
Note: "Integration method" in Table 12-1 is always the in-process domain event via the transactional outbox described above. External (out-of-product) integrations such as e-mail, ERP or LIMS are specified separately in Section 14.

12.2 Module Interaction Matrix

Table 12-1 enumerates the mandatory cross-module interactions. Each row is a contract: the trigger, the record that must result, the data carried by the event, and the behaviour required when handling fails. Failure handling is uniform: the outbox retries with exponential backoff (3 attempts over 15 minutes as a proposed target — pending business confirmation), then dead-letters the event, raises a system alert to the Tenant Administrator and Quality Manager, and lists the event on the integration health panel until resolved or manually replayed.

12.4 Data-Flow Across Modules and Shared Services

Figure 12-2 shows how records, evidence files, notifications, audit entries and search-index updates move between producing modules, the shared platform services and consuming modules. Shared services are tenant-aware: every payload carries the tenant ID and is validated against the caller's RLS context.

12.5 Quality-Record Traceability Example

Figure 12-3 illustrates a complete traceability chain for a worked example: customer complaint CMP-2026-014 escalates to a nonconformance, then to a CAPA whose corrective action revises an SOP and retrains staff, is verified for effectiveness, and finally feeds Management Review. Every arrow is a stored, bidirectional record link that is navigable in both directions and reportable end-to-end (Section 17).

Note: Record identifiers in Figure 12-3 are illustrative. Numbering schemes per record type are tenant-configurable (see §11.2).

13 Personas, Roles & Permissions

13.1 Persona Register

Table 13-1 defines the canonical personas used consistently throughout this SRS. A persona is a business role, not a system role: one user account may hold several personas (subject to the segregation-of-duties rules in §13.4), and each persona maps to one or more configurable system roles in IAM (§11.3). "Scope" states the default organizational reach of the persona's data access; Tenant Administrators may narrow (never widen) these defaults per assignment.

13.2 Access Model

NT.QMS combines role-based access control (RBAC) with attribute-based restrictions (ABAC). RBAC answers "what actions may this role perform in which module"; ABAC then filters "on which records", using record attributes — tenant, company, branch, department, site, record ownership, confidentiality class, record status and (for CAPA/AUD) SoD relationships. A user's effective permission on a record is the intersection of the two: an action is allowed only if at least one held role grants it and no attribute restriction blocks it. Deny always overrides allow.

  • Tenant isolation. Every tenant-owned row carries a tenant ID enforced by PostgreSQL row-level security. Tenant context is derived exclusively from trusted authentication claims — never from the request body or query parameters. Any cross-tenant access attempt is denied, security-logged and alerted; there is no administrative override inside the application (GEN-BR-004, §18).
  • Organizational scoping. Role assignments are made at a scope node — tenant, company, branch, department or site — and apply to that node and its descendants. A user may hold the same role at different scopes (e.g. Quality Manager for Site A only). Scope narrowing at assignment time is permitted; widening beyond the role definition is not.
  • Record ownership. Each record has exactly one owner (P-09) at any time. Owners receive implicit edit rights while the record is in an editable status, lose them when the record enters review/approved states, and never gain approval rights on their own record when SoD is enabled. Ownership transfer is a workflow action requiring the receiving user's scope to cover the record and the current manager's approval; the transfer is audited.
  • Confidential records. Records may be classified Standard, Restricted or Confidential. Confidential records (e.g. complaints containing patient/customer identity, HR-linked training assessments, MRV minutes) are visible only to roles with the matching confidentiality clearance and organizational scope; all other users see the record's existence masked (ID and status only) or fully hidden, per tenant configuration. Confidential exports require an additional permission and are individually audited.
  • Temporary delegation and acting assignments. A user (or their manager) may delegate a role for a defined period with a mandatory end date. The delegate acts "on behalf of" — both identities are recorded on every action and signature. Delegation can never grant permissions the delegate's own competency restrictions forbid (GEN-BR-010), can never create a self-approval situation, and is revocable at any time. Standing "acting manager" assignments follow the same mechanism with HR-confirmed dates.
  • Read-only access. Read-Only Users (P-28) and External Auditors (P-29) receive view/search/print permissions only. External Auditor accounts are additionally time-boxed (auto-disabled at the audit window end), restricted to an explicit grant list, and every record they open is written to the audit trail.
  • Segregation of duties and maker-checker. SoD is evaluated at action time, not only at role-assignment time: even if a user legitimately holds both "author" and "approver" roles, the approval of a specific record is blocked when they authored or own it. Maker-checker applies to security-sensitive administration — user role grants, workflow definition changes, SoD-rule configuration and retention-policy changes each require a second authorized administrator to confirm before taking effect (GEN-BR-006).
Assumption: SoD enforcement is enabled by default for all tenants. A tenant may relax specific SoD rules only via a documented configuration change that is itself maker-checker controlled and visibly flagged on affected records and reports.

13.4 Segregation-of-Duties Rules

The following business rules are global — they apply across all modules and take precedence over any role or delegation grant. Each is enforced at action time by the authorization service and every blocked attempt is recorded in the audit trail with rule ID, user, record and timestamp.

Rule IDRuleEnforcementException handling
GEN-BR-001 A user shall not review or approve a record they authored or currently own, when SoD is enabled (default). Approval action blocked at execution time with rule-violation message; workflow router excludes author/owner from eligible approver lists. Tenant may disable per record type via maker-checker-controlled configuration; affected records display an "SoD relaxed" flag and appear on the SoD exception report.
GEN-BR-002 Reviewer and approver of the same workflow stage shall be different users; a multi-step route shall not resolve two consecutive steps to the same person. Route validation at submission and at each step completion; violating routes cannot be activated. Where staffing makes this impossible for a small site, Quality Director may approve a documented per-route waiver; waiver is audited and time-boxed.
GEN-BR-003 The CAPA effectiveness verifier shall be different from the CAPA action implementer(s) and the CAPA owner. Verifier picker excludes implementers/owner; verification submission by an excluded user is rejected and logged. No exception. If no independent verifier exists in scope, escalation assigns the Quality Manager or Quality Director as verifier.
GEN-BR-004 Platform Administrators shall have no access to tenant quality content (records, documents, evidence, reports, dashboards). Structural: platform roles carry no tenant claims; RLS denies all tenant rows; PLT UI contains no tenant-content views. Attempts are security-logged and alerted. None. Support access follows the P-32 per-session tenant-grant procedure instead.
GEN-BR-005 Auditors shall be independent of the audited activity: an internal auditor shall not audit their own department or work; external auditor access shall be read-only, grant-listed and time-boxed. Audit team assignment validates auditor org-unit against audit scope; External Auditor accounts auto-expire and cannot receive write permissions. Independence conflict requires Lead Auditor to reassign; no override. Grant-list extensions require Quality Director approval, audited.
GEN-BR-006 Security-sensitive administration (role grants, workflow definition changes, SoD configuration, retention-policy changes) shall follow maker-checker: initiated by one administrator, confirmed by a different one before taking effect. Two-step pending-change queue in TEN/IAM; the initiator cannot confirm their own change; unconfirmed changes expire after a configurable period. Single-admin tenants must nominate a second checker (e.g. Quality Director) before such changes can be made; emergency break-glass changes require post-hoc review within 72 hours (proposed target — pending business confirmation).
GEN-BR-007 A Document Controller shall not approve the technical content of a controlled document they authored; editorial release and technical approval are distinct steps held by different users. DOC approval routes require at least one technical approver who is not the author or the releasing controller. Per-route waiver as in GEN-BR-002, Quality Director approval required.
GEN-BR-008 A complaint shall not be closed by the user who performed its investigation; closure approval rests with the Quality Manager or Quality Director. CMP closure action excludes the investigation performer; closure requires A-tier role. None. Absence of the approver is handled via delegation (§13.2), never by relaxing the rule.
GEN-BR-009 A trainer shall not record or assess their own training completion or competency; a user shall not sign their own competency verification. TRN assessment forms exclude self-assessment for qualification-bearing items; system rejects trainer = trainee submissions. Self-paced read-and-understand acknowledgements are exempt by design (acknowledgement, not competency assessment).
GEN-BR-010 Permissions gated by a competency (e.g. approver, auditor, trainer qualifications) shall be automatically withheld while the competency is lapsed, failed or expired; delegation shall not bypass this. Authorization service checks live competency flags from TRN at action time; nightly reconciliation closes any event-delivery gaps (see row 12 of Table 12-1). Temporary provisional qualification may be granted by the Quality Manager with an expiry date; provisional status is displayed on all affected approvals.

13.5 User & Permission Model Diagram

Figure 13-1 shows how a user's effective access to a quality record is derived: role definitions (RBAC) are assigned at an organizational scope, then filtered by attribute-based restrictions, all inside the tenant's row-level-security boundary. Platform and external identities sit outside that boundary with structurally limited paths in.

14 Integration Requirements

NT.QMS operates inside an existing enterprise landscape. It must consume identity, employee and master data from systems of record, publish quality events and analytics data to downstream consumers, and deliver notifications through the organization's approved channels. This section defines the integration architecture, the catalogue of supported integrations, and the general functional requirements that apply to every integration regardless of endpoint.

14.1 Integration Architecture Overview

NT.QMS follows an API-first integration architecture. Every capability exposed in the user interface is also available through versioned REST APIs (URI-versioned, e.g. /api/v1/…) published behind an API gateway that enforces authentication, authorization, request throttling, payload size limits and TLS termination. No external system connects directly to the application database.

  • Authentication. All machine-to-machine API access authenticates with OIDC / OAuth 2.0 (client-credentials flow) issued by the configured identity provider; interactive SSO uses OIDC authorization-code flow or SAML 2.0. Every integration runs under a dedicated service identity (persona P-31 Integration Service Account) with least-privilege, tenant-scoped permissions.
  • Webhooks. Outbound event delivery uses HTTPS webhooks with signed payloads (HMAC-SHA-256 signature header computed with a per-subscription secret), an event id, event type, tenant id, schema version and occurrence timestamp. Consumers must verify the signature; NT.QMS rotates webhook secrets on demand per tenant.
  • Reliable messaging. Outbound events are written to a transactional outbox table in the same database transaction as the business change and dispatched asynchronously; inbound messages land in an inbox table and are processed exactly once per (source, message id). This guarantees no event is lost or double-applied when a process crashes mid-operation.
  • Idempotency. All mutating inbound API calls accept an Idempotency-Key header; replays with the same key return the original result without re-executing the operation. Outbound webhook events carry a unique event id so consumers can de-duplicate.
  • Retry & dead-letter handling. Failed deliveries are retried with exponential backoff plus jitter (proposed schedule: 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, 1 h, 6 h, 24 h — proposed target — pending business confirmation). After the final attempt the message moves to a per-tenant dead-letter queue visible to Tenant Administrators, who can inspect, re-drive or discard entries; every re-drive and discard is audited.
  • Per-tenant configuration & credentials. Every integration is enabled, configured and credentialed per tenant. Endpoint URLs, mappings and schedules are stored as tenant configuration; secrets (client secrets, API keys, SMTP passwords, signing keys) are stored only in the platform secrets store, encrypted at rest, never returned by any API, never written to logs, and referenced by handle from configuration records.
  • Isolation. Integration processing always executes under an explicit tenant context derived from trusted claims or the owning subscription record — never from request bodies. Any cross-tenant addressing attempt is denied and security-logged (see Section 18).
Note: Integration endpoints, protocols and mappings named in this section describe the required NT.QMS capability. The concrete counterpart products at [Client Organization Name] are recorded per tenant during implementation.

14.4 General Integration Functional Requirements

The following requirements apply to every integration in the catalogue, in addition to any endpoint-specific behavior described in §14.3.

IDRequirementPriorityVerification
INT-FR-001 The system shall validate every inbound payload (API, file, webhook) against a published, versioned schema before processing; payloads failing validation shall be rejected (API) or quarantined (batch) with a machine-readable error code and shall never partially update business records. Must Submit malformed payloads per interface; verify rejection/quarantine, error code, and zero record changes.
INT-FR-002 The system shall log every integration exchange (direction, endpoint, tenant, correlation id, payload size, outcome, latency, retry count) in a queryable integration log, excluding secret values and, for notification channels, excluding message bodies containing personal data. Must Inspect logs after test exchanges; confirm required fields present and secrets absent.
INT-FR-003 The system shall apply the configured retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter) to failed outbound deliveries and shall move exhausted messages to a per-tenant dead-letter queue with re-drive and discard actions restricted to Tenant Administrators; both actions shall be audited with reason. Must Simulate endpoint outage; observe backoff schedule, DLQ placement, audited re-drive.
INT-FR-004 The system shall produce a reconciliation report for every scheduled sync run (INT-001, INT-004, INT-005, INT-007, INT-014) listing records received, created, updated, deactivated, quarantined and errored, retrievable by Tenant Administrators for at least 12 months (proposed target — pending business confirmation). Must Run sync with known deltas; verify report counts match injected changes.
INT-FR-005 The system shall enforce data ownership: fields mastered in an external system (directory identity, HR employee data, ERP master data) shall be read-only in NT.QMS and shall display their source system and last-sync timestamp; local overrides, where allowed, shall be flagged and reported. Must Attempt edit of synced fields via UI and API; verify denial and source labeling.
INT-FR-006 The system shall store all integration secrets exclusively in the platform secrets store, encrypted at rest, scoped per tenant, write-only from the administration UI (values never redisplayed), and shall support secret rotation without service restart. Must Verify API/UI never returns secret values; rotate a secret and confirm uninterrupted operation.
INT-FR-007 The system shall accept an Idempotency-Key header on all mutating public API endpoints and shall return the original response, without side effects, for any replay of the same key within the retention window (proposed: 24 hours — pending business confirmation). Must Replay a create request with the same key; verify single record and identical response.
INT-FR-008 The system shall version all public APIs and webhook event schemas; breaking changes shall require a new major version, and the previous major version shall remain available for a deprecation period of at least 12 months with deprecation headers/notices (proposed target — pending business confirmation). Should Review API version negotiation; confirm deprecated version still serves with warning headers.
INT-FR-009 The system shall provide an integration health dashboard per tenant (last run, success rate, queue and DLQ depth, secret/certificate expiry warnings) and shall raise configurable alerts to Tenant Administrators via INT-008/INT-009 on failure conditions. Must Induce failures per integration; verify dashboard status change and alert delivery.
INT-FR-010 The system shall enforce privacy minimization on outbound channels: SMS and third-party messaging payloads shall contain only record identifiers and action prompts, never personal data of third parties or confidential record content; BI exports shall exclude fields marked confidential unless the export definition is explicitly approved by the Tenant Administrator (approval audited). Must Inspect generated payloads/datasets for excluded field classes; verify approval gate and audit.

15 Reporting Requirements

NT.QMS reporting turns controlled quality records into decision-ready information for executives, operational managers, quality teams and auditors. The reporting subsystem is role-based end to end: a report never shows a user data that the user could not open directly in the source module, and drill-down always lands on records the user is permitted to view. All catalogued reports share a common engine providing:

  • Access control — every report is assigned to roles; row-level results are trimmed by the viewer's organization, department and confidentiality permissions.
  • Saved filters and views — users save named filter/grouping combinations privately or share them with their department; shared views are read-only to recipients.
  • Scheduling — authorized users schedule reports (daily, weekly, monthly, or cron-style custom) for email distribution to named users or roles; the delivered content is rendered under the recipient's permissions, not the scheduler's.
  • Export formats — on-screen (interactive), print-optimized layout, PDF, PDF/A-2b where the catalogue requires archival fidelity, Excel (.xlsx) and CSV (UTF-8). Exports carry generation timestamp, generating user, tenant, applied filters and page numbering.
  • Drill-down / drill-through — aggregate figures link to the underlying record list, and list rows link to the source record in its module, preserving filters.
  • Data refresh — operational and compliance reports read live transactional data; trend/analytics reports may read from a reporting replica or pre-aggregated datasets refreshed at a documented interval; every report displays its "data as of" timestamp.

15.6 General Reporting Requirements
IDRequirementPriorityVerification
REP-FR-001 The system shall enforce role-based and row-level access on every report: results shall be trimmed to the viewer's tenant, organization, department and confidentiality permissions, and drill-down shall never expose a record the viewer cannot open in the source module. Must Run each catalogued report as users with different scopes; verify trimming and drill-down denial.
REP-FR-002 The system shall visibly label any report output produced from a non-production tenant, training tenant or demonstration dataset with a persistent "SAMPLE DATA — NOT FOR QUALITY DECISIONS" watermark on screen and in every export format. Must Generate reports in a training tenant; verify watermark on screen, PDF, Excel and print output.
REP-FR-003 The system shall audit every report export and scheduled distribution (user/recipients, report, filters, format, row count, timestamp) and expose this in RPT-CO-10. Must Export and schedule reports; verify complete entries in export history.
REP-FR-004 The system shall render all §15.3 compliance reports, the Management Review package (RPT-EX-10) and the Compliance Status Report (RPT-EX-08) to PDF/A-2b with embedded fonts, generation metadata and page-of-pages numbering suitable for long-term archival. Must Validate exported files with a PDF/A conformance checker.
REP-FR-005 The system shall allow users to save named filter/grouping views per report (private or shared to department), set a personal default view, and shall audit creation, sharing and deletion of shared views. Must Create, share, apply and delete saved views; verify persistence and audit entries.
REP-FR-006 The system shall provide schedule management for report distribution: create/pause/resume/ delete schedules, recipient lists by user or role, per-recipient permission rendering, delivery via INT-008, failure notification to the schedule owner, and automatic suspension of schedules owned by deactivated users with administrator alert. Must Exercise schedule lifecycle including owner deactivation; verify behavior and alerts.
REP-FR-007 The system shall display on every report the "data as of" timestamp, applied filters, generating user and tenant; exports shall embed the same metadata in headers/footers or file properties. Must Inspect on-screen and exported outputs for complete metadata.
REP-FR-008 The system shall localize report labels, dates and numbers to the viewer's UI language (English, Arabic with RTL layout, French) and tenant timezone, while keeping stored values and record identifiers unchanged. Must Render the same report in all three languages; verify labels, RTL layout and timezone conversion.
REP-FR-009 The system shall paginate and stream large report results; interactive reports shall return the first page within the performance targets defined in Section 18, and exports exceeding a configurable row threshold shall run as background jobs with completion notification. Should Generate large-volume test datasets; measure first-page latency and verify background export flow.
REP-FR-010 The system shall prevent modification of catalogued compliance report definitions by tenant users; tenant-defined custom reports shall be visually distinguished, version-controlled, and shall never bypass access trimming (REP-FR-001). Must Attempt to edit a compliance report definition; create a custom report and verify trimming applies.

16 Dashboard Requirements

This section defines the role-oriented dashboards delivered by NT.QMS. Dashboards are the primary daily entry point for each persona: they surface the quality workload (tasks, approvals, overdue items), key performance indicators (KPIs), and trend analytics scoped to the records the signed-in user is permitted to see. Dashboard widgets are read-only visualizations; all data changes occur in the owning module reached by drill-down. Dashboards complement, and do not replace, the reporting catalogue defined in Section 15 and the executive analytics module 11.4 (DSH). Requirement IDs in this section use the prefix DSHB to avoid collision with module DSH functional requirements.

16.1 General Dashboard Requirements
DSHB-FR-001 Role-based default dashboard provisioning MustCore
Requirement
The system shall assign every user a default dashboard layout derived from the user's primary role (Sections 16.3–16.14). Users holding multiple roles shall receive the dashboard of their highest-privilege quality role and may switch between the dashboards of any role they hold via a dashboard selector.
Rationale
Each persona has a distinct daily workload; a single generic dashboard forces navigation overhead and hides overdue work.
Actor
All authenticated users; Tenant Administrator (default-layout configuration).
Preconditions / Trigger
User authenticates and lands on the home route.
Validation & Exceptions
If no role-specific dashboard is defined, the Standard Employee dashboard (16.14) is shown. A user with no module permissions sees only the personal task and training widgets.
Audit
Changes to tenant default layouts are audited (who, when, before/after layout definition).
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSHB-01
Related
DSHB-FR-002, Section 13
DSHB-FR-002 Role- and permission-based widget visibility MustCore
Requirement
The system shall render a widget only when the user holds view permission for the underlying module and record scope. Widget data shall be computed against the caller's effective permissions and tenant/organization scope; a widget shall never display counts, titles, or values that include records the user cannot open. Widgets the user is not entitled to shall be omitted entirely (not rendered greyed-out).
Rationale
Prevents information leakage through aggregate counts and preserves need-to-know confidentiality (e.g. complaint details, HR-linked training records).
Actor
All authenticated users.
Preconditions / Trigger
Dashboard load or widget refresh.
Validation & Exceptions
Permission changes take effect on the next widget refresh at the latest. A request for an unentitled widget's data via API returns HTTP 403 and is security-logged.
Audit
Denied widget data requests are recorded in the security log with user, widget id, and tenant context.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSHB-02
Related
SRC-FR-007, Section 13
DSHB-FR-003 Personalization within administrative limits ShouldConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall allow a user to add, remove, resize, and reorder widgets on their own dashboard from the catalogue of widgets permitted to their roles, subject to limits: maximum 20 widgets per dashboard and maximum 5 saved personal layouts per user (proposed targets — pending business confirmation). A one-click "Reset to role default" action shall restore the tenant-defined default layout. Personalization shall never grant access to widgets outside the user's permissions.
Rationale
Different departments emphasize different indicators; limits protect performance and support supportability.
Actor
All authenticated users; Tenant Administrator (may disable personalization per role).
Preconditions / Trigger
User opens dashboard edit mode.
Validation & Exceptions
Attempting to exceed the widget limit is blocked with an explanatory message. Widgets whose permission is later revoked are silently removed at next load.
Audit
Personal layout changes are stored per user; tenant-level disabling of personalization is audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSHB-01
Related
DSHB-FR-002
DSHB-FR-004 Dashboard performance MustCore
Requirement
The system shall render the dashboard shell within 2 seconds and complete loading of all default widgets within 3 seconds at the 95th percentile under the reference load defined in Section 18 (proposed targets — pending business confirmation). Widgets shall load independently and asynchronously so that one slow widget does not block the others, and each widget shall show a loading indicator until populated.
Rationale
The dashboard is the highest-traffic page; slow load directly reduces adoption.
Actor
All authenticated users.
Preconditions / Trigger
Dashboard load, filter change, refresh.
Validation & Exceptions
Widgets exceeding a 10-second data timeout render the widget error state (16.2) rather than blocking the page.
Audit
Not applicable (performance telemetry captured per Section 18).
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSHB-03
Related
DSHB-FR-005
DSHB-FR-005 Per-tenant, permission-aware caching MustCore
Requirement
The system shall cache computed widget aggregates server-side with cache keys that include at minimum tenant id, widget id, role/permission scope hash, and active filter values. Cached entries shall never be served across tenants or across users with different permission scopes. Default cache validity is 5 minutes for operational widgets and 60 minutes for trend widgets (proposed targets — pending business confirmation); manual refresh bypasses the cache.
Rationale
Aggregate queries are expensive at scale; caching must not undermine multi-tenant isolation or need-to-know visibility.
Actor
System; Platform Administrator (cache tuning).
Preconditions / Trigger
Widget data request.
Validation & Exceptions
Tenant context is derived from trusted claims only; a cache key missing tenant id is a defect condition and the request falls back to a live query.
Audit
Cache configuration changes at platform level are audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSHB-02
Related
Section 18, SRC-BR-001
DSHB-FR-006 Global dashboard filters MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide a global filter bar on every dashboard with: date range (preset ranges plus custom from/to), organization, branch, department, and site. Filter options shall be trimmed to the user's assigned scope. Applying a filter shall re-scope all widgets that support it; widgets not affected by a filter shall indicate "filter not applicable". The last-used filter set shall persist per user per dashboard.
Rationale
Multi-site tenants need consistent scoping without configuring each widget separately.
Actor
All authenticated users.
Preconditions / Trigger
User changes a filter value.
Validation & Exceptions
An invalid custom date range (from > to) is rejected inline. A saved filter referencing a unit the user no longer scopes to is reset to the user's default scope with a notice.
Audit
Not audited (user preference data).
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSHB-04
Related
DSHB-FR-007
DSHB-FR-007 Drill-down with preserved context and permissions MustCore
Requirement
The system shall make every KPI, card, chart segment, alert, and task row clickable, navigating to a pre-filtered list view in the owning module that reproduces the widget's scope (filters, status, date range). The target list applies the same permission trimming as direct navigation; if the user cannot access the underlying list, the element shall not be rendered as clickable.
Rationale
Dashboards must lead to action; a count without a path to the records behind it has no operational value.
Actor
All authenticated users.
Preconditions / Trigger
User clicks a widget element.
Validation & Exceptions
If records changed between widget computation and drill-down, the list shows current data and may differ from the cached count; the list header shows its own refreshed timestamp.
Audit
Access to confidential record lists via drill-down is audited identically to direct access.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSHB-04
Related
DSHB-FR-002
DSHB-FR-008 Refresh behavior, staleness, and failure indication MustCore
Requirement
The system shall display a "last refreshed" timestamp per widget, provide a per-widget and whole-dashboard manual refresh action, and auto-refresh operational widgets at the frequency defined per dashboard in 16.3–16.14 (tenant-configurable within 1–60 minutes). When a widget's data request fails, the widget shall show the standard error state (16.2) with a retry action while retaining the last successfully loaded values marked as stale.
Rationale
Users acting on overdue-item counts must know how current the numbers are.
Actor
All authenticated users; Tenant Administrator (refresh configuration).
Preconditions / Trigger
Timer elapse, manual refresh, transient backend failure.
Validation & Exceptions
Auto-refresh is suspended while the browser tab is hidden and resumes with an immediate refresh when the tab becomes visible.
Audit
Tenant refresh-frequency configuration changes are audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-DSHB-03
Related
DSHB-FR-004, DSHB-FR-005

16.2 Common Widget Conventions

The role dashboard definitions below reuse the following standard behaviors; per-dashboard tables state only role-specific specializations.

ConventionStandard behavior
