16.16 Dashboard Acceptance Criteria

AC-DSHB-01 — Role default and personalization limit

  • Given a user whose primary role is Quality Manager and whose dashboard already contains 20 widgets,
  • When the user signs in and then attempts to add a 21st widget in edit mode,
  • Then the Quality Manager dashboard (16.6) is shown by default and the add action is blocked with a message stating the 20-widget limit, with no partial save.

AC-DSHB-02 — No aggregate leakage across permission scope

  • Given two users in the same tenant where user A may view confidential complaints and user B may not, and 5 of 12 open complaints are confidential,
  • When each user loads the complaints widget within the same cache validity window,
  • Then user A sees a count of 12 and user B sees a count of 7, demonstrating that cached aggregates are keyed by permission scope and confidential records are excluded for user B.

AC-DSHB-03 — Independent widget failure

  • Given a dashboard with 8 widgets where the data source of one trend widget is unavailable,
  • When the user loads the dashboard,
  • Then the 7 healthy widgets populate normally within the performance target, and the failed widget shows the standard error state with a Retry action and its stale last-known values greyed out.

AC-DSHB-04 — Drill-down preserves filter context

  • Given a Quality Manager dashboard filtered to Branch "Main", Department "Production", last 90 days,
  • When the user clicks the "Open NCRs" KPI showing 14,
  • Then the NCR list opens pre-filtered to the same branch, department, date range, and open statuses, and the list result count matches the KPI value at the moment of computation or displays its own refreshed timestamp.

17 Search & Traceability

This section specifies system-wide search and end-to-end traceability across all NT.QMS modules. Search gives users fast, permission-safe access to records and documents; traceability links every quality record to its causes, consequences, and supporting evidence so that a complete chain (e.g. complaint → nonconformance → CAPA → verification) can be demonstrated to auditors and inspectors in support of BUS-OBJ-005 and BUS-OBJ-010. All search and traceability functions operate strictly within the caller's tenant and permission scope.

17.1 Functional Requirements
SRC-FR-001 Global search across permitted records MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide a global search box available from every page that searches record numbers, titles, descriptions, and key metadata across all modules (DOC, NCR, CAPA, CMP, AUD, TRN, EQP, RSK, MRV) in a single query, returning results grouped by module with record number, title, status, owner, and last-modified date. Exact record-number input (e.g. "CAPA-2026-0095") shall rank the matching record first and offer direct-open.
Rationale
Users frequently know a record number or fragment of a title but not its module location.
Actor
All authenticated users.
Preconditions / Trigger
User enters at least 2 characters and submits or pauses typing (type-ahead suggestions after 300 ms, proposed target — pending business confirmation).
Validation & Exceptions
Queries are sanitized against injection; a query matching zero permitted records returns an explicit "no results" state, identical whether restricted records matched or nothing matched (SRC-FR-007).
Audit
Search queries are logged with user, tenant, and timestamp for usage analytics; query logs are tenant-scoped.
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-01
Related
SRC-FR-007, SRC-BR-001
SRC-FR-002 Module-specific search MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide, in every module list view, a module-scoped search that combines free text with the module's structured fields (status, type, owner, dates, classification, site) and returns results in the module's list grid with sorting and column selection preserved.
Rationale
Module specialists (e.g. Document Controllers) work within one register and need field-aware precision beyond global search.
Actor
All users with module view permission.
Preconditions / Trigger
User opens a module list and enters criteria.
Validation & Exceptions
Field operators appropriate to type (equals, contains, before/after, between, in-list). Invalid combinations (e.g. date "between" with one bound) are rejected inline.
Audit
Not individually audited beyond standard query logging.
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-02
Related
SRC-FR-004
SRC-FR-003 Full-text search including attachment text extraction ShouldCore
Requirement
The system shall index the extractable text of uploaded attachments (PDF with text layer, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, plain text) and include attachment content in full-text search, indicating in the result whether the match occurred in metadata or attachment content. Indexing shall occur asynchronously after upload and virus scan; a record is searchable by metadata immediately and by attachment content within 5 minutes of upload (proposed target — pending business confirmation).
Rationale
The substantive content of SOPs, certificates, and investigation reports lives in attachments.
Actor
All authenticated users; System (indexing pipeline).
Preconditions / Trigger
Attachment upload completes and passes virus scan.
Validation & Exceptions
Unextractable or corrupt files are flagged "content not indexed" on the attachment without failing the upload. Indexing failures are retried and surfaced in the tenant admin job monitor.
Audit
Index pipeline failures are logged; no content is written to logs.
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-03
Related
SRC-BR-003
Optional future scope: OCR of scanned/image-only files (scanned PDFs, TIFF/JPEG certificates) to make their text searchable is not part of the base scope. If enabled in a later phase, OCR output shall be stored per tenant, inherit the source record's permissions, and be clearly marked as machine-extracted text.
SRC-FR-004 Advanced filters and query composition MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide an advanced search panel (global and per module) supporting multiple criteria combined with AND logic and per-field OR value lists, covering at minimum: module, record status, organization/branch/department/site, owner/assignee, created/modified/due date ranges, priority/severity, classification, and tag values. The active filter set shall be visible as removable chips above the results.
Rationale
Audit preparation and management reporting require precise, repeatable record slicing.
Actor
All authenticated users.
Preconditions / Trigger
User opens the advanced search panel.
Validation & Exceptions
Filters referencing values outside the user's scope return no results rather than an error; contradictory criteria yield an empty result with the criteria still displayed for correction.
Audit
Standard query logging.
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-02
Related
SRC-FR-005
SRC-FR-005 Saved searches ShouldCore
Requirement
The system shall allow a user to save a named search (criteria set, not results) for reuse, list and manage their saved searches (maximum 25 per user, proposed target — pending business confirmation), and re-execute one in a single action. Saved searches store criteria only; results are always evaluated against current data and current permissions at execution time.
Rationale
Recurring work queues (e.g. "my overdue CAPA actions", "docs due for review this quarter") should not be rebuilt daily.
Actor
All authenticated users.
Preconditions / Trigger
User executes a search and chooses "Save search".
Validation & Exceptions
Duplicate names per user are rejected. A saved search referencing a field later removed from configuration executes with that criterion ignored and a warning shown.
Audit
Not audited (personal preference data).
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-02
Related
SRC-FR-006
Note: Shared/team saved searches (published by a Quality Manager to a role or department) are classified Could and, if implemented, execute under each consumer's own permissions.
SRC-FR-006 Recent searches and recently viewed records ShouldCore
Requirement
The system shall show the user's last 10 search queries and last 10 viewed records as one-click shortcuts in the global search dropdown, stored per user per tenant, with a "clear history" action. Entries referencing records the user can no longer access are removed from display.
Rationale
Users repeatedly return to the same handful of records during an investigation or audit.
Actor
All authenticated users.
Preconditions / Trigger
User focuses the empty global search box.
Validation & Exceptions
History is not shared across users and is excluded from tenant data exports.
Audit
Not audited (personal preference data).
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-02
Related
SRC-FR-005
SRC-FR-007 Permission-trimmed results without leakage MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall evaluate every search result against the caller's effective permissions before returning it. Records the user may not view shall be omitted entirely: no title, snippet, record number, count contribution, or "restricted result" placeholder shall be returned. Result counts and pagination shall be computed over permitted records only, and this trimming shall apply identically to the UI, API, type-ahead suggestions, and exports.
Rationale
A confidential complaint's title alone (e.g. naming an employee) is a disclosure; search must not become a side channel around record permissions.
Actor
System (enforced on every search path).
Preconditions / Trigger
Any search execution.
Validation & Exceptions
Attempted direct-open of a restricted record from a stale link returns a generic "not found or not accessible" response (no existence confirmation) and is security-logged.
Audit
Denied direct-open attempts are security-logged with user, tenant, and requested id.
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-01
Related
SRC-BR-002, SRC-BR-004
SRC-FR-008 Record relationships and cross-module links MustCore
Requirement
The system shall support typed, directional relationships between records within a tenant (e.g. "escalated to", "addressed by", "references", "supersedes", "verifies"), created automatically by module workflows (e.g. NCR → CAPA creation) and manually by permitted users. Each link stores type, direction, creator, timestamp, and optional comment; manual link creation and removal are audited and removal requires a reason.
Rationale
Relationships are the raw material of traceability chains and the related-records panel.
Actor
System (workflow links); users with edit permission on at least one linked record (manual links).
Preconditions / Trigger
Workflow event or manual "Link record" action.
Validation & Exceptions
Both endpoints must belong to the same tenant; self-links and duplicate identical links are rejected; linking to a record the user cannot view is impossible (picker is permission-trimmed).
Audit
Link create/remove with who, when, link type, both record ids, and reason (on removal).
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-04
Related
SRC-FR-009, Section 12
SRC-FR-009 Traceability chains MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall compute and display, from any record, its full traceability chain by traversing relationships in both directions across modules, presented as an expandable tree and as a visual graph (Figure 17-1). Supported chains include at minimum: finding-to-CAPA (audit finding → CAPA → actions → effectiveness verification), complaint-to-investigation (complaint → investigation → NCR/CAPA → customer response), document-to-training (document revision → retraining assignments → completions), equipment-to-NC (out-of-tolerance event → NCR → impact assessment), audit-to-record (audit → findings → CAPAs → closure evidence), and requirement-to-test chains within validation (Section 23, Section 24). Traversal depth is limited to 10 levels with cycle detection (proposed target — pending business confirmation).
Rationale
Inspectors routinely ask "show me everything connected to this complaint"; assembling the chain manually is slow and error-prone (BUS-OBJ-005).
Actor
All users with view permission on the starting record.
Preconditions / Trigger
User opens the "Traceability" view on a record.
Validation & Exceptions
Nodes the user may not view are omitted along with their onward branches; the chain displays a neutral "1 or more linked records not shown due to permissions" summary flag at the tenant-configurable discretion of the Quality Director (default: flag shown; wording never reveals module, count beyond "1 or more", or titles).
Audit
Traceability views of confidential records follow the same audit rules as opening the record.
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-04, AC-SRC-05
Related
SRC-FR-008, SRC-FR-011
SRC-FR-010 Related-records panel on every record MustCore
Requirement
The system shall display on every record detail page a "Related records" panel listing all directly linked records the user may view, grouped by relationship type, each showing record number, title, module, status, and link creation date, with one-click navigation and (for permitted users) link management actions. The panel shall indicate the total number of visible related records and load without blocking the main record view.
Rationale
Context at the point of work: a CAPA owner must see the source NCR and finding without leaving the record.
Actor
All users with view permission on the record.
Preconditions / Trigger
Record detail page load.
Validation & Exceptions
Panel failure degrades gracefully (panel-local error with retry); the record itself remains fully usable.
Audit
None beyond link-management auditing (SRC-FR-008).
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-04
Related
SRC-FR-009
SRC-FR-011 Export of traceability chains ShouldCompliance
Requirement
The system shall export a computed traceability chain as (a) a structured tabular export (Excel/CSV: source record, relationship type, target record, statuses, dates, owners) and (b) a printable PDF containing the visual graph, the record list, generation timestamp, generating user, applied scope, and the permission-omission flag state of SRC-FR-009. Exports contain only records the exporting user may view and carry the document classification marking of the most restrictive included record.
Rationale
Audit and inspection evidence packages require portable traceability proof.
Actor
Users with export permission (per module permission matrices in Section 11).
Preconditions / Trigger
User invokes Export on a traceability view.
Validation & Exceptions
Exports exceeding 1,000 nodes are generated asynchronously with notification on completion (proposed target — pending business confirmation).
Audit
Every traceability export is audited: user, starting record, node count, format, timestamp.
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-05
Related
SRC-FR-009, Section 15
SRC-FR-012 Search index management and tenant partitioning MustCore
Requirement
The system shall maintain search indexes in per-tenant partitions such that every query executes against exactly one tenant's partition, selected from trusted token claims. Index entries shall be updated within 60 seconds of a record create/update/delete (proposed target — pending business confirmation), removed immediately on hard archival/purge per Section 21, and a per-tenant full reindex shall be executable by the Platform Administrator without affecting other tenants' search availability.
Rationale
Physical partition selection by trusted claim eliminates the class of cross-tenant leakage bugs that filter-based approaches permit.
Actor
System; P-01 Platform Administrator (reindex operations).
Preconditions / Trigger
Record change events; administrative reindex request.
Validation & Exceptions
A query that cannot resolve a valid tenant partition is rejected (never falls back to a cross-tenant search) and security-logged. During reindex, the tenant's search serves the existing index until cutover.
Audit
Reindex operations audited with tenant, initiator, duration, and outcome.
Acceptance criteria
AC-SRC-06
Related
SRC-BR-001, Section 18

17.2 Business Rules — Confidentiality & Tenant Isolation
Rule IDRuleEnforcementException handling
SRC-BR-001 Search indexes are physically partitioned per tenant; a query executes against exactly one partition resolved from trusted authentication claims, never from request parameters or body. Index pipeline writes to the owning tenant's partition only; query layer resolves partition from token claims; integration/service accounts (P-31) are bound to a single tenant partition. Unresolvable or mismatched tenant context: query rejected with a generic error, event security-logged, and repeated occurrences alert the Platform Administrator. No cross-partition fallback exists.
SRC-BR-002 Records classified Confidential or Restricted are indexed with their access-control descriptors; their titles, snippets, and existence are returned only to users satisfying those descriptors. Permission trimming applied at query time on every path (UI, API, suggestions, exports) per SRC-FR-007; classification changes trigger index-entry updates within the SRC-FR-012 latency target. If descriptor evaluation fails for an entry, the entry is excluded (fail-closed) and the evaluation failure is logged for investigation.
SRC-BR-003 Attachment-derived index content inherits the permissions and classification of the owning record and version; content of superseded document versions is searchable only to users permitted to view version history. Index entries carry owning record id, version, and classification; version-visibility rules of 11.5 applied at query time. Orphaned attachment index entries (owning record purged) are deleted by a daily reconciliation job; hits on orphans are suppressed in the interim.
SRC-BR-004 Search must not confirm the existence of an inaccessible record: zero-result responses, error messages, response timing, and pagination totals are indistinguishable between "no match" and "matches exist but are all restricted". Uniform response shaping in the search service; counts computed post-trimming only. Not applicable — behavior is unconditional. Verified in security testing (Section 23).
SRC-BR-005 Traceability traversal never crosses a tenant boundary; relationship creation between records of different tenants is impossible at the data layer. Relationship table carries a single tenant id enforced by constraint and PostgreSQL RLS; traversal queries are tenant-bound. Any attempted cross-tenant link via API returns 403, is security-logged, and is included in the tenant security report.
SRC-BR-006 Personal data in search: complainant identities, trainee assessment scores, and HR-linked fields are indexed only in restricted descriptors and are excluded from type-ahead suggestion text. Field-level index policy per module data dictionary; suggestion generator uses title/record-number fields only. Fields added to modules via configuration default to "not suggestion-eligible" until explicitly reviewed by the Tenant Administrator.
SRC-BR-007 Archived records remain searchable (flagged "Archived") to users holding archive-view permission; purged records are irreversibly removed from all index partitions and relationship tables per Section 21. Archival workflow updates the index flag; purge workflow deletes index entries and links in the same transaction boundary as record purge. Purge verification job confirms zero residual index entries; residuals raise a platform incident.
SRC-BR-008 External users (P-29 External Auditor, P-30 External Service Provider) can search only within the record collections explicitly shared with their engagement; global search for these roles operates on that shared subset. Engagement scope evaluated as an additional mandatory filter on every query from an external account. Expired engagements immediately reduce the searchable set to empty; the account retains sign-in until deactivated per 11.3.

17.3 Visual Traceability Example

The following graph illustrates a typical cross-module traceability chain as rendered by the traceability view (SRC-FR-009): a customer complaint escalated to a nonconformance, addressed by a CAPA whose actions drive a document revision and retraining, with side links to the audit finding and risk register entries connected to the same issue.

17.4 Acceptance Criteria

AC-SRC-01 — Restricted records are invisible in search

  • Given a tenant containing a confidential complaint titled with an employee's name, and a user without confidential-complaint permission,
  • When the user searches globally for that employee's name and also pastes the complaint's exact record number,
  • Then both queries return the standard "no results" state with no title, snippet, count, or placeholder revealing the record's existence, and the direct record-number attempt is security-logged.

AC-SRC-02 — Saved search executes with current permissions

  • Given a user with a saved search "Open NCRs — Site B" who is later re-scoped to Site A only,
  • When the user re-executes the saved search,
  • Then the search runs against current data and current permissions, returns zero Site B records, and displays the criteria chips so the user can see why the result is empty.

AC-SRC-03 — Attachment content becomes searchable

  • Given a Word investigation report containing the unique phrase "torque wrench batch 7741" uploaded to an NCR and passing virus scan,
  • When a permitted user searches for "torque wrench batch 7741" after the indexing latency window,
  • Then the NCR appears in results with an indication that the match occurred in attachment content, and a user without permission on that NCR gets no result for the same query.

AC-SRC-04 — Workflow-created links appear in the related-records panel

  • Given a CAPA created from NCR-2026-0387 via the NCR escalation workflow,
  • When a permitted user opens either record,
  • Then the related-records panel on each shows the typed link to the other ("addressed by" / "escalated from") with creation timestamp, and one-click navigation opens the counterpart record.

AC-SRC-05 — Traceability chain and export completeness

  • Given the chain of Figure 17-1 existing as live linked records, and a Quality Manager permitted to view all of them,
  • When the manager opens the traceability view on the complaint and exports it to PDF,
  • Then the view shows all nine linked records across five modules within 10 traversal levels, and the PDF contains the graph, record list, generating user, timestamp, and the permission-omission flag state, and the export event is audited.

AC-SRC-06 — Tenant isolation of search indexes

  • Given tenants T1 and T2 where T2 contains a document titled "Sterilization Validation Master Plan" and T1 contains no similar record,
  • When a T1 user searches for "Sterilization Validation Master Plan", including via direct API calls attempting to supply T2's tenant id as a parameter,
  • Then no T2 result is returned in any response, the parameter-supplied tenant id is ignored in favor of token claims, the mismatched attempt is security-logged, and a concurrent full reindex of T2 does not interrupt T1 search availability.

18 Non-Functional Requirements

This section defines the measurable quality attributes that NT.QMS must satisfy in addition to the functional behavior specified in sections 11–17. Each requirement carries a unique identifier, a measurable target, and a verification method so that compliance can be objectively demonstrated during validation (see Section 23 — Validation & Testing). Non-functional requirements apply platform-wide unless a requirement explicitly states a narrower scope.

Note: Where a requirement states a numeric threshold, the threshold is a contractual baseline once approved. Until then, all numeric values in this section are proposed baselines and are flagged as pending business confirmation in each subsection.

18.1 Performance

Performance requirements are stated against the reference environment defined in Section 10 (production-grade sizing) under nominal load (concurrent users per PER-NFR-008), measured at the server boundary excluding end-user network latency unless stated otherwise. Percentile targets are measured over rolling 24-hour production windows or a representative load-test run.

Pending business confirmation: All numeric performance targets in this subsection (response times, throughput, upload sizes, concurrency figures, batch windows) are proposed baselines derived from comparable QMS deployments and are pending formal approval by the client during the requirements sign-off workshop.
IDRequirementMeasure / Target (proposed)VerificationPriority
PER-NFR-001 Interactive page response: any standard page (list views, record detail views, forms) shall render server responses within the target percentile latency. P95 ≤ 2.5 s, P99 ≤ 5 s per page request at nominal load Load test + APM production percentiles Must
PER-NFR-002 Search: global and module search queries (see Section 17) shall return the first page of results within the target time for indexed corpora up to the volumes in SCA-NFR-004. P95 ≤ 3 s for result-set page 1 (25 rows) Load test with seeded corpus; production APM Must
PER-NFR-003 Dashboards: executive and module dashboards (see Section 16) shall complete initial load of all widgets, using pre-aggregated data where defined. P95 ≤ 4 s full dashboard load; individual widget refresh P95 ≤ 2 s Load test; synthetic monitoring Must
PER-NFR-004 Interactive report generation: on-demand reports (see Section 15) up to 5,000 rows shall generate synchronously; larger reports shall automatically switch to asynchronous (queued) generation with user notification on completion. Interactive: P95 ≤ 10 s; async threshold: > 5,000 rows or > 10 s estimate Functional test with boundary datasets; load test Must
PER-NFR-005 Scheduled/async reports: queued report jobs shall complete within their SLA and shall not degrade interactive traffic (resource isolation via job concurrency limits). 95% of scheduled reports complete ≤ 15 min from scheduled start; interactive P95 degradation ≤ 10% during report windows Load test with concurrent report execution Should
PER-NFR-006 File upload: attachments shall upload via streaming (no full in-memory buffering) up to the configured per-file size limit; the limit shall be configurable per tenant by the Platform Administrator. Default limit 100 MB per file (configurable 1–500 MB); server memory usage per upload ≤ 32 MB regardless of file size Functional test at limit boundaries; memory profiling Must
PER-NFR-007 File download / attachment retrieval: stored attachments shall begin streaming to the client within the target time-to-first-byte, independent of file size. P95 time-to-first-byte ≤ 2 s Load test; APM Should
PER-NFR-008 Concurrent users: the platform shall sustain the target concurrency without breaching PER-NFR-001..003, where a concurrent user issues at least one request per 60 s. 500 concurrent users per tenant; 5,000 concurrent users platform-wide Load test at 100% and 120% of target Must
PER-NFR-009 API latency: REST API CRUD endpoints (single-record create, read, update, workflow transition) shall meet percentile latency at nominal load, measured server-side. P95 ≤ 500 ms, P99 ≤ 1,000 ms for CRUD; list endpoints P95 ≤ 800 ms (25-row page) Load test; APM percentiles per endpoint group Must
PER-NFR-010 Background jobs and batch windows: recurring jobs (escalation sweeps, notification digests, KPI aggregation, retention sweeps) shall complete within defined SLAs, and heavy batch jobs shall run inside a configurable off-peak window. Escalation/notification sweep cycle ≤ 5 min end-to-end; KPI aggregation ≤ 15 min; retention/archival batch completes within a 4-hour nightly window (default 01:00–05:00 tenant local time, configurable) Job telemetry dashboards; batch runbook test Must

18.4 Security

Security requirements apply to all modules and all interfaces (UI, API, integrations, exports). They align with OWASP ASVS Level 2 and the OWASP Top 10, and support the tenant-data-protection objective BUS-OBJ-015.

Pending business confirmation: Numeric security parameters below (password policy values, lockout thresholds, session lifetimes, rate limits, patch SLAs) are proposed baselines pending approval by the client's information security function; tenant-configurable parameters are noted as such.
IDRequirementMeasure / Target (proposed)VerificationPriority
SEC-NFR-001 Authentication: all access shall require authenticated identity (local credentials or federated SSO per Section 14); no anonymous access to any tenant data or API endpoint except health probes and the login page. 100% of endpoints (excl. health/login/static assets) return 401 for unauthenticated requests Automated endpoint sweep in CI; penetration test Must
SEC-NFR-002 Authorization — backend-enforced, deny-by-default: every API operation shall enforce permission checks server-side against the caller's roles and scopes (Section 13); UI hiding of controls is never the sole control; absence of an explicit grant means denial. 100% of write endpoints covered by authorization tests; zero endpoints relying solely on client-side checks Authorization test suite; code review gate; penetration test Must
SEC-NFR-003 Password policy: local accounts shall enforce configurable complexity, history, and rotation rules; passwords stored only as salted adaptive hashes (e.g. Argon2id or bcrypt, cost tuned to ≥ 250 ms). Default: min length 12, screened against breached-password list, history 5, no forced periodic expiry unless tenant enables it; hash verification cost ≥ 250 ms Configuration test; code review of hashing implementation Must
SEC-NFR-004 Multi-factor authentication: MFA (TOTP; email OTP as fallback) shall be supported and enforceable per tenant, per role, or for privileged roles; MFA shall be mandatory for Platform and Tenant Administrators. MFA enrollment enforced at next login when policy enabled; admin roles cannot disable their own MFA requirement Functional test per policy combination Must
SEC-NFR-005 Session management: sessions shall use secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies or bearer tokens with expiry; idle and absolute timeouts shall be tenant-configurable; users and administrators shall be able to list and revoke active sessions/devices with effect within the stated bound. Default idle timeout 30 min, absolute 12 h (configurable); revocation effective ≤ 60 s; token replay after logout rejected Session lifecycle test; revocation test Must
SEC-NFR-006 Least privilege: default role templates shall grant the minimum permissions needed per persona (Section 13); service and integration accounts (P-31) shall be scoped to specific APIs and tenants and shall not hold interactive-login rights. Role-template review shows no default role with Configure or Delete rights outside admin personas; integration accounts blocked from UI login Permission-matrix review; functional test Must
SEC-NFR-007 Tenant isolation: every tenant-owned row shall carry the tenant id; PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies shall enforce tenant scoping at the database layer in addition to application filters; tenant context shall derive only from trusted authentication claims, never from request bodies or query parameters. RLS enabled on 100% of tenant-owned tables; automated cross-tenant denial test suite (read, write, attachment, export, report) passes with 0 leaks per release Automated cross-tenant test suite in CI; database policy audit; penetration test Must
SEC-NFR-008 Encryption in transit: all client, API, and integration traffic shall use TLS 1.2 or higher with strong cipher suites; plain HTTP shall redirect to HTTPS; HSTS enabled. TLS 1.0/1.1 and weak ciphers disabled; external TLS scan grade ≥ A; HSTS max-age ≥ 180 days TLS configuration scan per release Must
SEC-NFR-009 Encryption at rest: databases, file storage, and backups shall be encrypted at rest using AES-256 (or platform equivalent); encryption keys shall be rotatable without data loss. 100% of data stores and backup media encrypted; documented key-rotation procedure tested annually Infrastructure configuration audit; key-rotation drill record Must
SEC-NFR-010 Secrets management: application secrets (connection strings, API keys, signing keys) shall be stored in a secrets store or protected configuration, never in source control or client-delivered code; access to secrets shall be logged. 0 secrets in repository (automated scan per commit); secrets rotated on personnel change or suspected exposure ≤ 24 h Secret-scanning CI gate; operations procedure review Must
SEC-NFR-011 Secure SDLC: code changes shall pass peer review, static analysis (SAST), and dependency vulnerability scanning (SCA) before release; critical findings block release. 100% of releases have SAST/SCA evidence; critical vulnerabilities remediated before release, high ≤ 30 days Pipeline configuration review; release evidence sampling Must
SEC-NFR-012 API security: all API inputs shall be validated server-side (type, length, range, format, allow-lists); parameterized queries only; rate limiting per identity and per IP on authentication and expensive endpoints; standardized error responses that leak no stack traces or internal detail. Login rate limit: default 10 attempts/min/IP; API default 300 requests/min/user (configurable); 0 raw exception details in responses API fuzzing; rate-limit test; error-handling review Must
SEC-NFR-013 File security: uploads shall be validated by extension allow-list and content type, stored outside the web root with non-executable permissions, served with safe content-disposition headers, and scanned for malware before being made available for download. Malware scan verdict before first download availability (target ≤ 5 min); infected files quarantined and reporter notified; blocked-extension upload rejected 100% Functional test incl. EICAR sample; storage configuration review Must
SEC-NFR-014 Brute-force protection: repeated failed authentication shall trigger progressive delay and temporary account lockout with administrator-visible events; lockout shall not disclose whether the account exists. Default: lockout after 5 consecutive failures for 15 min (configurable); uniform error message for invalid user vs invalid password Functional test; penetration test Must
SEC-NFR-015 Security event logging: authentication events (success/failure), lockouts, permission changes, role assignments, cross-tenant denial events, export activities, and configuration changes shall be logged to the security log with actor, source IP, timestamp, and outcome; security logs shall be tamper-evident and access-restricted. 100% of listed event types logged; security log retention ≥ 12 months online, aligned with ADT-NFR-001 Log-coverage test per event type; log-access review Must
SEC-NFR-016 Vulnerability management: infrastructure and application shall be scanned for vulnerabilities on a defined cadence; an independent penetration test shall be performed at least annually and after major architectural change, with findings tracked to closure. Vulnerability scan ≥ monthly; penetration test ≥ annually; remediation SLA: critical ≤ 7 days, high ≤ 30 days, medium ≤ 90 days Scan reports; penetration-test report and remediation log Must
SEC-NFR-017 Secure configuration baseline: servers, database, and middleware shall be hardened against a documented baseline (e.g. CIS Benchmarks); default accounts disabled, unused services removed, security headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, frame-ancestors) applied. Baseline compliance ≥ 95% of applicable controls with documented exceptions; security-header scan passes per release Hardening audit; automated header scan Must
SEC-NFR-018 OWASP alignment: the application shall be assessed against OWASP ASVS Level 2 and the current OWASP Top 10; deviations shall be documented with compensating controls. ASVS L2 assessment completed before go-live; 0 unmitigated Top 10 findings at go-live ASVS assessment report; penetration test mapping Must

19 Electronic Signatures & 21 CFR Part 11 ESG

19.1 Overview and Compliance Modes

NT.QMS uses electronic approvals throughout its workflows (document approvals, CAPA sign-off, audit report approval, management review conclusions). This section defines two clearly separated levels of capability:

ModeClassificationAvailabilityWhat it provides
Standard approval functionality Core Always on, all tenants Authenticated in-app approve/reject/review actions bound to the user's session, recorded in the audit trail with actor, UTC timestamp, and record version. No credential re-entry at the moment of approval; suitable for ISO 9001-style quality systems without regulated e-signature obligations.
21 CFR Part 11 compliance mode Compliance Configurable Tenant-configurable (per tenant; enforcement scope per module/record type) Full electronic-signature controls per 21 CFR Part 11 Subpart C: identity re-verification at signing, signature meaning, cryptographic binding to the signed record version, signature manifestation on displays and printouts, non-repudiation controls, and signature-specific audit events. When enabled for a record type, signature-required workflow steps cannot complete without a compliant signature.

Enabling Part 11 mode is a tenant-level configuration performed by the Tenant Administrator (P-02) with the approval of the Quality Director (P-04); the activation itself is an audited configuration change (ADT-NFR-009). Where Part 11 mode is disabled, all standard approval audit behavior in Section 18.6 still applies. The requirements below state explicitly which mode they belong to.

Note — electronic signature vs digital signature: An electronic signature (as regulated by 21 CFR Part 11) is a legally significant computer-based act of signing — a combination of authenticated identity, intent, meaning, and timestamp bound to a record. A digital signature is a cryptographic technique (asymmetric-key signing of a document hash) that may be used to implement or strengthen an electronic signature. NT.QMS implements electronic signatures with cryptographic record binding (hash linkage per ESG-FR-005); issuance of certificate-based qualified digital signatures by an external trust service provider is optional future scope.
Pending business confirmation: (1) Whether any tenant requires qualified/certificate-based digital signatures from an accredited trust service provider (and, if so, which provider and jurisdiction — e.g. eIDAS-qualified or national PKI), which would add provider integration to Section 14. (2) The list of record types per module that require Part 11 signatures when the mode is enabled. (3) Whether signature re-authentication must use both credential re-entry and MFA, or credential re-entry with MFA only for elevated meanings (approval). Numeric parameters in this section (lockout thresholds, timeout values) are proposed baselines pending formal approval.
Out of scope: Handwritten (wet-ink) signature capture pads, biometric signature verification, and blockchain-anchored signatures are out of scope for this release.

19.2 Electronic Signature Functional Requirements
ESG-FR-001 Identity re-verification at the moment of signing (re-authentication) MustCompliance
Requirement
When Part 11 mode is enabled for a record type, the system shall require the signer to re-verify identity at the moment of signing by re-entering their password (and completing MFA where the tenant policy requires it), even within an authenticated session. For a series of signings within one continuous session, the first signing shall require both identity components (user id confirmation + password/MFA) and subsequent signings within the same session shall require at least the password component, per 21 CFR 11.200(a)(1).
Rationale
Part 11 requires that signatures cannot be executed by anyone other than the genuine owner; session possession alone is insufficient proof of identity at signing time.
Actor
Any signing role (Approver P-11, Reviewer P-10, Quality Manager P-05, etc.)
Preconditions / Trigger
Part 11 mode enabled for the record type; user invokes a signature-required action (approve, review sign-off, authorship declaration).
Validation & Exceptions
Failed re-authentication does not execute the signature and is counted toward lockout per ESG-FR-011. SSO-federated users re-authenticate via the identity provider's re-auth flow (forced fresh authentication), which must return a fresh authentication assertion no older than 2 minutes (proposed target — pending business confirmation).
Audit
Re-authentication success/failure logged with actor, record reference, and outcome (ADT-NFR-008).
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-01, AC-ESG-05
Related
SEC-NFR-004, ESG-BR-001
ESG-FR-002 Signature meaning selection MustCompliance
Requirement
The signing dialog shall require the signer to confirm the meaning of the signature from the configured set for the workflow step — at minimum: Authorship, Review, Approval, Responsibility/Accountability. Where the workflow step fixes the meaning (e.g. an approval step), the meaning shall be displayed read-only and explicitly acknowledged by the signer; it shall never be implicit or hidden.
Rationale
21 CFR 11.50 requires signed records to indicate the meaning associated with the signature.
Actor
Signing roles
Preconditions / Trigger
Signature dialog opened for a signature-required action.
Validation & Exceptions
Signature execution blocked until the meaning is confirmed; the confirmed meaning is stored immutably with the signature record.
Audit
Selected/confirmed meaning stored in the signature record and shown in the audit trail.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-01
Related
ESG-FR-006, ESG-BR-003
ESG-FR-003 Trusted signature timestamp (UTC with timezone display) MustCore
Requirement
The system shall record the date and time of every signature (and every standard approval action) from the synchronized server clock in UTC, never from the client device. Displays and printouts shall render the timestamp in the tenant timezone with an explicit timezone designator, with the stored UTC value available on demand.
Rationale
Trustworthy, non-manipulable time is required for signature integrity and audit reconstruction (21 CFR 11.50(a)(2)).
Actor
System (automatic)
Preconditions / Trigger
Signature or approval execution.
Validation & Exceptions
Client-supplied timestamps are ignored; server clock drift bound per ADT-NFR-004.
Audit
UTC timestamp stored in signature record and linked audit event.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-02
Related
USE-NFR-010
ESG-FR-004 Signature reason capture MustCompliance
Requirement
The signing dialog shall capture a reason for the signing action where the workflow step configuration requires it (mandatory for rejections, returns, and any signature that changes an already-effective record; configurable for routine approvals). The reason shall be selectable from a tenant-configurable list with an optional free-text elaboration, and shall be stored immutably with the signature.
Rationale
Reason capture supports audit reconstruction and is required by predicate-rule expectations for changes to regulated records.
Actor
Signing roles
Preconditions / Trigger
Signature dialog on a reason-required step.
Validation & Exceptions
Signature blocked until a reason is provided on reason-required steps; minimum free-text length per ADT-NFR-006.
Audit
Reason stored in the signature record and the linked audit event.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-01
Related
ESG-BR-004
ESG-FR-005 Cryptographic record linkage (hash binding) MustCompliance
Requirement
At signing time the system shall compute a cryptographic hash (SHA-256 or stronger) over the canonical serialized content of the signed record version, including its primary attachments' hashes, and store that hash within the signature record. On every subsequent display of the signed record, the system shall be able to re-verify the hash; any mismatch shall flag the signature as INVALID — record altered after signing on screen and on printouts, and raise a security audit event. Signatures shall be bound to their specific record version and shall not be transferable, by copying or otherwise, to any other record or version (21 CFR 11.70).
Rationale
Hash binding makes post-signature tampering detectable and prevents signature falsification by excision or transfer.
Actor
System (automatic)
Preconditions / Trigger
Signature execution; subsequent record display or verification job.
Validation & Exceptions
Verification failure never blocks viewing the record (evidence must remain inspectable) but prominently flags invalidity and notifies the Quality Manager.
Audit
Hash value stored with signature; verification failures logged as security events (SEC-NFR-015).
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-03
Related
ESG-FR-009, ESG-BR-005
ESG-FR-006 Signature manifestation on records and printouts MustCompliance
Requirement
Every signed record shall display, in human-readable form on screen and on all printed/PDF renderings: the signer's printed full name, the date and time of signing (per ESG-FR-003), and the meaning of the signature (per ESG-FR-002), together with the signed record id and version. The manifestation shall appear wherever the record is rendered in full, including controlled-copy printouts and report exports containing the record.
Rationale
21 CFR 11.50(b) requires signature information to be included in human-readable forms of the record.
Actor
System (automatic)
Preconditions / Trigger
Rendering of a signed record (screen, print, PDF, export).
Validation & Exceptions
Partial renderings (list rows, dashboard tiles) show a signed indicator linking to the full manifestation.
Audit
Not applicable (display behavior); printout generation itself is audited per ADT-NFR-010.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-02
Related
Figure 19.3-1, ESG-FR-014
ESG-FR-007 Signature revocation restrictions — supersede, never delete MustCore
Requirement
Executed signatures (and standard approval actions) shall never be deletable or editable by any role. Where a signed decision must be changed, the system shall require creation of a new record version (or a new workflow cycle) that is itself signed; the original signature remains attached to the original version with status "Superseded by vN". No function shall exist to remove, reassign, or alter a signature record.
Rationale
Non-repudiation: signature history must reflect what was actually signed and when.
Actor
System-enforced; Record Owner initiates new versions
Preconditions / Trigger
Any attempt to change a signed record or decision.
Validation & Exceptions
API and UI reject signature mutation with an authorization error; attempts are security-logged.
Audit
Supersession events link old and new versions and their signatures.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-04
Related
ESG-FR-010, ESG-BR-006
ESG-FR-008 Full signature audit trail MustCore
Requirement
Every signature lifecycle event — dialog opened, re-authentication success/failure, signature executed, signature verification pass/fail, supersession — shall generate an immutable audit event per Section 18.6, containing actor, UTC timestamp, record id and version, meaning, reason (where captured), session id, and source IP.
Rationale
Complete reconstruction of the signing history is required for inspections.
Actor
System (automatic)
Preconditions / Trigger
Any signature lifecycle event.
Validation & Exceptions
Audit write failure aborts the signature transaction (signature and audit are atomic — no signature without its audit event).
Audit
Self-defining; audit store immutability per ADT-NFR-001.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-01, AC-ESG-05
Related
ADT-NFR-007
ESG-FR-009 Record locking after signature MustCompliance
Requirement
Once a record version carries at least one executed signature, the signed content of that version shall become read-only for all roles. Permitted post-signature operations are limited to: appending further required signatures on the same version, adding clearly separated post-signature annotations (where the module allows them, stored as new audited entries — never edits), and creating a new version per ESG-FR-010. Administrative "unlock" of signed content shall not exist.
Rationale
Preserves the integrity of what was signed; prevents silent post-approval edits.
Actor
System-enforced
Preconditions / Trigger
First signature executed on a record version.
Validation & Exceptions
Edit attempts on locked content rejected with an explanatory message directing the user to the new-version flow; attempts audited.
Audit
Lock activation and rejected edit attempts audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-03, AC-ESG-04
Related
ESG-BR-007
ESG-FR-010 Versioning of signed records MustCore
Requirement
Changes to a signed record shall be made only by creating a new version that references its predecessor; each version retains its own signatures, hash, and audit history. The system shall present the full version chain with, for each version: version number, status (Draft / Effective / Superseded), signatures, and effective dates. Prior signed versions shall remain retrievable for the record's full retention period.
Rationale
Regulated record history must show every signed state, not only the latest.
Actor
Record Owner (P-09), Document Controller (P-06)
Preconditions / Trigger
Authorized change request on a signed/effective record.
Validation & Exceptions
New version creation requires the module's change permission and, where configured, a change reason; concurrent new-version creation prevented by optimistic concurrency.
Audit
Version creation, predecessor link, and supersession all audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-04
Related
ESG-FR-007, Section 11.5
ESG-FR-011 Failed signature attempt logging and lockout MustCompliance
Requirement
Failed signature re-authentication attempts shall be logged as security events and counted; after the configured threshold of consecutive failures the signing capability for that user shall be temporarily locked and the Tenant Administrator and Quality Manager notified. The lockout shall not reveal to third parties which record was being signed.
Rationale
21 CFR 11.300(d) requires transaction safeguards detecting and reporting attempted unauthorized use of electronic signatures.
Actor
System (automatic); Tenant Administrator (unlock)
Preconditions / Trigger
Consecutive failed re-authentications in signature dialogs.
Validation & Exceptions
Default threshold: 5 consecutive failures → 15-minute signing lockout and immediate notification (proposed targets — pending business confirmation); administrator may unlock early with an audited reason.
Audit
Each failure, the lockout, notifications, and any manual unlock audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-05
Related
SEC-NFR-014, ESG-BR-008
ESG-FR-012 Delegation restrictions — no signing on behalf of another person MustCore
Requirement
The system shall not provide any mechanism for one user to execute a signature in another user's name. Where workflow duties are delegated (absence, role change), the delegate signs under their own identity, and the signature record shall state that the delegate acted under a documented delegated authority (delegation record id, delegator, scope, validity period). Delegation of signature-required steps requires a pre-existing, approved delegation record; ad-hoc "sign for me" is prohibited. Users shall be able to hold and use only their own signature credentials, which shall not be shared or reassigned.
Rationale
Part 11 requires signatures to be executed only by their genuine owners; delegated authority must be evident, not impersonated.
Actor
Delegate (any signing role); Department Manager / Quality Manager approve delegations
Preconditions / Trigger
Signature-required task assigned or reassigned to a delegate.
Validation & Exceptions
Signature on a delegated task blocked unless an active approved delegation record covers the record type, scope, and date; expired delegations block signing.
Audit
Delegation creation/approval/expiry and every delegated signature (with delegation reference) audited.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-06
Related
ESG-BR-009, Section 13
ESG-FR-013 Signature record storage (signature certificate/reference) MustCompliance
Requirement
Each executed signature shall be persisted as a discrete, immutable signature record containing at minimum: unique signature id, signer user id and printed name at time of signing, tenant id, signed record type/id/version, content hash (ESG-FR-005), meaning, reason (if captured), UTC timestamp, authentication method used (password / password+MFA / IdP re-auth), session id, source IP, delegation reference (if applicable), and status (Valid / Superseded / Invalid). Where a certificate-based digital signature is used (optional future scope), the certificate reference and signature blob shall be stored in the same record. Signature records shall be retained at least as long as their associated record (Section 21).
Rationale
A canonical signature entity enables verification, manifestation, and inspection export independent of module-specific data.
Actor
System (automatic)
Preconditions / Trigger
Signature execution.
Validation & Exceptions
Persistence is transactional with the workflow transition; failure rolls back the transition.
Audit
Creation event linked per ADT-NFR-007.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-02, AC-ESG-03
Related
Section 20 (Signature entity)
ESG-FR-014 Printed and exported display of signatures MustCompliance
Requirement
All printed and PDF renderings of signed records shall include the signature manifestation block (per ESG-FR-006) for every signature on the rendered version, plus the signature verification status as at generation time and the generation timestamp. Printouts of superseded versions shall carry a prominent "SUPERSEDED" watermark; uncontrolled copies shall carry the tenant's configured uncontrolled-copy notice.
Rationale
Inspectors and downstream users rely on printed evidence; it must carry the same signature information as the electronic record.
Actor
System (automatic) on print/export
Preconditions / Trigger
Print or PDF/export generation of a signed record.
Validation & Exceptions
If verification fails at generation time, the printout carries the INVALID flag per ESG-FR-005.
Audit
Print/export generation audited per ADT-NFR-010.
Acceptance criteria
AC-ESG-02
Related
CPT-NFR-006, Figure 19.3-1

19.3 Signature Manifestation — Illustrative Mockup
Note: The block below is an illustrative mockup of the signature manifestation rendered on signed records and their printouts. Final visual design follows the UI style guide; the content elements shown (printed name, date/time with timezone, meaning, record version binding, verification status) are mandatory per ESG-FR-006.

19.4 Business Rules
Rule IDRuleEnforcementException handling
ESG-BR-001 When Part 11 mode is enabled for a record type, no signature-required workflow step can complete without a compliant electronic signature (re-authentication + meaning + timestamp + hash binding). Workflow engine blocks the transition server-side. None. Disabling Part 11 mode for the record type is itself an audited configuration change requiring Quality Director approval.
ESG-BR-002 Standard approval actions (Part 11 mode off) always record actor, UTC timestamp, and record version in the audit trail; they are never anonymous. Audit write is atomic with the approval transaction. Audit-store unavailability aborts the approval; the user is instructed to retry.
ESG-BR-003 Signature meaning is fixed by the workflow step definition and cannot be altered by the signer at signing time; the signer explicitly acknowledges it. Signing dialog renders meaning read-only from step configuration. Changing a step's meaning requires workflow-configuration permission and takes effect only for future signatures.
ESG-BR-004 A reason is mandatory for every rejection signature, return-for-correction signature, and any signature applied to change an effective record. Server-side validation on the signature payload. None; reason lists are tenant-configurable but the mandatory rule is fixed.
ESG-BR-005 A signature is valid only for the exact record version content it hashed; any content difference invalidates it. Signatures are never copied, migrated, or re-pointed to other versions or records. Hash verification per ESG-FR-005; no API exists to re-point signatures. Invalid signatures are flagged, never hidden; investigation is handled as a quality incident (NCR).
ESG-BR-006 Signatures cannot be deleted by any role, including Platform Administrator; a signed decision is superseded only by a newer signed version. No delete pathway in UI, API, or admin tooling; database permissions deny deletes to the application role. None.
ESG-BR-007 Signed content is locked; corrections require a new version. Post-signature annotations, where a module permits them, are stored as separate audited entries and are visually distinct from signed content. Field-level write lock on signed versions. Edit attempts rejected with guidance to the new-version flow; attempt audited.
ESG-BR-008 Five consecutive failed signature re-authentications lock the user's signing capability for 15 minutes and notify the Tenant Administrator and Quality Manager (proposed values — pending business confirmation). Counter enforced server-side per user across sessions. Early unlock by Tenant Administrator with mandatory audited reason.
ESG-BR-009 Signing under delegation requires an active, approved delegation record covering the record type and date; the delegate always signs under their own identity with the delegation reference recorded. Delegation check executed at signature time, not only at task assignment. Expired or out-of-scope delegation blocks signing; the task is escalated to the delegator's manager.
ESG-BR-010 Separation of duties: a user cannot execute both the authorship signature and the approval signature on the same record version, even if they hold both roles, unless the tenant explicitly disables SoD for that workflow (audited configuration). SoD check at signature time against prior signatures on the version. Violation attempt rejected and audited; workflow reroutes to an alternate approver.

19.5 Acceptance Criteria

AC-ESG-01 — Compliant signature execution captures identity, meaning, and reason

  • Given Part 11 mode is enabled for SOP documents and an Approver has an approval task on SOP-QA-014 v3.0,
  • When the Approver invokes "Approve & Sign", re-enters their password (and MFA per tenant policy), acknowledges the meaning "Approval", and provides the required reason,
  • Then the system executes the signature, stores the signature record with meaning, reason, and UTC timestamp, completes the workflow step, and writes the linked audit event in a single transaction.

AC-ESG-02 — Manifestation appears on screen and PDF

  • Given SOP-QA-014 v3.0 carries an executed approval signature,
  • When a user views the record and generates its controlled-copy PDF,
  • Then both the screen and the PDF display the signer's printed full name, the signing date/time in the tenant timezone with timezone designator, the meaning "Approval", the record id and version, and the verification status as at generation time.

AC-ESG-03 — Tampering invalidates the signature

  • Given a signed record version whose stored content is altered directly in the database (simulated tamper in a test environment),
  • When any user next opens the record or the verification job runs,
  • Then the signature is flagged "INVALID — record altered after signing" on screen and on any printout, a security audit event is raised, and the Quality Manager is notified; the record remains viewable.

AC-ESG-04 — Signatures survive supersession and cannot be deleted

  • Given SOP-QA-014 v3.0 is signed and effective, and an authorized user creates and gets approval for v4.0,
  • When v4.0 becomes effective and any user (including a Platform Administrator) attempts to delete or modify the v3.0 signature via UI or API,
  • Then v3.0 shows status "Superseded" while retaining its intact signature and hash, the deletion/modification attempt is rejected with an authorization error, and the attempt is recorded as a security audit event.

AC-ESG-05 — Failed attempts lock signing and alert administrators

  • Given Part 11 mode is enabled and a user has entered an incorrect password in the signing dialog 4 consecutive times,
  • When the user fails re-authentication a 5th consecutive time,
  • Then the system blocks further signing attempts by that user for 15 minutes, records all five failures and the lockout as security audit events, and notifies the Tenant Administrator and Quality Manager without disclosing the record content in the notification.

AC-ESG-06 — Delegated signing requires documented authority

  • Given an approval task reassigned to a delegate whose delegation record expired yesterday,
  • When the delegate attempts to sign the approval,
  • Then the system blocks the signature with a message identifying the missing/expired delegation, audits the attempt, and escalates the task per the escalation chain; after a valid delegation is approved, the delegate signs under their own name and the signature record stores the delegation reference.

20 Conceptual Data Model

20.1 Modelling Approach & Conventions

This section defines the conceptual data model of NT.QMS at the business-entity level. It identifies the major entities the system must persist, their key relationships, their tenancy ownership, and their retention, confidentiality and audit characteristics. It deliberately excludes physical design detail (columns, indexes, partitioning); the physical model is produced during technical design and must remain traceable to the entities catalogued here.

The model is organized into bounded contexts that mirror the functional module structure of Section 11:

  • Platform — tenant registry, workflow definitions, report definitions, integration messaging (owned by Platform Administration, §11.1).
  • Organization & Identity — organization hierarchy, sites, users, roles, permissions, employees (§11.2, §11.3).
  • Document Control — documents, versions, approvals, electronic signatures (§11.5, §19).
  • Quality Records — nonconformances, CAPAs, complaints, audits, findings, risks, quality objectives, KPIs, management reviews, suppliers (§11.6–§11.13).
  • Assets & People — equipment, calibration, maintenance, training assignments, competencies (§11.10, §11.11).
  • Shared Kernel — tasks, notifications, attachments and audit events referenced by every other context.
Note: Each functional module owns a dedicated PostgreSQL schema (for example plt, org, iam, doc, ncr, capa, cmp, aud, trn, eqp, rsk, mrv, shared). Cross-schema access is permitted only through defined module interfaces (see Section 12); no module writes directly into another module's schema.
Tenancy enforcement: Every tenant-owned table carries a non-nullable TenantId column. Tenant isolation is enforced in the database by PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies in addition to application-level filters. The tenant context is derived exclusively from trusted authentication claims — never from the request body or query string — and every denied cross-tenant access attempt is recorded as a security audit event (see Section 18).

Legend used in the entity catalogue below:

  • Retention class — RC-1 master/configuration data retained for the life of the tenant contract; RC-2 quality record with long-term configurable retention (defaults per Section 21); RC-3 operational record with medium-term configurable retention; RC-4 transient data eligible for automatic purge.
  • Confidentiality class — Internal (visible to authenticated tenant users per role), Confidential (restricted to involved roles), Restricted (named individuals / explicit grants only).
  • Audited — Y indicates all create/update/status/permission-relevant changes are written to the immutable audit trail (§18).

20.3 Conceptual Entity-Relationship Diagram

20.4 Data Ownership & Tenancy Enforcement
  • Every entity marked Tenant-owned = Y carries a mandatory TenantId; PostgreSQL RLS policies deny any row access where the session tenant claim does not match, independently of application code (defense in depth, see Section 18).
  • Platform-owned entities (Tenant registry, Permission catalogue, platform-seeded Report Definitions) are readable to tenants only through controlled projections; tenants never see other tenants' registry rows.
  • Module schemas are the single source of truth for their entities; other modules consume them through published interfaces and integration events only (Section 12).
  • Polymorphic references (Attachment, Task, Notification, Audit Event) always store the owning TenantId redundantly and are covered by the same RLS policies as their parents.
  • Deletion is logical (status change) for all quality records; physical disposal happens only through the controlled disposal workflow in Section 21.

21 Data Retention & Archiving

21.1 Retention Principles

NT.QMS manages regulated quality records whose retention obligations differ by industry, jurisdiction and tenant compliance context (ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 17025, ISO 15189, ISO 13485, GxP / 21 CFR Part 11 where enabled). The system therefore implements a configurable retention policy engine rather than hard-coded retention periods: each tenant assigns retention rules per record category, and the platform ships conservative proposed defaults.

Pending business confirmation: All retention periods shown in the catalogue below are proposed configurable defaults. They are not statements of legal or regulatory requirements. Final default values per record category must be confirmed with the client's regulatory affairs / quality function per applicable jurisdiction before go-live, and remain tenant-configurable thereafter.
  • Retention clocks start from a defined trigger per category (e.g. record closure, document supersedence, employee separation, equipment decommissioning).
  • Archived records remain retrievable, read-only, and fully searchable by authorized roles; archiving never breaks traceability links or audit-trail chains.
  • The audit trail for a record is always retained at least as long as the record itself (see RET-FR-006).
  • Legal hold suspends both automatic archiving-related disposal and manual disposal for affected records regardless of expired retention.
  • Backups are governed separately: disposed records may persist in encrypted backups until backup rotation completes; the disposal certificate records this and the backup expiry horizon (see RET-FR-005).
