21.3 Retention Functional Requirements
RET-FR-001 Configurable retention policy engine per record category and tenant MustConfigurable
Requirement
The system shall allow the Tenant Administrator to define retention policies per record category (per the catalogue in §21.2), specifying retention period, retention trigger event, archive conditions and disposal behavior. Policies shall be versioned, effective-dated, and applied automatically by a scheduled retention evaluation job.
Rationale
Retention obligations vary by jurisdiction and standard; hard-coded periods would make the platform non-compliant for some tenants.
Actor
Tenant Administrator (P-02), Quality Director (P-04)
Preconditions / Trigger
Tenant provisioned; policy changes take effect from their effective date and never retroactively shorten retention of existing records below their previously promised period.
Validation & Exceptions
Retention period cannot be set below the platform minimum for the category; audit-trail retention cannot be set below the referenced record retention. Attempts are rejected with an explanatory message.
Audit
Policy create/change/activation recorded with before/after values, actor and reason.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RET-01
Related
RET-FR-006, §18
RET-FR-002 Legal hold MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall allow authorized roles to place a legal hold on individual records, record sets (by filter), or entire categories. Records under legal hold shall be excluded from disposal and from any anonymization job regardless of expired retention, until the hold is explicitly released with a documented reason.
Rationale
Litigation and regulatory inspection obligations override normal retention schedules.
Actor
Quality Director (P-04), Tenant Administrator (P-02)
Preconditions / Trigger
Legal or regulatory event communicated to the tenant.
Validation & Exceptions
A disposal job encountering a held record skips it, continues, and reports the skipped set. Release of a hold requires a second authorized role (four-eyes) when the hold scope exceeds a configurable record count.
Audit
Hold placement, scope, reason, release and releasing actors are audit events.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RET-02
Related
RET-FR-005
RET-FR-003 Archiving to read-only tier MustCore
Requirement
The system shall automatically move records meeting their archive conditions to an archive state: the record becomes read-only, is excluded from default operational lists and dashboards, retains all relationships, attachments and audit-trail links, and is flagged "Archived" in search results. Attachments of archived records may be relocated to cold object storage with checksum verification.
Rationale
Keeps operational views fast and focused while preserving regulated history.
Actor
System (scheduled job); manual archive by Record Owner with approval where configured.
Preconditions / Trigger
Archive conditions of the category policy met (e.g. closed + inactivity period).
Validation & Exceptions
Records with open child records (e.g. CAPA with open actions) are never archived; the job logs the blocking reason.
Audit
Archive transition logged per record with policy version applied.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RET-03
Related
RET-FR-004, §17
RET-FR-004 Retrieval of archived records MustCore
Requirement
The system shall allow authorized roles to search, open, print and export archived records including their full audit trail and attachments. Retrieval from cold attachment storage shall complete within a configurable service level (proposed target: 15 minutes — pending business confirmation) and verify file checksums on restore.
Rationale
Inspections and audits require timely access to historical records (BUS-OBJ-007, BUS-OBJ-010).
Actor
Quality Manager (P-05), auditors (P-15/P-16/P-29 via granted access)
Preconditions / Trigger
Record in Archived state; requesting role holds view permission for the category.
Validation & Exceptions
Checksum mismatch on restore blocks delivery, raises a security alert and an incident task.
Audit
Every archived-record retrieval and export is logged (who, when, record, purpose field).
Acceptance criteria
AC-RET-03
Related
RET-FR-003
RET-FR-005 Controlled disposal workflow with approval and disposal certificate MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall dispose of records only through a controlled workflow: (1) the retention job proposes a disposal list of records past retention and not under legal hold; (2) the designated approver reviews and approves or excludes items, with e-signature where the tenant's compliance profile requires it; (3) the system executes disposal and generates an immutable disposal certificate listing record identifiers, categories, retention policy applied, approver, execution timestamp, attachment hashes, and a statement of the backup expiry horizon after which disposed data ceases to exist in backups.
Rationale
Auditable, deliberate destruction is itself a quality-record requirement; accidental or silent deletion is prohibited.
Actor
System (proposal), Quality Director (P-04) or configured approver (approval)
Preconditions / Trigger
Retention expired; no legal hold; disposal approval granted.
Validation & Exceptions
Partial failures roll the affected items back to the pending list with error detail; the certificate covers only actually disposed items. Disposal of a record whose audit trail is referenced by a retained record is refused.
Audit
Disposal proposal, approval decision, execution and certificate issuance are audit events; the certificate itself is retained permanently.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RET-04
Related
RET-FR-002, §19
RET-FR-006 Audit-trail retention at least equal to record retention MustCompliance
Requirement
The system shall retain the audit trail of every record for at least as long as the record itself, and shall prevent any configuration in which audit-event retention is shorter than the retention of the referenced record category. Audit events are disposed only together with their referenced records under RET-FR-005.
Rationale
An audit trail that outlives its record preserves accountability (BUS-OBJ-008); one that expires earlier destroys it.
Actor
System (enforcement); Tenant Administrator (configuration attempts)
Preconditions / Trigger
Any retention policy save or disposal execution.
Validation & Exceptions
Policy saves violating the invariant are rejected with the conflicting category named.
Audit
Rejected configuration attempts are themselves logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RET-01
Related
§18 (ADT NFRs)
RET-FR-007 Tenant termination export MustCore
Requirement
Upon tenant contract termination, the system shall produce a complete, structured export of all tenant-owned data: records in a documented machine-readable format (JSON or CSV per entity, with schema documentation), attachments as original files with checksum manifest, audit trail in full, and human-readable renditions (PDF) of controlled documents and signature manifests. The export shall be integrity-sealed (package hash) and delivered through a secure channel. Post-export data destruction follows the disposal workflow of RET-FR-005 after a contractually defined grace period.
Rationale
Tenants own their quality records and must be able to leave the platform without losing regulated evidence (BUS-OBJ-015).
Actor
Platform Administrator (P-01) on tenant's formal request
Preconditions / Trigger
Termination notice; identity and authority of requester verified.
Validation & Exceptions
Export reconciliation report compares entity counts and attachment checksums against the live database before delivery; discrepancies block delivery.
Audit
Export request, generation, verification, delivery and subsequent destruction are audit events retained at platform level.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RET-04
Related
§11.1, §18 (DRB NFRs)
RET-FR-008 Anonymization of personal data after retention where permitted ShouldConfigurable
Requirement
For record categories flagged as anonymizable in the retention catalogue, the system shall support replacing personal identifiers (names, contact details, free-text personal data fields) with irreversible pseudonyms after the retention period, while preserving the record's quality-evidence content and referential integrity. Anonymization is per-category configurable, requires the same approval workflow as disposal, and is blocked by legal hold.
Rationale
Balances privacy obligations (data minimization) with quality-record integrity.
Actor
Tenant Administrator (configuration), Quality Director (approval)
Preconditions / Trigger
Retention expired for an anonymizable category; approval granted.
Validation & Exceptions
Categories where identity is part of the quality evidence (e-signatures, approvals, training completion identity) are excluded and cannot be flagged anonymizable.
Audit
Anonymization runs are logged with record counts and field classes affected — never the original values.
Acceptance criteria
AC-RET-04
Related
§18 (PRI NFRs), RET-FR-002

21.4 Acceptance Criteria

AC-RET-01 — Policy engine enforces audit-trail invariant

  • Given a record category configured with 10-year retention,
  • When the Tenant Administrator attempts to set audit-event retention for that category to 5 years,
  • Then the system rejects the save, names the conflicting category and minimum permitted value, and logs the rejected attempt in the audit trail.

AC-RET-02 — Legal hold blocks disposal

  • Given a closed complaint past its retention period that is under legal hold,
  • When the scheduled disposal job runs and the disposal list is approved,
  • Then the held record is excluded from disposal, listed in the job report as skipped with reason "legal hold", and remains fully retrievable.

AC-RET-03 — Archived record retrieval preserves integrity

  • Given an archived nonconformance whose attachments were moved to cold storage,
  • When an authorized Quality Manager opens the record and downloads an attachment,
  • Then the record opens read-only with complete audit trail, the attachment is restored with a verified checksum, and the retrieval is logged as an audit event.

AC-RET-04 — Disposal produces a complete certificate

  • Given an approved disposal list of 50 records,
  • When the disposal job executes and 2 records fail due to a storage error,
  • Then 48 records are disposed, the disposal certificate lists exactly those 48 with identifiers, approver, timestamps and attachment hashes, the 2 failures return to the pending list with error detail, and the certificate is stored immutably.

22 Migration Requirements

22.1 Scope & Approach

The client currently maintains quality records in a mixture of legacy systems, spreadsheets and paper (see Section 5). Migration into NT.QMS covers master data, identities, controlled documents with version history, open quality records, and selected historical records needed for audit readiness. Migration is executed per tenant/organization as a project workstream with formal stage gates (§22.3), and every migrated record is flagged with a migration source reference for traceability.

  • Data mapping workbook — a controlled artifact mapping every source field to its NT.QMS target field, transformation rule, code-list mapping, default and validation rule; approved by the client data owner before any load.
  • Cleansing — performed on extracted staging data against documented rules (mandatory fields, formats, code lists, referential integrity); cleansing changes are logged, never silent.
  • Validation rules & duplicate handling — automated pre-load validation rejects or quarantines invalid rows; configurable duplicate detection (exact keys + fuzzy match on names/numbers) routes candidates to a review queue with merge/keep-both/skip decisions recorded.
  • Reconciliation — post-load reports compare source vs. loaded counts per entity, sum checks on numeric fields, and file checksums for attachments; all discrepancies must be dispositioned.
  • Trial migrations — at least one full-volume trial migration into a staging tenant precedes the final run; the final cutover plan includes freeze window, sequence, verification steps and rollback criteria.
  • Sign-off — migration completion requires documented client sign-off based on reconciliation evidence; sign-off is a prerequisite for go-live (§27).
Assumption: The client will provide source-system extracts in an agreed machine-readable format (CSV/Excel/database export) and nominate data owners empowered to make cleansing and duplicate-resolution decisions. Source-system remediation is out of scope for NT.QMS.

22.2 Migration Functional Requirements
MIG-FR-001 Master and reference data migration MustCore
Requirement
The system shall provide an import capability for master and reference data — code lists, document types and classifications, NC/CAPA categories, complaint categories, audit types, risk scales, supplier records and units of measure — from the approved mapping workbook, with per-row validation and an import report (accepted / rejected / warnings with reasons).
Rationale
All transactional migration depends on consistent reference data being in place first.
Actor
Migration engineer with Tenant Administrator (P-02) oversight
Preconditions / Trigger
Mapping workbook approved; target tenant configured.
Validation & Exceptions
Duplicate codes rejected; unknown parent references quarantined; the import is idempotent (re-running with the same batch id does not duplicate rows).
Audit
Each import batch logged with source file hash, row counts and outcome.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-01
Related
MIG-FR-002
MIG-FR-002 Organization structure migration MustCore
Requirement
The system shall import the organization hierarchy (organizations, branches, departments, sites) preserving parent-child relationships, codes and manager assignments, and shall validate that every imported node resolves to exactly one parent and that codes are unique per level.
Rationale
Ownership, routing and permissions all resolve through the organization hierarchy.
Actor
Migration engineer, Organization Administrator (P-03)
Preconditions / Trigger
MIG-FR-001 completed for dependent code lists.
Validation & Exceptions
Orphan nodes and cyclic references are rejected with row-level detail.
Audit
Import batch logged; post-load hierarchy snapshot stored for reconciliation.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-01
Related
§11.2
MIG-FR-003 User account migration MustCore
Requirement
The system shall import user accounts (identity attributes, role assignments, org-unit scope, status) without importing passwords: migrated users are created in a "pending activation" state and complete activation through the standard invitation flow (or SSO linkage where INT identity federation is configured).
Rationale
Password hashes from legacy systems are neither portable nor trustworthy; activation re-establishes verified identity.
Actor
Migration engineer, Tenant Administrator (P-02)
Preconditions / Trigger
Roles configured; organization structure loaded.
Validation & Exceptions
Duplicate emails are quarantined for resolution; role names not matching the target role catalogue are rejected with mapping guidance.
Audit
Account creation events logged as migration-sourced with batch id.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-01
Related
§11.3, MIG-FR-004
MIG-FR-004 Employee record migration MustCore
Requirement
The system shall import employee records (identifiers, names, department, job title, hire date, status) and link them to migrated user accounts where a deterministic match exists (employee number or verified email); unmatched links are routed to a manual linking queue.
Rationale
Training and competency records attach to employees, not user accounts.
Actor
Migration engineer, Training Coordinator (P-18)
Preconditions / Trigger
Departments and users loaded.
Validation & Exceptions
Duplicate employee numbers quarantined; employees in unknown departments rejected.
Audit
Import batch and each manual link decision logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-02
Related
MIG-FR-006
MIG-FR-005 Controlled document and version migration with legacy numbering map MustCore
Requirement
The system shall import existing controlled documents including their version history (at minimum the current effective version plus available prior versions), metadata, effective dates and source files. Each migrated document shall retain its legacy number in a dedicated "legacy reference" field, and the system shall maintain a searchable legacy-to-new numbering map so users and auditors can locate documents by either number. Migrated effective versions enter status Active/Effective without re-approval, flagged "approved in legacy system" with the legacy approval evidence attached where available.
Rationale
Continuity of document control and inspection traceability across the cutover (BUS-OBJ-003, BUS-OBJ-005).
Actor
Document Controller (P-06), migration engineer
Preconditions / Trigger
Document types/classifications loaded; mapping workbook covers numbering scheme translation.
Validation & Exceptions
Missing source files quarantine the version; duplicate legacy numbers require Document Controller disposition; checksum recorded per imported file.
Audit
Every migrated document/version carries a migration provenance audit event (source system, legacy id, batch, file hash).
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-03
Related
§11.5, MIG-FR-010
MIG-FR-006 Training record migration MustCore
Requirement
The system shall import historical training records (employee, training item, completion date, result, trainer, evidence file) as completed training assignments linked to migrated employees and, where applicable, to migrated document versions. Records lacking a resolvable employee or training item are quarantined.
Rationale
Competency evidence must survive the cutover for audit readiness (BUS-OBJ-011).
Actor
Training Coordinator (P-18), migration engineer
Preconditions / Trigger
Employees and documents loaded.
Validation & Exceptions
Completion dates in the future rejected; duplicate employee+item+date rows deduplicated with report.
Audit
Batch logged; migrated records flagged as historical (not re-triggering training workflows).
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-02
Related
§11.10
MIG-FR-007 Equipment and calibration record migration MustCore
Requirement
The system shall import the equipment register (asset data, site, status, criticality) and calibration history (events, results, certificates as attachments, next-due dates) such that calibration scheduling resumes correctly from the migrated next-due dates immediately after cutover.
Rationale
Calibration continuity is a direct compliance obligation (BUS-OBJ-012).
Actor
Equipment Coordinator (P-21), Calibration Coordinator (P-22), migration engineer
Preconditions / Trigger
Sites loaded; calibration code lists loaded.
Validation & Exceptions
Equipment without a site is quarantined; past-due next-due dates are imported and immediately surface as overdue (not silently rescheduled).
Audit
Batch logged; per-asset provenance recorded.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-02
Related
§11.11
MIG-FR-008 Open CAPA migration MustCore
Requirement
The system shall import open CAPAs with their current workflow state mapped to the nearest NT.QMS state, open actions with owners and due dates, root-cause documentation and evidence attachments, so that work continues in NT.QMS without re-initiation. State mapping is defined per source system in the mapping workbook and approved by the CAPA Coordinator.
Rationale
Open corrective actions must not lose momentum or history at cutover (BUS-OBJ-009).
Actor
CAPA Coordinator (P-12), migration engineer
Preconditions / Trigger
Users/employees loaded so ownership resolves; state map approved.
Validation & Exceptions
CAPAs whose owner cannot be resolved are assigned to the CAPA Coordinator's triage queue rather than rejected; unmapped states block the batch.
Audit
Migration provenance plus an explicit audit event noting the legacy state and mapped state.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-04
Related
§11.7, MIG-FR-009
MIG-FR-009 Open nonconformance migration MustCore
Requirement
The system shall import open nonconformances with mapped workflow state, containment/disposition data, links to migrated CAPAs where the source relationship exists, and evidence attachments, following the same state-mapping and triage rules as MIG-FR-008.
Rationale
Open deviations remain actionable and traceable after cutover.
Actor
Quality Manager (P-05), migration engineer
Preconditions / Trigger
CAPAs loaded first where links exist (or link-resolution pass after both loads).
Validation & Exceptions
Broken NC→CAPA links reported and queued for manual re-linking; not silently dropped.
Audit
Provenance and state-mapping events per record.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-04
Related
§11.6
MIG-FR-010 Historical audit and complaint migration ShouldCore
Requirement
The system shall import closed historical audits (with findings) and closed complaints for a client-selected history window (proposed default: last 3 years — pending business confirmation) as read-only closed records flagged as migrated history, preserving finding-to-NC/CAPA links where resolvable.
Rationale
Inspection readiness requires recent history in one searchable system (BUS-OBJ-010).
Actor
Quality Manager (P-05), Complaint Coordinator (P-14), migration engineer
Preconditions / Trigger
History window agreed and documented in the migration plan.
Validation & Exceptions
Records outside the window are excluded and listed in the exclusion report retained as migration evidence.
Audit
Provenance per record; exclusion report hash logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-04
Related
§11.8, §11.9
MIG-FR-011 Attachment migration with checksum verification MustCore
Requirement
The system shall migrate source files as attachments linked to their target records, computing and storing a checksum per file at extraction and verifying it after load; files shall pass the standard virus scan and type validation pipeline. A per-batch attachment manifest (file name, size, checksum, target record) is produced as reconciliation evidence.
Rationale
Evidence files are the substance of many quality records; silent corruption or loss is unacceptable.
Actor
Migration engineer
Preconditions / Trigger
Target records loaded; object storage provisioned.
Validation & Exceptions
Checksum mismatch or failed scan quarantines the file with its target record flagged "attachment pending"; oversized/unsupported files listed for manual disposition.
Audit
Manifest hash and per-file verification results logged.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-03
Related
MIG-FR-005
MIG-FR-012 Legacy audit-trail import as read-only history ShouldConfigurable
Requirement
Where the source system can export its audit trail in a parseable form, the system shall import legacy audit events as clearly labelled read-only historical records attached to the migrated records, stored separately from the native NT.QMS audit trail and excluded from its cryptographic chain.
Rationale
Preserves whatever accountability history exists without misrepresenting it as NT.QMS-generated evidence.
Actor
Migration engineer, Quality Director (acceptance of limitation)
Preconditions / Trigger
Legacy export available and mapped.
Validation & Exceptions
Unparseable events are stored as raw text attachments rather than dropped.
Audit
The import itself is a native audit event; imported events are immutable.
Acceptance criteria
AC-MIG-05
Related
§18 (ADT NFRs)
Limitation (accepted): Legacy audit trails imported under MIG-FR-012 cannot be integrity-verified by NT.QMS; they are evidence of the legacy system's records only, carry a visible "Imported — integrity not verifiable by NT.QMS" label, and are excluded from tamper-evidence chaining. Where the source system offers no usable export, the legacy audit trail is preserved outside NT.QMS by the client (e.g. archived database backup) and this is recorded in the migration sign-off.

22.3 Migration Process & Stage Gates
StageEntry criteriaActivitiesExit criteriaOwner
1. Discovery & data mappingSource systems identified; data owners nominatedProfile sources; author data mapping workbook (fields, transformations, code maps, validation rules, duplicate rules, state maps)Mapping workbook approved by client data owners and Quality ManagerMigration lead + client data owners
2. Extraction & stagingMapping workbook approved; staging environment provisionedExtract source data; load staging; compute row counts and checksums per extractExtract manifest complete; source counts baselinedMigration engineer
3. Cleansing & validationStaging loadedRun validation rules; cleanse per documented rules; resolve duplicates via review queue; log all changesRejection rate below agreed threshold; all quarantined items dispositioned or consciously deferredClient data owners + migration engineer
4. Trial migrationCleansed staging data; target trial tenant configuredExecute full-volume load into trial tenant; run reconciliation (counts, checksums, sample deep-dives); user spot verificationReconciliation clean or all discrepancies dispositioned; trial report accepted; go/no-go for cutoverMigration lead + Quality Manager
5. Final migration & cutoverTrial accepted; cutover plan (freeze window, sequence, rollback criteria) approvedFreeze legacy updates; delta extract; final load; reconciliation; smoke verification against cutover checklistReconciliation clean; rollback criteria not triggered; cutover checklist signedMigration lead + client project manager
6. Post-migration verification & sign-offCutover completeBusiness verification of agreed samples per module; open-items log closure; produce migration summary reportClient migration sign-off recorded (prerequisite for go-live); hypercare plan activeClient Quality Director + project sponsor
Rollback criteria: The cutover plan shall define measurable rollback triggers before execution — at minimum: reconciliation discrepancy above the agreed threshold on any critical entity, corruption or loss detected in attachment verification, or inability to complete the load within the freeze window. If triggered, the legacy system remains the system of record, the target tenant load is discarded or reset, and a corrective rerun is planned. Rollback execution and its reason are documented in the migration summary report.

22.4 Acceptance Criteria

AC-MIG-01 — Import is validated and idempotent

  • Given a master-data import file containing 1,000 rows of which 40 violate validation rules,
  • When the batch is executed twice with the same batch id,
  • Then exactly 960 rows are loaded once (no duplicates from the rerun), the 40 rejected rows are reported with row-level reasons, and both runs are logged with the source file hash.

AC-MIG-02 — Reconciliation report proves completeness

  • Given a completed training-record load,
  • When the reconciliation report is generated,
  • Then it shows source count, loaded count, quarantined count and rejected count per entity with source-vs-target checksums, and the counts sum exactly to the source total.

AC-MIG-03 — Legacy document numbering remains searchable

  • Given a migrated document that had legacy number "QP-017" and received NT.QMS number per the tenant numbering scheme,
  • When a user searches for "QP-017",
  • Then the migrated document is returned with its legacy reference visible, its imported version history intact, and each imported file's checksum verified.

AC-MIG-04 — Open records continue their lifecycle

  • Given an open legacy CAPA mapped to NT.QMS state "In Progress" with two open actions,
  • When the assigned CAPA Action Owner opens the migrated CAPA after cutover,
  • Then the actions appear in the owner's task list with migrated due dates, the record shows its legacy state mapping in the audit history, and the workflow proceeds without re-initiation.

AC-MIG-05 — Imported legacy audit trail is labelled and immutable

  • Given a migrated record with imported legacy audit events,
  • When a user views the record's history,
  • Then legacy events are visually separated, labelled "Imported — integrity not verifiable by NT.QMS", cannot be edited or deleted by any role, and native NT.QMS events begin their own tamper-evident chain from the migration timestamp.

23 Validation & Testing

23.1 Validation Strategy

NT.QMS is verified through layered testing during development and validated against this SRS before each release to production. Every functional requirement, business rule and NFR in this document is traceable to at least one test scenario through the Requirements Traceability Matrix (Section 24). Test evidence is retained as a controlled deliverable.

Computerized System Validation (CSV): Formal CSV with IQ/OQ/PQ-style protocols applies only when a tenant operates under a GxP-regulated compliance context (configurable compliance profile per tenant, see Section 19). For non-GxP tenants the standard verification and UAT evidence set applies. The platform release process always produces the full evidence set once; GxP tenants additionally execute their own PQ/UAT against their configured processes.

23.4 Acceptance Criteria

AC-VAL-01 — Cross-tenant denial suite passes completely

  • Given two seeded tenants A and B and an authenticated Tenant A user with maximum tenant privileges,
  • When the tenant-isolation suite attempts every read, write, list, search, export and attachment-download path against Tenant B identifiers,
  • Then every attempt is denied without revealing whether the target record exists, no Tenant B data appears in any response payload, and each attempt is recorded as a security audit event.

AC-VAL-02 — Tamper evidence detected

  • Given a test database where one historical audit event row has been altered directly in storage,
  • When the audit-trail chain verification job runs,
  • Then the verification reports the exact broken chain position, raises a critical security alert, and the validation test records the detection as evidence for VAL-FR-015.

AC-VAL-03 — Release gate enforces traceability

  • Given a release candidate in which one Must-priority functional requirement has no linked passing test scenario in the RTM,
  • When the Validation Summary Report is compiled,
  • Then the gap is listed as a blocking deviation and release approval cannot be recorded until the requirement is tested or the deviation is formally dispositioned with documented risk acceptance.

AC-VAL-04 — Restore test proves recoverability

  • Given the most recent scheduled backup set,
  • When a full restore into a clean environment is executed per the runbook,
  • Then the system starts successfully, reconciliation checks on record counts, attachment checksums and audit-chain verification all pass, and the elapsed time is within the RTO defined in Section 18.

24 Requirements Traceability Matrix

24.1 RTM Approach

The Requirements Traceability Matrix connects every requirement in this SRS to its business justification and to its verification evidence, so that (a) no business objective is left uncovered, (b) no requirement exists without a business reason, and (c) no requirement ships untested. Each RTM row traces one thread through the following chain:

  • Business objective (BUS-OBJ-###, Section 6)
  • → Business process / workflow (Sections 9, 11.x.7)
  • → Module (Section 11)
  • → Functional requirement (<CODE>-FR-###)
  • → Business rule (<CODE>-BR-###)
  • → Persona (P-##, Section 13)
  • → Report (RPT-<CODE>-##, Section 15)
  • → Integration (INT-###, Section 14)
  • → Acceptance criterion (AC-<CODE>-##)
  • → Test scenario (TST-###, §24.2)
  • → Compliance reference (standard clause, e.g. ISO 9001:2015 §7.5, 21 CFR 11.10)

Not every row populates every column (for example, a purely internal rule may have no integration); empty cells are recorded as "—" deliberately, never left blank. The RTM is maintained as a controlled validation deliverable (§23.3) and updated whenever requirements, tests or configuration change; the release gate in AC-VAL-03 enforces its completeness for Must-priority requirements.

25 Risks & Mitigations

This section registers the principal project and product risks identified during requirements elaboration for NT.QMS. Each risk carries a probability and impact rating, a derived risk level, a mitigation strategy (actions taken to reduce probability or impact), a contingency plan (actions executed if the risk materialises), an accountable owner, a measurable trigger, and a current status. The register is a living artefact: it shall be reviewed at every project steering meeting and updated whenever a trigger condition is observed.

25.1 Risk Level Legend

Risk level is derived from the combination of probability and impact as follows:

Probability \ ImpactLow (L)Medium (M)High (H)
High (H)MediumHighCritical
Medium (M)LowMediumHigh
Low (L)LowLowMedium

Critical and High risks require a named owner, an active mitigation plan, and review at every steering meeting. Medium risks are reviewed monthly. Low risks are monitored via their triggers. A fine-grained 5×5 scoring matrix used by the product Risk Management module is reproduced in Appendix F.

Project / ScopeHHCritical Baseline this SRS with formal sign-off per section; enforce MoSCoW priorities (Section 27); route every scope change through documented change control with impact analysis. Invoke change-control board; re-baseline schedule and budget; defer contested items to a later release. Project Manager > 3 open scope disputes at any review gate Open
RISK-002 Regulatory interpretation differences: tenants operating under different standards (ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 17025, ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 11) expect conflicting behaviours from the same shared feature set. ComplianceMHHigh Model compliance-specific behaviour as tenant-configurable options with documented defaults (Section 19); obtain written interpretation from each tenant's quality authority before configuration freeze. Engage external regulatory consultant; isolate the disputed behaviour behind a tenant feature flag. Quality Director (client) / Business Analyst Conflicting compliance requirement raised by two or more tenants Open
RISK-003 Tenant-isolation defect: a coding or configuration error exposes one tenant's records to another tenant, breaching confidentiality and contractual obligations. Product / SecurityLHMedium Enforce PostgreSQL Row-Level Security on all tenant-owned tables; derive tenant context only from trusted token claims; mandatory automated cross-tenant denial tests in every CI run (Section 23); independent penetration test before go-live. Activate security-incident procedure; disable affected endpoints; notify affected tenants per contract; forensic review of audit logs. Solution Architect / Security Officer Any failed isolation test or security-log cross-tenant denial anomaly Mitigating
RISK-004 Data-migration quality: legacy documents, NCRs, CAPAs and training records are incomplete, inconsistent or wrongly classified, undermining trust in the new system from day one. Project / DataHHCritical Execute migration discovery and data-profiling early (Section 22); define field-level mapping and cleansing rules with client data owners; run at least two full rehearsal migrations with reconciliation reports signed off by record owners. Migrate a reduced "active records only" set; retain legacy system read-only for the residual history; extend hyper-care period. Migration Lead Rehearsal reconciliation error rate above agreed threshold Open
RISK-005 User adoption resistance: staff continue to use paper forms, spreadsheets and email in parallel, so the system never becomes the single source of truth. OrganizationalMHHigh Involve process owners in workflow validation; deliver role-based training before go-live (TRN module used for the rollout itself); executive sponsorship communications; retire legacy templates at cut-over. Targeted floor-walking support; simplify high-friction screens in a fast-follow patch; management mandate on uncontrolled records. Client Programme Sponsor System usage below agreed adoption KPI 30 days after go-live Open
RISK-006 Approval-workflow delays: client-side reviewers and approvers of project deliverables (SRS, design, validation protocols) are slow to respond, stalling the critical path. ProjectMMMedium Agree review SLAs per deliverable in the project charter; nominate deputies for every approver; publish an approvals dashboard in steering reports. Escalate to sponsor; apply "approved by elapse" rule where contractually agreed; re-plan dependent tasks. Project Manager Any deliverable in review longer than its agreed SLA Open
RISK-007 Integration dependency: client HR system, ERP or identity provider is unavailable, undocumented, or its interfaces change during the project (Section 14). External / IntegrationMHHigh Confirm interface contracts and test-environment access before build starts; design integrations with retry, queuing and manual-fallback modes; version all interface contracts. Ship with CSV/manual import fallback; decouple integration go-live from core go-live. Integration Lead Test environment or interface specification not available at sprint entry Open
RISK-008 Performance under load: dashboards, searches and reports degrade once record volumes and concurrent users reach production scale, breaching Section 18 targets. Product / PerformanceMMMedium Define load profiles early; execute load and soak tests against production-like data volumes before UAT; index and query-plan review as a release exit criterion. Scale infrastructure vertically/horizontally; introduce read replicas or materialised reporting views; defer heavy reports to scheduled generation. Solution Architect Any load-test scenario missing its PER-NFR target Mitigating
RISK-009 File/attachment security: uploaded evidence files introduce malware or leak confidential content through uncontrolled download links. SecurityMHHigh Enforce file-type and size allow-lists; malware scanning on upload; store attachments outside the web root with permission-checked, expiring download tokens; audit every download of Confidential/Restricted records. Quarantine affected storage; revoke download tokens; incident response and tenant notification. Security Officer Any malware detection or unauthorized-download audit event Mitigating
RISK-010 E-signature legal acceptance: electronic signatures produced by NT.QMS are challenged by a regulator, external auditor or court in a given jurisdiction. Compliance / LegalMHHigh Implement signature manifestation, meaning, and record-linking per Section 19; obtain client legal review of the signature policy per operating jurisdiction before enabling; retain signature audit records immutably. Enable qualified/digital-certificate signing via an external provider for the affected jurisdiction; fall back to hybrid wet-ink procedure for the disputed record class. Quality Director (client) / Legal Counsel Regulator or auditor observation questioning signature validity Open
RISK-011 Localization/RTL quality: Arabic right-to-left layouts, mixed-direction text and localized notifications contain rendering or translation defects that damage credibility with Arabic-first users. Product / UsabilityMMMedium Build RTL support into the component library from the start (not as a retrofit); dedicated Arabic linguistic review of UI strings and notification templates; RTL scenarios included in every regression cycle. Prioritized localization defect backlog with a dedicated fix sprint before Arabic-tenant go-live. UX Lead RTL defect density above threshold in system test Mitigating
RISK-012 Reporting complexity creep: stakeholders continuously request new reports, pivots and export variants during build, inflating Section 15 scope. ScopeHMHigh Freeze the Release 1 report catalogue at SRS baseline; provide generic filtered-list export to cover ad-hoc needs; route new reports to Release 2+ backlog via change control. Offer BI-tool extract (read-only reporting views) as an interim answer for unplanned analytics. Business Analyst New report requests exceeding 2 per module after baseline Open
RISK-013 Infrastructure readiness: hosting environment, TLS certificates, backup storage or network access are not provisioned in time for system test, UAT or go-live. External / InfrastructureMMMedium Publish an environment readiness checklist with dates in the project plan; provision environments one phase ahead of need; automate environment build (infrastructure as code). Use vendor-hosted temporary environment for testing while client environment is completed. Infrastructure Lead Environment checklist item late by more than 5 working days Open
RISK-014 Disaster recovery gaps: backup and restore procedures exist on paper but an actual restore fails or misses the agreed RPO/RTO (Section 18). OperationalLHMedium Automated, monitored backups with alerting; documented restore runbook; full restore rehearsal as a go-live entry criterion and at least annually thereafter. Restore from secondary backup location; invoke degraded-mode operation (read-only) during recovery. Operations Manager Failed or untested restore in any quarter Mitigating
RISK-015 Source data quality: master data feeding the system (employee lists, departments, equipment registers, supplier lists) is duplicated, stale or unowned, degrading assignments, notifications and reports. DataHMHigh Appoint client data owners per master-data domain; cleanse and deduplicate before load; establish ongoing HR-sync validation reports (Section 14). Manual master-data correction workflow with audit; quarantine unmatched records for owner review. Data Owner (client) Master-data exception queue above agreed threshold Open
RISK-016 Permission model over-complexity: excessive custom roles and record-level exceptions make the RBAC/ABAC model (Section 13) unmaintainable and unauditable. Product / GovernanceMMMedium Ship a small canonical role set mapped to personas; require governance approval for custom roles; provide a permission-matrix report so administrators can review effective access. Role rationalisation exercise; merge redundant roles; time-boxed access recertification campaign. Tenant Administrator / Security Officer Custom roles per tenant exceeding agreed ceiling Mitigating
RISK-017 Excessive per-tenant customization: tenants demand bespoke workflows, fields and reports beyond the configurable envelope, fragmenting the product into unmaintainable variants. Product / ScopeHMHigh Define the configuration envelope explicitly (workflow templates, custom fields, numbering, terminology) in TEN; refuse code-level per-tenant forks; product board reviews every extension request against the roadmap. Package genuinely common requests as product features in the next release; decline or commercially separate one-off demands. Product Owner Customization request outside the configuration envelope Open
RISK-018 Key-person dependency: critical domain knowledge (quality processes, legacy data structures) is concentrated in one or two client individuals who may become unavailable. OrganizationalMMMedium Document decisions and process knowledge in the project workspace as they are gathered; require at least two client SMEs per module workshop. Re-run discovery workshops with substitutes; extend elaboration timeline for affected modules. Project Manager Single-SME module with SME absence > 2 weeks Open
Note: Risk status values: Open (mitigation not yet fully effective), Mitigating (mitigation in place and monitored), Closed (risk retired). All register changes are recorded in project change history.

27 Implementation Priorities & Phasing

This section defines the prioritization scheme applied throughout this SRS and proposes a three-release delivery plan. Priorities are assigned per requirement using MoSCoW; the phasing groups modules and cross-cutting capabilities into releases that each deliver a coherent, independently valuable increment.

27.1 MoSCoW Priority Definitions

PriorityBadgeDefinitionAcceptance implication
MustMust Mandatory for the release in which it is scheduled; the release cannot be accepted without it. Blocking: any failed Must requirement blocks release acceptance.
ShouldShould Important but not release-blocking; a documented workaround must exist if deferred. Deferral requires change-control approval and a recorded workaround.
CouldCould Desirable enhancement delivered if capacity allows within the release. May be dropped from the release without change control; remains in backlog.
FutureFuture Recognised need assigned to a later release or the product roadmap. Not tested in the current release; tracked in the roadmap backlog.
Out of ScopeOut of Scope Explicitly excluded from the current programme; requires a new agreement to add. Not delivered; documented in Section 7 exclusions.

27.3 Phased Delivery Plan

Pending business confirmation: the phasing below is Proposed — pending formal approval by the client steering committee. Release contents may be re-balanced at scope freeze (Section 26.6) without changing the requirements themselves.

27.3.1 Release 1 — Core Platform & Quality Loop

Objectives. Establish the multi-tenant platform foundation and digitize the core quality loop: controlled documents, nonconformances and CAPAs, with immutable audit trails, notifications and management visibility. Achieve BUS-OBJ-001–005, 006, 008, 009 and 015 for the pilot organization.

  • Included capabilities: PLT, TEN, IAM (local accounts + RBAC + MFA), DOC, NCR, CAPA, basic dashboards (DSH) and the Release 1 report catalogue, full audit trail, email and in-app notifications, English and Arabic (RTL) UI, attachment handling with malware scanning, data migration for documents and open NCR/CAPA records.
  • Exclusions: CMP, AUD, TRN, EQP, RSK (beyond basic risk fields), MRV, external integrations other than SMTP, French UI, SCIM, SMS/WhatsApp, BI export.
  • Entry criteria: SRS sections for R1 modules baselined and signed; DEC-DEV-001..005 recorded; environments provisioned; migration discovery complete.
  • Exit criteria: all R1 Must requirements passed in UAT; zero open Critical/Major defects; tenant-isolation and security test suites passed; rehearsal migration reconciled and signed (DEC-DEP-004); DR restore rehearsal passed; training of pilot users completed.
  • Key dependencies: hosting decision (Q-TEC-001), SMTP relay (Q-TEC-005), client SME availability (ASM-007), source-data cleansing (RISK-015).

27.3.2 Release 2 — Extended QMS & Integrations

Objectives. Complete the operational QMS record set (complaints, audits, training, equipment), connect NT.QMS to the enterprise identity and HR landscape, and extend reporting and language coverage. Achieve BUS-OBJ-007, 010, 011, 012 and 014.

  • Included capabilities: CMP, AUD, TRN, EQP; integrations — HR employee sync, SSO (OIDC/SAML), e-signature step-up via IdP; advanced reporting (scheduled reports, cross-module dashboards); French UI; complaint-to-NCR/CAPA and audit-finding-to-CAPA linking.
  • Exclusions: full RSK register, MRV, supplier audits/scorecards, SCIM, SMS/WhatsApp channels, BI export.
  • Entry criteria: Release 1 in stable production (agreed defect and availability thresholds met for 30 days); IdP and HR interface contracts confirmed (Q-TEC-004); R2 module sections re-validated with SMEs.
  • Exit criteria: all R2 Must/Should requirements passed in UAT or formally deferred with workaround; integration failover (manual fallback) demonstrated; regression suite for R1 modules green; French linguistic review signed.
  • Key dependencies: HR/ERP interface availability (RISK-007), IdP federation (UNV-005), equipment master-data cleansing.

27.3.3 Release 3 — Risk, Review & Analytics

Objectives. Close the strategic layer of the QMS: enterprise risk management, management review, deeper supplier quality, and analytics openness, plus provisioning and channel automation. Achieve BUS-OBJ-013 and complete BUS-OBJ-016.

  • Included capabilities: RSK full module (risk register, 5×5 matrix, FMEA-style assessments, risk-based linkage to NCR/CAPA/AUD); MRV (inputs aggregation, actions, minutes); supplier quality depth (supplier audits, SCAR lifecycle, scorecards) subject to Q-BUS-002; advanced analytics and BI export (read-only reporting views/extract); SCIM provisioning; optional SMS/WhatsApp notification channels subject to Q-TEC-002.
  • Exclusions: native mobile application, user-content machine translation, any capability marked Out of Scope in Section 7.
  • Entry criteria: Release 2 stable in production for 30 days; KPI targets approved (DEC-DEP-002); messaging provider contracted if optional channels are confirmed.
  • Exit criteria: R3 acceptance per MoSCoW rules; analytics extract validated against report catalogue figures; MRV executed end-to-end for at least one real review cycle in UAT.
  • Key dependencies: populated operational data from R1/R2 modules; provider selection decisions (Q-TEC-002, Q-TEC-004).

28 Glossary & Acronyms

Terms and acronyms used throughout this SRS, in alphabetical order. Where a term has a specific meaning inside NT.QMS that differs from general usage, the NT.QMS meaning governs.

TermDefinition
ABACAttribute-Based Access Control — authorization decisions based on attributes of the user, record and context (e.g. department, site, confidentiality level), complementing RBAC.
APIApplication Programming Interface — the documented HTTP interface through which the SPA client and external systems interact with NT.QMS services.
Audit trailChronological, tamper-evident record of who did what, when, to which record, including before/after values and reason where required; immutable once written.
Bounded contextDDD term for a boundary within which a domain model and its terms are consistent; NT.QMS modules (DOC, NCR, CAPA, …) are designed as bounded contexts.
CAPACorrective Action / Preventive Action — the structured process of eliminating causes of detected (corrective) or potential (preventive) nonconformities and verifying effectiveness.
CFRCode of Federal Regulations — codified US federal rules; in this SRS specifically Title 21 CFR Part 11 on electronic records and electronic signatures.
Controlled documentA document whose creation, review, approval, distribution, revision and withdrawal are governed by the DOC module so that only the current approved version is available at points of use.
CQRSCommand Query Responsibility Segregation — architectural pattern separating state-changing commands from read queries, used for workflow actions vs dashboards/reports.
DDDDomain-Driven Design — design approach modelling software around the business domain, its language and boundaries.
Digital signatureA cryptographic signature bound to a certificate (PKI), providing mathematical integrity and signer authentication; a possible implementation of an electronic signature (see Section 19).
Effective dateThe date from which an approved controlled document version is the binding version at points of use; may be later than the approval date.
Effectiveness verificationThe CAPA step confirming, with objective evidence after a defined period, that implemented actions actually prevented recurrence before closure.
Electronic signatureA legally significant computer-based act (e.g. authenticated approve action with meaning and manifestation) equivalent to a handwritten signature on the record.
FMEAFailure Mode and Effects Analysis — structured risk technique scoring failure modes by severity, occurrence and detection; supported by the RSK module.
GxPCollective abbreviation for "good practice" regulations (GMP, GLP, GCP, …) in regulated life-science industries.
IdempotencyProperty of an operation that produces the same result when executed more than once; NT.QMS APIs use idempotency keys so retries do not duplicate records or notifications.
KPIKey Performance Indicator — a measured value with a target used to track quality performance (e.g. CAPA on-time closure rate).
MFAMulti-Factor Authentication — authentication requiring at least two independent factors (knowledge, possession, inherence).
MoSCoWPrioritization scheme: Must, Should, Could, Won't/Future — defined for this SRS in Section 27.1.
NCRNonconformance Report — the record documenting a detected nonconformity, its containment, disposition and linkage to CAPA.
OIDCOpenID Connect — identity federation protocol layered on OAuth 2.0, used for SSO and signing step-up authentication.
OOTOut of Tolerance — a calibration result outside acceptance limits, triggering impact assessment of measurements made since the last passing calibration (EQP module).
Optimistic concurrencyConflict-control technique where updates carry a record version; a stale version is rejected with a conflict message instead of silently overwriting.
Outbox patternReliability pattern where domain events are stored transactionally with the business change and dispatched afterwards, guaranteeing notifications/integrations are not lost.
OWASPOpen Worldwide Application Security Project — source of the security practices (e.g. OWASP ASVS, Top 10) referenced by SEC-NFR requirements.
PDF/AISO-standardized archival profile of PDF used for long-term readable renditions of controlled documents and signed records.
QMSQuality Management System — the set of processes, records and responsibilities by which an organization directs and controls quality (ISO 9001 context); also the product domain of NT.QMS.
RACIResponsibility matrix notation: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed.
RBACRole-Based Access Control — permissions granted to roles, roles assigned to users (Section 13).
Root causeThe fundamental underlying reason for a nonconformity which, if eliminated, prevents recurrence; documented via structured analysis (e.g. 5 Whys, fishbone) in CAPA.
Row-Level SecurityPostgreSQL feature enforcing per-row access policies in the database itself; NT.QMS uses it as the hard tenant-isolation layer.
RPORecovery Point Objective — maximum tolerable data loss, measured as time between the incident and the last recoverable state.
RTMRequirements Traceability Matrix — the mapping of business objectives to requirements to test cases (Section 24).
RTORecovery Time Objective — maximum tolerable time to restore service after an incident.
SAMLSecurity Assertion Markup Language — XML-based federation protocol supported as an SSO alternative to OIDC.
SCARSupplier Corrective Action Request — a corrective-action demand issued to an external supplier and tracked to closure.
SLAService Level Agreement — a committed, measurable service target (e.g. response time, availability, review turnaround).
SOPStandard Operating Procedure — a controlled document prescribing how an activity is performed.
SSOSingle Sign-On — authentication delegated to a central identity provider so users sign in once for multiple applications.
Superseded documentA previously effective document version replaced by a newer effective version; retained read-only, watermarked, and excluded from points of use.
TenantA contractually and logically separate customer organization within the shared NT.QMS platform, owning its users, configuration and records.
Tenant isolationThe guarantee that no user, query, report, export or integration can read or affect another tenant's data; enforced by claims-based context plus Row-Level Security and verified by dedicated tests.
UATUser Acceptance Testing — client-executed testing confirming the system meets the agreed requirements before go-live (Section 23).
WCAGWeb Content Accessibility Guidelines — accessibility standard referenced by USE-NFR requirements.

Appendix B — Workflow-Status Dictionary

Canonical record statuses used across modules. A module uses only the statuses relevant to its lifecycle (see each module's "Record Lifecycle" subsection).

StatusDefinitionTypical entry action
DraftRecord created and editable by its owner; not yet visible in operational lists. Create record; or Return for Correction reverts editable content to owner.
SubmittedOwner has formally handed the record to the workflow; owner editing is locked. Submit action with completeness validation.
Under ReviewAssigned reviewer(s) are evaluating content; comments may be recorded. Reviewer accepts the review task or routing engine assigns it.
Returned for CorrectionReviewer/approver sent the record back with mandatory comments; owner may edit and resubmit.Return action with reason (mandatory).
ApprovedAll required approvals (and signatures where configured) are complete; record awaits activation/effectivity where applicable. Final approver approves/signs.
RejectedApproval was refused terminally; record cannot proceed without a new submission cycle or is closed as rejected.Reject action with reason (mandatory).
Active / EffectiveRecord is the operative version (documents) or in execution (plans, actions).Effective date reached, or explicit Activate action.
In ProgressWork items (CAPA actions, audit fieldwork, maintenance orders) are being executed.Assignee starts the first action.
Pending VerificationExecution finished; awaiting effectiveness or quality verification before closure (CAPA, NCR disposition). Last action completed; verifier task created.
SuspendedRecord temporarily withdrawn from operation pending investigation or decision; not usable at points of use.Suspend action by authorized role with reason.
SupersededA newer approved version became effective; this version is retained read-only and watermarked.Automatic on activation of the successor version.
CancelledRecord abandoned before completion; retained for traceability, excluded from KPIs unless configured otherwise.Cancel action by authorized role with reason.
ClosedLifecycle complete, including verification where required; record is read-only except for authorized reopen.Close action after closure criteria validated.
ArchivedRetention-managed storage state; read-only, excluded from operational searches by default (Section 21). Archiving job per retention schedule.

Appendix C — Record-Classification Dictionary
ClassificationDefinitionHandling rules
PublicContent approved for release outside the organization (e.g. published quality policy). Viewable by all authenticated tenant users; export/print unrestricted; still audited on change.
InternalDefault level for operational quality records. Visible per role/department permissions; export allowed to permitted roles; included in standard reports.
ConfidentialRecords whose disclosure could harm individuals or the business (e.g. complaint files with patient/customer data, audit findings before publication). Access restricted to named roles/participants; downloads audited individually; excluded from broad exports; watermarked prints.
RestrictedHighest sensitivity (e.g. legal-hold records, security investigations). Named-user access list only; view and download individually audited; no bulk export; reports show existence only to authorized users; legal-hold overrides retention disposal.

Appendix D — Priority Definitions

Requirement priorities use the MoSCoW scheme defined normatively in Section 27.1. In addition, operational work items inside the product (NCRs, CAPAs, complaints) use a record priority:

Record priorityMeaningDefault due-date behaviour
HighSignificant quality, safety or compliance exposure; management attention required. Shortest configured target dates; escalation on first missed reminder.
MediumStandard operational handling.Standard configured target dates.
LowMinor issue; batched handling acceptable. Extended target dates; reminders without escalation until final threshold.

Appendix E — Severity Definitions
SeverityDefinitionExamplesInitial response / containment target
CriticalDirect risk to patient/consumer safety, legal violation, or stop-ship / stop-service condition. Released product out of specification with safety impact; falsified record discovered; sterility failure. Containment initiated within 4 business hours; management notified same day.
MajorSignificant nonconformity likely to cause customer impact, regulatory observation or repeated failure. Missed calibration on measurement equipment in use; SOP not followed with product impact; repeated audit finding. Containment within 1 business day; investigation started within 3 business days.
MinorIsolated deviation with no product/service impact and low recurrence risk. Typographical error in a controlled form; single overdue read-and-understand acknowledgement. Correction planned within 10 business days.
Pending business confirmation: the response and containment targets above are proposed defaults; each tenant confirms its own SLA values during onboarding configuration (proposed target — pending business confirmation).

Appendix H — Role-Permission Matrix Pointer & Delegation Summary

The full role-permission matrix (personas P-01..P-32 × module actions, with SoD constraints) is defined normatively in Section 13 and per module in each "Permission Requirements" subsection. Delegation rules summary:

  • Delegation is time-bounded (start/end date mandatory) and limited to roles the delegator holds.
  • Approval authority may be delegated only to users already eligible for the approval role; Segregation-of-Duties checks apply to the delegate as if acting personally.
  • The audit trail records both identities on every delegated action ("performed by X on behalf of Y").
  • E-signatures are never delegable: a delegate signs with their own identity and credentials.
  • Active delegations are visible to Tenant Administrators and expire automatically; extension requires a new delegation record.

Appendix O — Sample Traceability Chain

Illustrative end-to-end traceability path demonstrating how the RTM (Section 24) links strategy to evidence:

  1. Business objective — BUS-OBJ-004 "Enforce approvals and segregation of duties".
  2. Functional requirement — DOC-FR series requirement mandating sequential approval routes with SoD validation (Section 11.5).
  3. Business rule — DOC-BR rule: an author may not approve their own document.
  4. Acceptance criterion — AC-DOC Given/When/Then verifying that an out-of-sequence or self-approval attempt is rejected and audited.
  5. Test case — system/UAT test executing the criterion, referenced from the RTM with its result (Section 23).
  6. Runtime evidence — audit events AEV-009 and AEV-010 on production records, exportable for inspection.

Any requirement in this SRS can be traversed in both directions along this chain: from objective down to evidence, and from a production audit event back to the objective that justified the behaviour.
